> [!IMPORTANT]
> Off-topic comments and AI slop/spam in this thread will be deleted. Keep the discussion focused.

---

Draft. Adds support for `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` (HF `model_type: qwen4_exp`, `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`): converter, text graph, sparse attention, vision, and three quantizer fixes the model needs. Opening as a draft because the weights are not public yet, so the accuracy numbers below cannot be reproduced from outside at the moment.

## Architecture

| subsystem | how it is handled |
|---|---|
| Gated delta net (3 of every 4 layers) | subclasses the existing delta-net base; the only delta from Qwen3.5 is a sigmoid output gate instead of silu |
| MoE, 512 experts, top-10, gated shared expert | `build_moe_ffn`, unchanged |
| Interleaved mrope, partial rotary 64/256 | `ggml_rope_multi` with `LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_IMROPE`, unchanged |
| Hyper-connections (`hc_count = 4`, low rank) | self-contained in `qwen4exp.cpp`; `deepseek4.cpp` is untouched |
| Per-layer embeddings, 97.7 GiB n-gram hash table | host-side row indices in a `set_input`, then `ggml_get_rows` |
| QSA sparse attention (budget 2048, ratio 4) | new graph plus an optional third cache in `llama_memory_hybrid` |
| Vision | stock Qwen3-VL ViT through the existing clip path |

`git diff master --stat -- ggml/` is empty: no new ggml op, and no change to any existing one.

## Correctness, against the reference implementation

| check | result |
|---|---|
| wikitext-2 perplexity, 145 chunks at ctx 2048 | 4.0068 +/- 0.02271 vs 4.0126 for the reference |
| top-1 agreement, 512 tokens of prose | 98.0 percent |
| QSA vs dense below the budget | bit identical, max logit delta 0.0 over all 2051 rows |
| QSA vs dense above the budget, 8192 tokens | diverges on 3 percent of positions |
| indexer selection vs the reference | 0.975 mean jaccard against a 0.991 precision floor |
| `test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` | OK on CPU (0.00e+00) and CUDA (8.00e-08), roundtrip OK |

The bit-identical result below the budget is the useful one: QSA is dense by construction under `indexer_top_k + compress_ratio - 1` cached tokens, so it is a free oracle on the whole selection and masking path.

## Effect on other architectures

Six shared files contain deletions rather than pure additions:

- `llama-quant.cpp`: three fixes, each byte-exact against the parent commit. `tensor_type_fallback` had no case for 32-block types, so a tensor whose ncols is not divisible by 32 aborted instead of falling back; `--tensor-type` could not name `per_layer_token_embd` because `--token-embedding-type` returned first; and the `work` buffer was sized `nelements * 4` as an upper bound on a value already known exactly, which is 150 GB per process on a model with a 51.2 G element tensor. Six A/B cases, six matching md5s.
- `llama-graph.cpp`: `build_attn_mask_top_k` lifted verbatim out of the DSA `build_attn` overload so both share it. The node construction sequence is identical after splicing the helper back into its call site, and `deepseek32` and `glm-dsa` both pass at 0.00e+00 on CPU.
- `llama-memory-hybrid.cpp`: the new `filter_idx` defaults to `nullptr` and every use is guarded.
- `llama-model-loader.cpp`: adds a `GGUF_TYPE_UINT64` case to a type check that previously threw.
- `llama-hparams.cpp`, `llama-model.cpp`: new fields and new switch cases.

A shared hyper-connection base with `deepseek4` was considered and rejected: the two formulations agree on the residual layout and nothing else (full-rank projection with Sinkhorn normalisation there, low-rank silu gate and a mean collapse here), so factoring it out would touch DSV4's hot path to share about ten lines.

## Note for reviewers

This branch was developed against a snapshot and rebased onto current master. Two rebase conflicts were resolved by hand, both additive: `test-llama-archs.cpp` where master had added a `LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4` condition to a line this port also edits, and `llama-model-saver.cpp` where master reworked the DSV4 key block. Worth a close look, since the local build was against the pre-rebase tree.

## AI Usage
Used Claude and Local Models for testing, iteration and code design - manual verification of model / PR usage

### Name and Version

llama-b10639-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64
build: 5e6a37cb1 (10639)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64


### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0

or

llama-bench.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

On the ROCm backend, using any q5_0 KV cache type (either K or V) causes the compute graph to fragment from 2 splits into 34 splits. This pushes ~550-580 MiB of compute to the CPU host buffer and causes a ~68% regression in prompt processing throughput.

The issue is **specific to the ROCm backend**. The same build on Vulkan handles q5_0 KV cache correctly (2 splits, no regression). A fork of llama.cpp (build 11429) also handles it correctly on ROCm.

## Environment

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), 24 GB VRAM
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7900X
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL (16.34 GiB, 27.32 B params)
- Flash attention: enabled (`-fa 1`)

## Benchmark results

| KV Cache | graph splits | GPU compute buf | CPU compute buf | pp512 | tg128 |
|----------|:-----------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|:-----:|:-----:|
| q8_0 / q8_0 (ROCm) | 2 | 786.53 MiB | 161.53 MiB | 957.11 t/s | 37.53 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **551.28 MiB** | **300.10 t/s** | **27.96 t/s** |
| q5_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **580.53 MiB** | **302.49 t/s** | **28.39 t/s** |
| q8_0 / q8_0 (Vulkan, same build) | 2 | 270.53 MiB | 158.53 MiB | 771.39 t/s | 37.17 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (Vulkan, same build) | **2** | **295.03 MiB** | **183.03 MiB** | **762.60 t/s** | **37.01 t/s** |

The trigger is q5_0 in the KV cache. It does not matter whether it's used for K, V, or both. The broken GPU compute buffer size is identical (122.28 MiB) in both q8_0/q5_0 and q5_0/q5_0 cases, confirming it's the same code path.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build llama.cpp with ROCm support (or use a prebuilt ROCm binary)
2. Run `llama-bench -m <model.gguf> -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` (or `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0`)
3. Observe ~68% pp512 regression vs. q8_0/q8_0
4. Compare with the same build on Vulkan — no regression

## Expected behavior

q5_0 KV cache should perform similarly to q8_0 KV cache (within a small margin) when using flash attention, as it does on Vulkan and on the beellama fork (build 11429).

## Key log evidence

The main model's `sched_reserve` output:

**Working (q8_0/q8_0, ROCm):**

sched_reserve: ROCm0 compute buffer size = 786.53 MiB
sched_reserve: ROCm_Host compute buffer size = 161.53 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 2

**Broken (q5_0/q5_0, ROCm):**

sched_reserve: ROCm0 compute buffer size = 122.28 MiB
sched_reserve: ROCm_Host compute buffer size = 580.53 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 34

**Working (q8_0/q5_0, Vulkan, same build 10639):**

sched_reserve: Vulkan1 compute buffer size = 295.03 MiB
sched_reserve: Vulkan_Host compute buffer size = 183.03 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 2


The 4135-node graph is the main model forward pass. The 34 splits mean 32 extra GPU↔CPU synchronization points per step.


### First Bad Commit

Not yet identified. The issue is present in build 10639.

## Overview

Long-context generation quickly exhausts VRAM when retaining the entire KV cache. This PR implements StreamingLLM-style KV cache eviction via `--kv-evict-sink` and `--kv-evict-window`.

By capping the physical cache at `sink + recent + n_ubatch` cells while allowing the logical context to grow indefinitely, both VRAM footprint and per-token decode latency remain constant over arbitrary sequence lengths.

## Implementation Details

- **Masking**: `set_input_kq_mask_impl` masks cells in the range `[n_kv_sink, p1 - n_kv_recent)`. Mask row reuse is disabled while eviction is active.

- **Slot Recycling**: `find_slot` reclaims the oldest cell outside the sink and active recent window; `apply_ubatch` bypasses contiguity purges during eviction.

- **Memory Footprint**: Fixed at `n_seq_max * (sink + recent) + ubatch` for unified multi-sequence caches (`sink + recent + ubatch` otherwise). Recurrent states (e.g., DeltaNet) remain untouched.

- **Compatibility**: Disables context shifting (`get_can_shift = false`). Safe for MTP speculative decoding since rollback spans stay within the recent window.

- **Benchmarks**: Wikitext-2 perplexity remains stable (~6.31 baseline vs. ~6.48 with a 1024-token window), while decode throughput stays flat across long sequences.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

- AI Usage disclosure: YES - the code implementation was drafted with AI and reviewed/tested by me before submission.

# [draft-mtp] Draft acceptance collapses to 0.0 under `-np N` with multi-ubatch batches — async `t_h_nextn` device→host copy race

## Summary

Self-speculative decoding (`--spec-type draft-mtp`) silently breaks under parallel slots (`-np 4`): as soon as concurrent requests carry long prompts (decode batches spanning multiple ubatches), draft acceptance drops from a healthy **0.48–0.85** to **exactly 0.00000** on all slots, generation falls back below no-MTP speed, and consumers of the endpoint see empty `message.content` completions (`finish_reason=stop` after a handful of `reasoning_content` tokens).

The trigger is a race between the **async device→host copy of `t_h_nextn`** (the MTP draft's input hidden states) and **any later graph that reuses the `t_h_nextn` extra buffer** — the next ubatch within the same `decode()`, or the next `decode()` call under `-np N` continuous batching. When the copy loses, the MTP draft conditions on NaN `h` rows, its logits go NaN, and every draft is rejected.

Verified at [`f5b9bd39b`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/f5b9bd39b) (build 10176), HIP backend. The same binary is correct at `-np 1` and for single-ubatch batches.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| llama.cpp | [`f5b9bd39b`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/f5b9bd39b) (b10176), HIP build, `AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151` |
| ROCm | 7.2.2 (pinned; gfx1151 native) |
| GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo, gfx1151), 256 GB unified |
| Model | [unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF) `UD-Q4_K_XL` + `mmproj-F16` (`qwen35` hybrid: Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention, embedded nextn/MTP layer) |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.17 |

Server flags:

```bash
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf --jinja \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9999 -ngl all -fit off -np 4 \
  -c 1048576 -n 131072 -b 1024 -ub 256 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 \
  --load-mode dio --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 -rea on \
  --reasoning-format deepseek --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0 --metrics
```

## Reproduction

Self-contained script (stdlib only, no client framework needed) — it fires 4 concurrent chat completions, each with a ~19k-token system prompt, and prints per-request `OK`/`EMPTY` plus finish reasons.

<details>
<summary>repro_mtp_np4.py (click to expand)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce the draft-mtp acceptance collapse under -np N concurrent load."""
import json, sys, threading, time, urllib.request

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:9999/v1/chat/completions"
N_CONC = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 4
TARGET_TOKENS = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 19000

unit = ("### Skill {i}: skill_{i} handles topic {i}. Steps: analyze, plan, "
        "execute, report. Constraints: verify outputs, cite sources.\n")
SYS = "You are an agent. Available skills:\n" + "".join(
    unit.format(i=i) for i in range(TARGET_TOKENS // 9))

def one(idx, results):
    body = {"model": "local_llm", "max_tokens": 1200, "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": SYS},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"[{idx}] Say hello and list what you can help with, one line."}]}
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1200))
        c = r["choices"][0]
        content = (c["message"].get("content") or "").strip()
        results.append((idx, "OK" if content else "EMPTY", c["finish_reason"],
                        r["usage"]["completion_tokens"], time.time() - t0))
    except Exception as e:
        results.append((idx, "ERROR", type(e).__name__, 0, time.time() - t0))

def round_test(round_n):
    results = []
    ts = [threading.Thread(target=one, args=(i, results)) for i in range(N_CONC)]
    for t in ts: t.start()
    for t in ts: t.join()
    empty = sum(1 for r in results if r[1] != "OK")
    for r in results:
        print(f"  round {round_n} req{r[0]}: {r[1]:5s} finish={r[2]:6s} ct={r[3]:5d} {r[4]:7.1f}s")
    print(f"  round {round_n}: empty {empty}/{N_CONC}")
    return empty

if __name__ == "__main__":
    total = sum(round_test(n + 1) for n in range(2))
    print(f"TOTAL empty: {total}/{2 * N_CONC}")
```

</details>

### Expected output on an affected build

Server log (`--metrics`, per slot, at task end):

```
slot print_timing: id 0 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 1 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 2 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 3 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
```

The same server, **sequential** single request on a cold slot:

```
slot print_timing: id 3 | draft acceptance = 0.57865 (  206 accepted /   356 generated), mean len = 3.31
```

Client side, affected requests return `finish_reason=stop` with empty content after a few reasoning tokens, or run away in reasoning until the token cap — both surface as "empty completion" to an agent/chat client.

### What does *not* trigger it

- `-np 4` with short prompts (single-ubatch batches): 0/12 failures over 3 rounds
- Long prompts processed **sequentially** (one slot active): healthy acceptance
- Warm prefix cache (prefill mostly cached): healthy
- `-np 1` with MTP: always healthy

→ the failure requires **concurrent** requests producing decode calls whose batches split across ubatches (long prompts), under multi-slot continuous batching.

## Root-cause analysis

Instrumentation adds two probes (patch inlined at the end of this section):

items.body:
## Overview

DFlash2 adds two more modules compared to DFlash, grouped dynamic depthwise convolution and candidate selector. 

The formula is for reference. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`. `base` is the static kernel, `δ` is the dynamic part predicted from the input.`x` is divided into groups `g(c)` and `δ` is shared across a group. Another one is `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`. `A`/`B` are the codebooks for the predecessor and the candidate. This position's hidden is projected by `project(h)`to the same rank to multiply `A`. And `unary[c]` is the draft's own score for `c`.  

DFlash2 is enabled when the checkpoint is DFlash2; no need to use extra flag.

We evaled `Qwen3.8-27B` at `Q4_K_M`on Apple M5 Pro 64 GB. And the test data is first 8 problems of GSM8K.
Concurrency is set to 1 and temperature is 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20. We use default `xhigh` reasoning and set
2,048 maximum new tokens.

| Method | Draft quant | Block | Decode TPS | Decode speedup | Acceptance | Normal stops |
|--------|------|--:|------:|------:|-----:|---|
| Autoregressive | — | — | 10.42 | 1.00× | — | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | BF16 | 8 | 19.31 | 1.85× | 4.92 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q8_0 | 8 | 18.43 | 1.77× | 5.08 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q4_K_M | 8 | 18.89 | 1.81× | 5.03 | 8/8 |


## Requirements

<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. Using AI to inspect and analyze code in the llama.cpp project, and using AI to update the code.

## Disclosure

I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, benchmarking and drafting of this PR, including this description and the commit messages. I have reviewed and validated everything myself; all measurements below were run on my own hardware and are reproducible. Flagging this explicitly per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Summary

`ggml_vk_should_use_mmvq()` returns early with *"MMVQ is generally good for batches"* for any `n > 1`. A speculative-decode step evaluates `n = 1 + n_draft` tokens, so it takes that path and enables MMVQ — bypassing the per-vendor small-`k` heuristics below it.

Those heuristics predate speculative decoding and were only ever reachable at `n == 1`. This PR raises the cutoff so decode-like `n` reaches them too. **No vendor threshold is changed** — they simply now apply at the small `n` a speculative step actually uses.

Enabling MMVQ there costs twice:

1. The Q8_1 quantization of the activations does not amortize at such small `n`.
2. It **perturbs the logits**, so the draft and the target disagree on tokens they should agree on — lowering **draft acceptance**.

The second effect is the less obvious one: MMVQ was not merely slower in the speculative path, it was degrading speculation quality.

## Commits

- `vulkan: don't use MMVQ for k-quants at small k on AMD` — AMD-specific tuning: for k-quants the Q8_1 quantization does not pay for itself at small `k`; DMMV is faster.
- `vulkan: treat a speculative-decode step as decode, not as a batch` — vendor-agnostic; raises the `n > 1` cutoff to `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N`.

## Testing

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" (gfx1151, 40 CU, RADV/Mesa), 128 GB unified memory.
Model: 35B-A3B MoE, Q6_K attention + Q4_K FFN. MTP self-speculation (`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`), ~33k context, 2 runs each, against master `7f575c39d`.

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TG, speculative | 75.2 t/s | **84.9 t/s** (+12.9%) |
| draft acceptance | 72–75% | **83–85%** |
| TG, non-speculative | 72.9 t/s | 73.9 t/s |
| PP (prefill), pp4096 | 679.4 t/s | 677.5 t/s (unchanged) |

Prefill is unaffected because `n` there is far larger — with a 2048 ubatch the per-expert token counts are ~64+, well above the cutoff, so batched MMVQ is retained.

An op-level trace of the MMVQ decisions during a speculative step on master shows the mechanism directly:

```
984x  n=3 k=2048 m=512  q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert up/gate)
492x  n=3 k=512  m=2048 q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert down)
220x  n=1 ...          q4_K -> dmmv      (plain decode, correctly bypassed)
```

## Caveats

- **I could only test gfx1151.** The second commit now applies to all vendors per review feedback, but I have no NVIDIA or Intel hardware to validate against. Numbers from someone with a dGPU would be very welcome — particularly whether MMVQ at `n = 2..8` is a win on those backends, since if so the cutoff may need to stay vendor-conditional.
- The first commit changes AMD behaviour at `n == 1` and therefore also affects **discrete** RDNA cards, which I likewise could not test. It is kept as a separate commit so it can be dropped independently.
- `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N = 8` is a bound chosen to cover common draft widths. Happy to derive it from the actual draft width instead if you'd prefer something less arbitrary.

items.body:
## Overview

Add benchmark-only synthetic speculative acceptance to llama-server and llama-cli, similar to [vLLM's benchmarking options](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/api/vllm/config/speculative/#vllm.config.speculative.SpeculativeConfig.synthetic_acceptance_length).

The motivation is that most performance benchmarks (like [aiperf](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiperf.git), [llama-benchy](https://github.com/eugr/llama-benchy)) use synthetic inputs so that prompt length, output length, batch size, and concurrency are easy to control. That works well for measuring non-speculative throughput, but it is not a good workload for speculative decoding. On random tokens, acceptance can be very low or noisy.

A synthetic acceptance mode would let us keep the reproducibility of a synthetic dataset while controlling the acceptance ratios independently. We can measure acceptance ratios in real workloads and then use those with synthetic dataset. This would also make it easier to measure and compare different spec dec techniques independent of the draft quality.

* Expose mutually exclusive `--spec-synthetic-acceptance-length` and `--spec-synthetic-acceptance-rates` options.
* Convert a requested mean length using a constant conditional probability satisfying `p + ... + p^K = L - 1`.
* Resolve `K` from initialized implementations, including DFlash, DSpark, and MTP model-specific limits.
* Replace draft/target token matching with seeded synthetic decisions while still running target sampling.
* Prevent draft EOG tokens from bypassing `ignore_eos`.
* Avoid advancing grammar and reasoning-budget state with synthetic draft tokens.
* Preserve speculative rollback, replay, and acceptance statistics.

## Overview

Adds support for NVIDIA's Nemotron-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B (`NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM`), a hybrid mamba2/attention/MoE model with a per-layer heterogeneous MoE configuration.

Puzzle reuses the existing `nemotron_h_moe` machinery (latent MoE, relu2, routed scaling, hybrid cache) but is *heterogeneous per layer*: 88 blocks = 40 mamba2 + 8 attention (GQA 32/2, NoPE) + 40 MoE where `moe_intermediate_size` (1280–2688) and `num_experts_per_tok` (4–18) vary per block.

**Scope note:** this PR was slimmed down on request — the MTP/NEXTN draft-head support it originally carried has been removed and will come back as a separate follow-up PR once this lands, so the two can be reviewed independently. The removal covers the converter as well, not just the model code: it was emitting the `nextn` tensors, which would have produced GGUFs this loader rejects. `mtp.*` is now skipped for Puzzle. Note this is no longer the same as "what the other NemotronH variants do": #26725 landed MTP export on `NemotronHModel` after this branch was written, so the base class now keeps the head. Puzzle stays opted out explicitly (`supports_mtp_export = False`), since its head is laid out by `mtp_block_configs` rather than the `mtp.layers.*` form the base maps, and there is no Puzzle MTP inference path in tree.

Changes:

1. **Per-layer `n_ff_exp` / `n_expert_used`** — the existing GGUF keys become scalar-OR-array via `get_key_or_arr` (same pattern as `n_ff_arr`). Scalar GGUFs broadcast, so this is 100% backward compatible and adds no new keys. `build_moe_ffn` aggregation is bounded by the per-layer top-k.
2. **Mechanical rename** — `n_ff_exp` → `n_ff_exp_impl`, `n_expert_used` → `n_expert_used_impl`, in its own isolated commit. This is what makes most of the file count: the scalar accessors had to give up their names to the per-layer ones, so every arch touching them is updated in a single no-behaviour-change commit.
3. **Converter** — `NemotronHPuzzleModel` parses `block_configs`, writes the per-layer arrays, dequantizes the FP8 checkpoint (weight_scale absorption), and accepts both tensor namings in the wild: the original `backbone.*` prefix and the officially distributed BF16 upload's `model.*` (`model.layers.*`, `model.embeddings`, `model.norm_f`) with `e_score_correction_bias` instead of `e_score_correction.bias`. Also fixes a pre-existing `_experts` AttributeError on `NemotronHModel`.
4. **75B.A9B vs 120B.A12B** — both have 88 layers; a heterogeneity check on the per-layer top-k array distinguishes them. Super is uniform, so it still resolves to 120B.A12B and keeps working as before.

## Additional information

**Validation.** The full-scope version of this branch was validated end to end on Strix Halo 128GB unified / Radeon 8060S: FP8 → Q8_0 conversion (83.4G, 781 tensors) clean with metadata verified, Q8_0 load and coherent generation under `-ngl 99`, an 18K-token long-context needle retrieved, and a quant A/B (wikitext-2, 24 chunks) giving PPL 5.325 Q8_0 / 5.377 IQ4_XS-mix / 5.404 Q4_K_M at 17.7–19.9 t/s decode and 211–243 t/s prefill on ROCm.

To be straight about what the *slimmed* branch has and has not been through: it is compile-gated, not load-gated. I no longer have the Puzzle GGUF or the HF checkout on this machine, so I have not re-run a conversion or a load smoke since the split. What is verified since: the tree builds clean, every commit builds individually (bisectable), the converter is lint- and syntax-clean at every commit, the model code has zero `nextn` references left, and the converter emits exactly the 88 trunk blocks the loader expects. It has also been rebased repeatedly onto master without conflicts, most recently onto the current tip. Re-verified on the current tip: builds clean, converter flake8-clean, and the `mtp.*` handling above is fixed and covered by the class docstring.

GGUFs and a reusable imatrix: https://huggingface.co/YanissAmz/Nemotron-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B-GGUF

A separate converter extension to Nemotron-3-Super-120B has been proposed by another contributor in the comments below; it is small and independent, and best as its own PR.

Note unrelated to this diff: Vulkan (RADV gfx1151) decode collapses on 4-bit MoE quants (`mul_mat_id` path) while Q8_0 is fine — ROCm/HIP is the fast backend for this model on Strix Halo. Possibly worth a separate issue.

## Overview

Related to #25890.

Up to 20-60% lower RPC model load time by adding GGML_RPC_LOAD_THREADS. 

On RPC-cache loads, the client fully FNV-hashes each large RPC tensor one at a time before dispatching it. For large models, this can pin a single CPU core at 100% while the remaining cores sit mostly idle.

This change:
- Uses an opt-in worker pool (GGML_RPC_LOAD_THREADS) to hash large mmap-backed RPC tensors concurrently.
- Serializes complete set_tensor transactions, because RPC devices for the same endpoint may share a socket (e.g. RPC0 and RPC1 will share a socket).
- Makes no changes to the default loading path, RPC protocol, or cache format

items.body:
Fixes crash when running with Gemma MTP and Tensor. Originally found while playing with [beelama](https://github.com/Anbeeld/beellama.cpp), discovered it also affected mainline, and found others with the issue. 

Two contexts sharing memory under SPLIT_MODE_TENSOR (e.g. Gemma4 MTP or EAGLE3 draft + target) both create views into the same meta-backend buffers. Reusing a stale graph after the peer has rebuilt leaves dangling per-device tensor references, causing fattn.cu:579 crashes.

Fix: disable graph reuse for both contexts when either uses tensor split and they share memory. Backend-agnostic, applies to Gemma4 MTP and EAGLE3. 

Confirmed on 2x 7900 XTX (ROCm/HIP/RCCL) with 3 sequential same-slot requests.
Also confirmed on NVIDIA by testers in #24314.

Fixes #24324, #24314, #24440  

- [x] I have read and agree with the contributing guidelines

items.body:
# RCA: Whole-Host Lock During MTP Prefill

**Model:** Qwopus3.6-27B-Fusion-Q5_K_M on dual RTX 3090 (tensor split) 
(tested with multiple models and they all do it. This is not a bug in a particular model's mtp head as detailed below.)

**Context:** llama.cpp b9745, speculative decoding via MTP

**Impact:** Full host lock requiring power cycle during long-prompt prefill with MTP active.

I have read and agree with the contributing guideline =  Yes
AI usage disclosure = Yes
---

## Summary

Huge prefills (100k+ tokens) reliably locked the system within a short period when MTP speculative decoding was enabled. MTP-off completed identical requests fine (~295 s).

Root cause: MTP draft catch-up queued two GPU graphs against the same mutable KV cache without waiting for either to finish. Under prolonged tensor-split prefill, the overlapping work hit a dependency error inside the CUDA/meta backend and at least one GPU entered a non-completing kernel. 

Note: **The issue inside the backend is still unknown.** I spent probably 6 hours and a dozen of hard-wedges solving the sync issue. I'm spent. Additionally, I didn't want to mix a speculative CUDA fix into a concrete MTP repair.

Fix: serialize MTP ubatches so each finishes before the next starts.

---

## How it was finally pinpointed and reproduced reliably

Added explicit `llama_synchronize(ctx_dft)` after the catch-up call. The host locked at that synchronize confirming the failing work lives inside the draft context, not the target.

Both draft ubatches had already logged success (`CTX-COMPUTE-EXIT status=0`, `AR-EXIT ok=1`) because the API accepts queued work without waiting for GPU completion.

To confirm serialization alone was the cure, I added per-ubatch synchronization inside `llama_context::decode()` no eval callback, normal graph UID reuse. I then ran three consecutive high-prefill sweeps (100k-180k). Each completed successfully, zero failures. Great success.

Earlier tests using scheduler eval callbacks succeeded too, including a terminal-only callback creating no interior graph cut which rules out theories about K/V or attention boundaries being required.

None of these fixes were necessary when MTP was off. I can say with confidence that it is a race issue on systems with multiple GPUs and MTP.

---

## Other theories disproven

Disabling CUDA graphs, switching to fallback/butterfly allreduce, disabling ASPM L1, reverting from kernel 7.0.0-29 to 7.0.0-28. None of these prevented the wedge. Memory and VRAM remained available throughout. Failure position varied from ~78k to ~143k tokens with no deterministic boundary. 

These results narrow the failure to the overlap condition itself.

---

## When the code was introduced

PR #22673 added `llama_decode(ctx_dft, batch)` for MTP catch-up on May 16, 2026 without synchronization between internally split ubatches. Has been there since MTP support was added to llama.cpp. Short-context operations fit in one ubatch so they never triggered it. This workload guarantees multiple ubatches (2048 batch vs. 1024 ubatch). This bug has been present since MTP support was added to llama.

---

## Fix

Synchronize after each internal ubatch for MTP contexts:

```cpp
bool mtp_multi_ubatch = false;
do {
    const auto & ubatch = mctx->get_ubatch();
    // ... process ...
    bool has_next = mctx->next();
    mtp_multi_ubatch |= has_next;
    if (cparams.ctx_type == LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP && mtp_multi_ubatch) {
        synchronize();
    }
} while (has_next);
```

Only activates for MTP contexts with multiple ubatches. Target decode, non-MTP speculative decoding, and short MTP drafts pass through unchanged.

---

## Regression test

The upstream-ready checkout adds `test-mtp-ubatch-sync` to `tests/test-llama-archs.cpp`.

The test builds a tiny synthetic Qwen3.5 model with one MTP layer and runs a four-token MTP batch on CPU:
- `n_batch=4`, `n_ubatch=2`: two internal ubatches. The test requires synchronization before the second ubatch starts.
- `n_batch=4`, `n_ubatch=4`: one internal ubatch. The test verifies that this path remains asynchronous.

The CPU abort callback runs while each graph is executing. `synchronize()` accounts the queued tokens in `llama_perf_context`, so the callback on the second ubatch can tell whether the first ubatch was synchronized. This tests ordering inside the actual decode loop without requiring CUDA or reproducing a host lock in CI.

Before:

```text
MTP ubatches were not synchronized
test-mtp-ubatch-sync: Failed
```

After:

```text
test-mtp-ubatch-sync: Passed (0.02 s)
```


## Upstream issue

The existing report that most closely matches this failure is [#23210: llama-server crashes on CUDA with Qwen3.6-27B](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/23210). It includes Qwen3.6, CUDA, MTP, long-context prefill, multi-GPU configurations, and hard GPU/host hangs. No open PR matching the ubatch serialization fix was found.

Issue #26558 is a different MTP crash involving CUDA graph-cache growth and an invalid cuBLAS stream. Its `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` workaround did not fix this reproducer in two controlled atts. I wanted to note it anyway for reviewers looking at the PR.

# Disclosure Note
Investigative analysis was done manually and in conjunction with GPT 5.6 Sol. I sign off on the code used to patch llama. It is the proper chokepoint for the repair. I explored a bunch of different approaches and this was the right one as it does not have a performance impact in day-to-day usage and fixes the issue as close to the root (without getting into repairing the backend) as possible.

version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10428, commit 885c5bbe8)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

1 RTX 5070TI + 1 RTX3060TI

### Models

Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF/tree/main

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

While decoding tokens, generation suddenly freezes and GPU utilization jumps from around 85 % while generating to 100% in the frozen state. The server doesn't report an error and doesn't recover. System is stable and responsive. Restarting llama-server solves the problem, till next lockup.

The problem does seem to only occur with using --split-mode tensor and --spec-type draft-mtp together. Sometimes it occurs after 7 tokens, sometimes after 40,000 tokens and sometimes never. The higher the --spec-draft-n-max value, the sooner the lockup happens. Everything over --spec-draft-n-max 2 seems to lead to a pretty much instant lockup.

Without --spec-type draft-mtp enabled, --split-mode tensor seems stable.

With --split-mode layer the problem doesn't occur at all, not even at dysfunctional --spec-draft-n-max 5.

Here my config. Tried removing ngram-mod and ngram-map-k4v as well but this had no influence. Neither did reducing --ctx-size for more VRAM headroom. I had a feeling though, that modifying --batch-size and --ubatch-size had an influence on when the problem occurs but that very well could have been a random fluke.

--spec-draft-device CUDA0
--spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod,ngram-map-k4v
--spec-draft-n-max 2
--spec-draft-n-min 0
--spec-draft-p-min 0.0
--spec-ngram-mod-n-match 36
--spec-ngram-mod-n-min 48
--spec-ngram-mod-n-max 64
--spec-ngram-map-k4v-size-n 12 
--spec-ngram-map-k4v-size-m 48
--spec-ngram-map-k4v-min-hits 1
--parallel 1
--main-gpu 0
--ctx-size 65336
--batch-size 1024
--ubatch-size 512
--cache-type-k q8_0
--cache-type-v q8_0
--kv-unified
--split-mode tensor
--tensor-split 2.05,0.95
--cache-reuse 256
--cache-ram 32768
--checkpoint-min-step 512
--ctx-checkpoints 8 

### First Bad Commit

Unidentified, but the problem ranges at least from b10428 to b10436

items.title: Eval bug: MTP triggers reproducible CUDA lockups with Qwen3.8-27B while --split-mode tensor

items.body:
### Name and Version

llama.cpp b10595
commit e8eed4525aaca00a78d8f837dce90dd4d4708133

Official Windows x64 CUDA 13.3 build:
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b10595

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Ryzen 9 9950X
96 GB DDR5
2x RTX 3090 24 GB
Windows 11

Both GPUs are used with:

--device CUDA0,CUDA1
--split-mode tensor
--tensor-split 1,1

### Models

Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_M.gguf
BF16 mmproj

https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I have been investigating persistent instability in the 2-GPU tensor-split path on Windows with Qwen 3.8 27B.

There are already reports such as #27122 where the problem appears tied to MTP. In my case I was also able to reproduce a failure on an official upstream llama.cpp b10595 build with MTP completely disabled, so MTP is not required for at least one failure surface.

The upstream test used:

```text
Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_M.gguf
BF16 mmproj

Windows 11
2x RTX 3090 24 GB

--device CUDA0,CUDA1
--split-mode tensor
--tensor-split 1,1
--ctx-size 131072
--fit off
-b 4096
-ub 1024
--cache-type-k bf16
--cache-type-v bf16
--kv-unified

mmproj enabled with --no-mmproj-offload
MTP disabled
````

On b10595:

1. Initial small canary passed.
2. A large request with 24,344 prompt tokens passed.
3. The following image-first request failed.
4. The client connection was reset and llama-server later aborted with a CUDA error at `ggml-cuda.cu:107`.

The minimum free VRAM during this run was about 8,536 MiB on CUDA0 and 8,440 MiB on CUDA1.

As a preface, I am not claiming that every failure described below has the same root cause. The upstream failure surfaced as a CUDA abort, while some of my fork reproductions surfaced as a no-progress GPU state instead. What I can establish is that the affected execution area is not limited to MTP.

I have been working on this in BeeLlama, which is a llama.cpp fork. I pushed the current investigation checkpoint here:

Branch: [v0.4.4-wddm](https://github.com/Anbeeld/beellama.cpp/tree/v0.4.4-wddm)
Commit: [0c594be](https://github.com/Anbeeld/beellama.cpp/commit/0c594be0d96a409e21a4dd4e0a35e4a6e2c23506)

This is NOT a fix or a stable candidate. It contains the useful correctness work that survived the investigation, but the remaining multi-GPU failure is still unresolved.

The investigation covered tensor-split metadata propagation, projected graph reuse/lifetime, scheduler topology reuse, CUDA resource/device ownership, and the Windows two-device no-P2P collective path.

Some useful negative results:

* Disabling CUDA graphs did not eliminate the failure.
* `LLAMA_GRAPH_REUSE_DISABLE=1` did not eliminate the BeeLlama reproducer either. One fresh request still stopped making progress after 20,535 prompt tokens while running at about 1,368 prompt tok/s.
* Reducing the local WDDM collective to one reusable generation slot did not fix it.
* Broad synchronization/retirement of prior projected graph generations moved the failure but did not eliminate it.
* The exact projected operation observed near one failure was:
  `Q5_K [3072,5120] x F32 [3072,1024] -> F32 [5120,1024]`.
  The same operation completes standalone on both RTX 3090s at about 79-80 TFLOPS.
* Routing that exact projected Q5_K operation through cuBLAS did not fix the real workload.
* Broadly disabling CUDA fusion/MMQ also did not establish a fix.
* Several slower synchronization/single-stream variants could make the test sequence pass, but prefill dropped from about 1,349 tok/s to roughly 795-806 tok/s. I treated those as timing/order sensitivity evidence, not fixes.
* Reproduced failures frequently occurred with roughly 8 GiB of dedicated VRAM still free per GPU and without progressive shared-memory growth.

There is also no established deterministic token boundary.

During prompt minimization an approximately 14-15k-token request initially failed, but after freezing the exact request it tokenized to 14,425 prompt tokens and passed three fresh processes. So I do not think this is a simple "Nth 4096-token batch always fails" problem. The failure appears timing/order sensitive.

Retained same-process state is also not universally required. On a clean diagnostic-free BeeLlama build I reproduced a first-request stall around 16,439 / 24,345 prompt tokens at about 1,365 tok/s, again with about 8.4 GiB free per GPU.

At the same time, retained workloads are clearly affected too. After publishing the checkpoint I tried using it normally with:

```text
--ctx-size 262144
-b 4096
-ub 2048
--split-mode tensor
--tensor-split 1,1
--spec-type draft-mtp
mmproj enabled
```

It ran normally for several requests and reached 62,261 retained tokens. On the next request it generated 247 tokens and then crashed with:

```text
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_ar_wddm_allreduce
cudaEventSynchronize(p->published[i][slot])
```

So the current state is:

* 2-GPU CUDA tensor split is demonstrably unstable in this workload family.
* MTP can trigger failures, but an upstream MTP-off reproduction also exists.
* VRAM exhaustion is not required.
* CUDA graph reuse alone is not sufficient to explain it.
* The exact projected Q5_K arithmetic works in isolation.
* Slower/synchronizing execution often suppresses the problem, which suggests an ordering/lifetime race, but I have not isolated the owning invariant.

I am stuck after a fairly extensive investigation and would appreciate collaboration from anyone familiar with the meta backend, tensor-split scheduler, CUDA event/resource lifetime, or multi-GPU execution.

I can run targeted builds, diagnostics, or reduced test cases.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown.

Confirmed on upstream b10595 / e8eed4525aaca00a78d8f837dce90dd4d4708133.

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Upstream b10595 result</summary>

```console
Configuration:
Windows 11
2x RTX 3090
Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_M
tensor split 1,1
ctx 1310

items.title: Eval bug: GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL) on Vulkan since b9318

items.body:
## Overview

`llama-server` / `llama-cli` with `--spec-type draft-mtp` aborts on the Vulkan backend (#23737, open since May 26):

```
ggml-backend.cpp:348: GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated") failed
```

backtrace: `common_prompt_checkpoint::update_dft → server_context_impl::create_checkpoint → pre_decode`. First bad commit: 6c4cbdc70 (#23646).

The k_stream/v_stream views are created **before** the k/v tensors are allocated. On allocation paths that skip `ggml_backend_view_init` (observed: the draft-MTP KV on Vulkan — debugged down to `cache_k_l64 (view)` / `cache_v_l64 (view)`, layer 64 being the nextn/draft layer), they keep `tensor->data == NULL` forever while their storage lives on `view_src`. Direct IO — the draft-mtp checkpoint serialization and stream-to-stream copies (`llama-kv-cache.cpp:846`) — then feeds those views to `ggml_backend_tensor_get/set`, which require an initialized tensor on every backend that addresses via `tensor->data` (CPU memcpy; CUDA/HIP analogous).

Fix: after the KV buffers are allocated, initialize any still-uninitialized stream view via `ggml_backend_view_init`. 20 lines, guarded to `!hparams.no_alloc`, and only touches views that are actually uninitialized (`data == NULL`, backing allocated).

The root-cause analysis originates with @Yoshi4470 (issue thread, June 6, fork commit 09c1af8dd). This PR fixes the same bug at the source rather than relaxing the ggml-backend asserts: we verified that assert relaxation alone leaves the CPU backend reading through a NULL `tensor->data` (segfault) — only backends whose get/set address via `view_src` (Vulkan) survive it.

## Reproduction / verification (gfx1151 / RADV 25.2.8, ROCm 7.2.2 for the HIP control, Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL + mmproj)

Before (stock fc35562ba): abort in 14 s at first inference.

```
./llama-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
  -fa on -ctk q5_1 -ctv q5_1 -c 1048576 --no-mmap \
  -p "Say hello in one sentence." -n 32 --temp 0 --single-turn
```

After (this branch @ 67e1862fd, rebuilt from the pushed commit):

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| CLI repro above | abort in 14 s | completes, coherent output, 31.8 t/s |
| server `-np 4 -c 1048576 --spec-type draft-mtp` | crash | 8 sequential requests OK, 0 asserts |
| `/slots` save/restore (same IO family) | crash path | save + restore + correct generation after |
| tool calling / JSON schema / vision (mmproj) + draft-mtp | — | all pass |
| HIP build, same tests | unaffected | unaffected |

A unit test would need a full `llama_kv_cache` construction (model + device context); the CLI command above is the reproducible regression check, matching the issue's reporter environment.

### Additional information

The issue has four independent reporters (Strix Halo / RADV, Radeon AI PRO r9700); the most recent crash report in the thread is from July 20. cc @cdanis @artisticMink @Andy4OS — verification on your machines welcome.

### Performance (cross-backend data taken while verifying this fix)

Measured on a tree combining #27311 (the scheduler input-ring fix — required for valid HIP numbers under `--parallel`, see #27572) and this fix; both backends built from the same source. Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL, `-fa on -ctk/-ctv q4_0 -b 1024 -ub 512`, per-slot ctx 262144, realistic corpus, temp 0, 3-run medians; server-process CPU from /proc deltas.

**Server tg t/s (draft-mtp n4 / plain), with draft acceptance medians:**

| prompt | HIP MTP | HIP acc | VK MTP | VK acc | HIP plain | VK plain |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 616 | 21.1 | 0.64 | 19.5 | 0.53 | 11.5 | 7.3 |
| 3796 | 18.0 | 0.52 | 18.1 | 0.55 | 9.6 | 6.8 |
| 7404 | 16.1 | 0.47 | 14.4 | 0.44 | 7.6 | 6.7 |
| 15681 | 14.8 | 0.45 | 16.0 | 0.50 | 6.4 | 6.5 |

VK MTP tg tracks its acceptance, not length: the 7404 dip is a less draft-predictable corpus chunk (acc 0.44 vs ~0.50 elsewhere), while VK plain decode is position-flat — HIP MTP declines on both counts (position + acceptance).

**Server pp t/s:** HIP 266–315, VK 127–233 across the same sizes.

**Position scaling (llama-bench tg32, depth fill, r1, no-warmup):**

| depth | HIP | VK |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 11.35 | 9.71 |
| 16384 | 9.75 | 9.20 |
| 32768 | 8.31 | 9.43 |
| 65536 | 6.41 | 10.28 |
| 98304 | 4.84 | 10.03 |

Vulkan decode is position-invariant (~9.2–10.3 flat) while HIP degrades linearly (-57% over 98K); crossover ~20–30K tokens. This is independent of this fix but is the reason it matters: long-context draft-mtp on Vulkan becomes reachable for the first time on this hardware class, and it is the faster backend there.

**Server-process CPU:** VK 0.6–1.0% avg (p95 2–3%) vs HIP 3.8–5.1% (p95 12–18%).

**Vision (mmproj) image encode, 640×480:** HIP 1.64 s, VK 3.60 s.

No measurable delta from this fix itself: the change only initializes views that were previously uninitialized (and aborting) — it adds no work to any steady-state path.

## Requirements

- [x] I have read and agree with the contributing guidelines
- AI usage disclosure: YES — the change and verification commands were developed with AI assistance (root-cause debugging, patch, benchmark harness); the root cause was first identified by @Yoshi4470 in the issue thread. Reviewed and verified on hardware by the PR author.

### Name and Version

fox@ubuntu-llm:~/kitsu$ llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server --version
version: 9893 (d75936111)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL --fit-target 512 --n-gpu-layers 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -np 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### TL;DR

When running with `--fit-params` enabled and without specifying a `--ctx-size`, `load_model` overestimates the memory footprint of any mtp/draft context. It uses `n_ctx_train` to estimate the speculative component's size, rather than the actual context size, which is not determined until after fit is run for the draft/mtp context.

On my 32 GB VRAM machine, I found that `fit-params` was overestimating qwen3.6's MTP context by ~500 MiB.

### Examples

After identifying this bug, I tested loading models when `fit-params` was enabled and disabled, and provide outputs below to show that the speculative context footprint is significantly overestimated. Each of these outputs are taken (and condensed for brevity) from llama-server logs run with the base command included above. I'm running this on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB VRAM). The only variation is in the `--ctx-size` passed in.

1. No `--ctx-size` specified (Estimated: 1672 MiB | Actual: 1189 MiB)

```ini
# MTP (Estimated):
[spec] estimated memory usage of MTP context is 1672.03 MiB
# ...
projected to use 34125 MiB of device memory vs. 31003 MiB of free device memory
# ...
context size reduced from 262144 to 179712 -> need 5313 MiB less memory in total

# MTP (Actual):
creating MTP draft context against the target model 'Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf'
# ...
llama_kv_cache:      CUDA0 KV buffer size =              702.00 MiB
sched_reserve:        CUDA0 compute buffer size =   487.03 MiB
```

2. `--ctx-size 179712` (Estimated: 1189 MiB | Actual: 1189 MiB)

```ini
# MTP (Estimated):
[spec] estimated memory usage of MTP context is 1189.03 MiB
# ...
projected to use 28812 MiB of device memory vs. 31003 MiB of free device memory
will leave 2190 >= 1701 MiB of free device memory, no changes needed

# MTP (Actual):
creating MTP draft context against the target model 'Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf'
# ...
llama_kv_cache:      CUDA0 KV buffer size =              702.00 MiB
sched_reserve:        CUDA0 compute buffer size =   487.03 MiB
```

_Here I saw I could push ctx higher, so I found the highest ctx value I could while still leaving enough memory to satisfy `fit-target 512`_

3. `--ctx-size 186600` (Estimated: 1229 MiB | Actual: 1229 MiB)

```ini
# MTP (Estimated):
[spec] estimated memory usage of MTP context is 1229.53 MiB
#...
projected to use 29257 MiB of device memory vs. 31003 MiB of free device memory
will leave 1745 >= 1741 MiB of free device memory, no changes needed

# MTP (Actual):
creating MTP draft context against the target model 'Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf'
# ...
llama_kv_cache:      CUDA0 KV buffer size =              729.00 MiB
sched_reserve:        CUDA0 compute buffer size =   500.53 MiB
```

### First Bad Commit

I think this has been around since MTP was introduced

### Relevant log output

See above

### Conclusion

This issue exists because of the way fit is calculated in `load_model`. 

The fit process is performed separately between the `mmproj`, `spec/mtp`, and main model/ctx. However, the best fit for one component clearly depends on the fit results for the others. The proper fix for this is likely to pull "fit" out of the `common_init_result` constructor and into a dedicated library that performs fit for all loaded components, together.

## Overview

When running with `--fit-params` enabled and without specifying a `--ctx-size`, `load_model` overestimates the memory footprint of any draft/mtp context. It uses `n_ctx_train` to estimate speculative context size, rather than the actual context size. This is due to the fact that `n_ctx` is not determined until after the main model fit is run.

As a result, speculative contexts take up more VRAM than they should. On my 32 GB machine, I found that `--fit-params` was overestimating qwen3.6's MTP context by ~500 MiB.

- a helper method now splits speculative context fit into two parts: a fixed component, and a per-ctx component

items.title: Eval bug: AMD Vulkan vk::DeviceLostError crash sensitive to ubatch-size and context length

items.body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

items.title: Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets

items.body:
## Overview

Implements adaptive mtp with a new option `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive`

Suggested configuration to use is: `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive --spec-draft-n-max 12`

The algorithm is a counting based state machine with a climb counter and a weighted drop-pressure accumulator. The depth climbs one step after a number consecutive verifies that accepted every drafted token; any miss adds (N - acceptance) to the drop pressure and the depth drops one step once it exceeds a certain amount. High depths fall quickly (a total miss adds N), low depths hold, and at the floor no pressure accumulates at all.  The specific climb difficulty and drop pressure values were empirically determined over a wide range of tests.

`--spec-draft-n-max` bounds the upper adaptive range and both the floor and the cold-start depth default to 3.  The default floor of 3 may be adjusted  with `--spec-draft-n-min-adpative`, although in testing 3 seems to be the best value to choose here.

As higher depths are reached the barrier to climb higher is reduced.  This allows for predictive runs to quickly ascend after they've "proven" themselves.

## Latest Testing and Performance Results
_(Updated 23 Aug 2026)_

Latest performance results can be seen here: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5385811671

Extended discussion of results can be seen here: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5386016928

### Test Setup

- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (`Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf`
- Hardware: 2x AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32.6 GiB each), tensor split, Ryzen 9
  9950X3D2, ROCm, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2`, `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=0`
- Server: `llama-server` from branch `adaptive-mtp` (build 10459, 0c6426bcd,
  freshly rebuilt)
- Decode: greedy (temp 0.0, seed 675), top-k 20, top-p 0.95, min-p 0.001,
  ctx 262144, f16 KV, `--parallel 1`, mlock, reasoning on
  (`--reasoning-budget 65536 --reasoning-preserve`)
- 2 repeats per cell; tok/s = mean of `timings.predicted_per_second`
  (generation only, >= 4000 tokens per request)

 
### Configurations Tested

| ID | spec type | args |
|----|-----------|------|
| C0 | none | - |
| C1 | draft-mtp, fixed 3 | `--spec-draft-n-max 3` |
| C2 | draft-mtp, fixed 12, p-min | `--spec-draft-n-max 12 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75` |
| C3 | draft-mtp-adaptive 3..12 | `--spec-draft-n-min-adaptive 3 --spec-draft-n-max 12` |
| C4 | adaptive 3..12 + p-min | C3 + `--spec-draft-p-min 0.75` |
| C5 | ngram-mod | `--spec-ngram-mod-n-match 24 --spec-ngram-mod-n-min 48 --spec-ngram-mod-n-max 64` |
| C6 | adaptive + ngram-mod | C3 args + C5 args |
| C7 | fixed 3 + ngram-mod | C1 args + C5 args |
| C8 | fixed 12 + p-min + ngram-mod | C2 args + C5 args |

### Results

| config | reasoning | prose | code | recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 baseline | 30.03 | 30.08 | 30.03 | 29.93 |
| C1 fixed 3 | **51.68** | 55.89 | 69.28 | 81.94 |
| C2 fixed 12 + p-min 0.75 | 38.59 | 43.46 | 71.46 | 151.25 |
| C3 adaptive 3..12 | 51.42 | **56.64** | **78.03** | 147.46 |
| C4 adaptive + p-min 0.75 | 40.67 | 43.35 | 70.92 | 147.43 |
| C5 ngram-mod | 30.03 | 30.10 | 29.98 | 292.88 |
| C6 adaptive + ngram-mod | 51.48 | 56.61 | 73.06 | 321.25 |
| C7 fixed 3 + ngram-mod | 51.65 | 55.90 | 68.36 | 324.10 |
| C8 fixed 12 + p-min + ngram-mod | 41.34 | 43.73 | 64.39 | **325.68** |


## Additional information

218 lines of the diffs are a newly added test case file, and 92 lines are the new self-contained adaptive MTP header algorithm file. 

Half of the remaining ~150 lines of diffs are adding the two new command line options, and the other half (~75 lines) is the wiring of Adaptive MTP into llama.cpp.

I tried to keep the size of the functional changes to llama.cpp itself as small as possible, and I tried to keep this diff as independent as I could so that unless it's specifically activated, it won't interfere with normal llama.cpp operations.

I searched known issues and open PRs and did not find anything precisely mentioning this sort of feature.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: Yes.  I designed the exact algorithm.  AI chose the best place for it, and added it.  I then went over it all, reviewed it, cleaned up and changed half of it  to better reflect my intent, and then tested and refined the algorithm manually over the day.

items.body:
## Environment

- llama.cpp: upstream master as of 2026-08-26 (build **b10643**), self-built Release / CUDA sm_86. The only local patches are unrelated GGML kernel optimizations; `common/chat.cpp` and the server chat pipeline are vanilla.
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M GGUF with embedded official jinja template (+mmproj)
- Server flags: `-c 120000 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --split-mode layer -ts 1,1,1 --spec-type draft-mtp --tools all` (jinja default on)
- Client: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming, `tool_choice: auto`, ~33 tools (agentic CLI workload)

## Observed

Episodically (~2×/day under heavy agent use) a slot finishes a long generation normally and then the request dies:

```
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | eval time = 515042.58 ms / 11708 tokens
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | draft acceptance = 0.52296 (7151 accepted / 13674 generated)
I slot      release: id 3 | task 0 | stop processing: n_tokens = 37979, truncated = 0
W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <think>
W srv          stop: cancel task, id_task = 0
```

Note that `common_chat_peg_parse()` logs `effective_input.substr(result.end)` — i.e. **only the unconsumed tail**. In both captured occurrences that tail was literally `<think>\n` (8 bytes).

## Analysis

The model produced a fully valid turn — reasoning + content + one or more well-formed `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` blocks that match the per-request grammar — and then emitted a stray opening `<think>` immediately before stopping. Since the lazy grammar necessarily releases around/between tool calls, a few free tokens can land there; generation then stops (EOS / `n_predict`) leaving an unclosed tag behind.

The strict final parse (non-partial `common_chat_peg_parse()`) fails on that tail and throws:

```
The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format
```

…which makes the server cancel the task, so the client loses the entire already-generated response (~11.7k tokens here) purely because of 8 bytes of trailing garbage.

## Suggested remedies

Any of the following would remove the user-visible failure:

1. Make the autoparser's tool-call root tolerate trailing garbage after the last complete call (e.g. optional untagged `rest()` before end).
2. In `common_chat_peg_parse()` for non-partial input: before failing, retry the parse truncated right after the last complete `</tool_call>`; if it succeeds, return the structured message.
3. At minimum, don't throw on a *final* parse mismatch — degrade to raw-content passthrough instead of canceling the task.

We are running (2)+(3) locally with good results and would be happy to prepare a PR if this direction is acceptable.

## Related

- #27720 — gpt-oss malformed Harmony channel header fails the final PEG parse and errors the turn
- #27279 — peg-native + `response_format.json_schema`: parse throws → 500
- #27025 — same error string, Muse Glimmer tool calls

### Name and Version build : b10549-b2e5e9b28 windows vulkan 64bit ### Operating systems Windows ### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected? llama-server ### Command line ```shell Server (no speedup from MTP): llama-server.exe ^ -m "Gemma4-26B-A4B-QAT-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Balanced.Q4_0.gguf" ^ --model-draft "mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.gguf" ^ --spec-type draft-mtp ^ --spec-draft-n-max 2 ^ -np 1 ^ -ngl 99 ^ -c 34096 ^ -b 512 ^ --mlock ^ --flash-attn on ^ --no-mmap ^ --temp 0.6 --top-k 64 --top-p 0.9 --min-p 0.05 --repeat-penalty 1.1 ^ --jinja ^ --chat-template-file "chat_template.jinja" ^ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8081 --ctx-size 34096 CLI (full MTP speedup, same models/params): llama-cli.exe ^ -m "Gemma4-26B-A4B-QAT-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Balanced.Q4_0.gguf" ^ --model-draft "mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.gguf" ^ --spec-type draft-mtp ^ --spec-draft-n-max 2 ^ -ngl 99 -c 34096 -b 512 ^ --mlock --flash-attn on --no-mmap ^ --temp 0.6 --top-k 64 --top-p 0.9 --min-p 0.05 --repeat-penalty 1.1 ^ --jinja ^ --chat-template-file "chat_template.jinja" ^ ``` ### Problem description & steps to reproduce This is in regard to core ultra 135u igpu with unified memory.

Problem description & steps to reproduce

With MTP speculative decoding enabled, llama-cli gets a consistent, repeatable ~25–30% generation speedup over the plain (non-MTP) baseline. llama-server, run with the identical model pair and identical sampling/context/GPU-offload flags, gets effectively no speedup from MTP — despite a healthy draft acceptance rate (draft tokens are being accepted, not rejected).

Baseline (MTP flags removed entirely) is identical between the two binaries, which rules out generic server/CLI dispatch overhead as the cause and isolates the regression to the MTP draft/verify path specifically:

  | No MTP | With MTP (--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2) -- | -- | -- llama-cli | 6.8 t/s | ~8.5–9.2 t/s llama-server | 6.8 t/s | ~6.7–6.8 t/s

Server-side draft acceptance is reported as healthy (see log below), so the draft model is doing useful work — the accepted tokens simply aren't translating into wall-clock throughput on the server the way they do on the CLI.

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Launch llama-server with the command above.
  2. Send a single completion/chat request with a long-form prompt (~1800+ generated tokens in my testing) and note timings.predicted_per_second and the draft acceptance line in the server console.
  3. Launch llama-cli with the equivalent command (same models, same sampling params, -p/-n instead of a server request) and note the [ Prompt: X t/s | Generation: Y t/s ] summary.
  4. Repeat both with --model-draft/--spec-type/--spec-draft-n-max removed entirely to get the non-MTP baseline for each.
  5. Compare: baseline matches within noise; MTP uplift does not.
(CLI on this build does not print the detailed n_draft/n_accept breakdown even at -lv 2; only the summary line above is available — happy to rebuild with a patch or test flag if that would help narrow this down further.) Additional notes Both binaries give identical throughput (6.8 t/s) with MTP disabled, so this does not appear to be generic server dispatch/slot-loop overhead — it's specific to how the server executes the draft/verify cycle. Not immediately fixed by upstream PR #17808 ("server: improve speed of speculative decoding") — my build (b10549-b2e5e9b28) postdates that merge by a wide margin. Possibly related, though none is an exact match for this combination (Vulkan, discrete GPU, llama-server, healthy acceptance rate, zero net speedup): #23126 — Vulkan UMA/iGPU draft+target serialization (my case may or may not be UMA; symptom matches, hardware class may not) #23752 — MTP net-negative/net-zero throughput on Metal despite good acceptance (symptom matches closely, different backend) #27428 — draft-mtp regression on multi-GPU layer splits; code discussion explicitly references Gemma 4's MTP mem-share path in common/speculative.cpp, though the reported trigger there is layer-split specific and my setup is single-GPU ### First Bad Commit _No response_ ### Relevant log output slot print_timing: id 0 | task 0 | eval time = 258920.73 ms / 1760 tokens ( 147.20 ms per token, 6.79 tokens per second) total time = 268315.40 ms / 1880 tokens graphs reused = 768 draft acceptance = 0.63548 ( 985 accepted / 1550 generated), mean len = 2.27 CLI, MTP enabled, same prompt/model: [ Prompt: 8.7 t/s | Generation: 8.5 t/s ]

items.title: Eval bug: CUDA kernel stall during model execution, killed by watchdog

items.body:
## Summary

On a gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU, RDNA3.5) system with ROCm 7.2.4, the **HIP/ROCm** backend
produces corrupted output where the **Vulkan** backend, running the **same weights, the same
build, and byte-identical flags on the same machine**, is correct on every attempt.

Measured on three architectures. Two fail on HIP, with **different severity**; one is
unaffected:

| model | `general.architecture` | topology | Vulkan | HIP/ROCm |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct `Q4_K_M` | `llama` | dense | **16/16** @30,516 · 6/6 @1,616 | **0/16** @30,516 · **0/6 @1,616** |
| Qwen3.8-27B `UD-Q8_K_XL` | `qwen35` | dense | **16/16** @29,355 | **0/16** @29,355 · 6/6 @1,349 |
| Ling-3.0-flash `IQ4_XS` | `bailingmoe3` | 512-expert MoE | **16/16** @29,275 | **16/16** @29,275 |

(`@N` = prompt tokens. Each cell is 8 requests run twice; the repeat is deliberate, because a
single 8/8 is not enough to call a backend clean.)

Backend and binary path were read from `/proc/<pid>/exe` on **every** run, not inferred from
the launcher — an earlier "Vulkan" result in this investigation turned out to be the HIP server
still answering after a boot script silently failed.

### Two severities, deliberately not merged

- **`llama` is broken outright on HIP** — at *every* depth tested, including a 1,616-token
  prompt. Output is degenerate word salad:
  `'for 4\n<|contextual background\nline keep track\nTheater in line while mind the material and context in'`
  The same model, flags and template on Vulkan is 6/6 shallow and 16/16 at 30,516 tokens, so
  this is not a configuration error.
- **`qwen35` is correct at shallow depth and fails past roughly 29k tokens** when the request
  also carries a moderately large tool array. Output stays fluent and well-formed; the model
  confidently mis-states **its own tool list**. With an array of `read_file`, `tool_00` …
  `tool_15`:

  > I don't have a `read_file` tool available in my current toolset. The tools I have access to
  > are `tool_01` through `tool_15`, which are placeholder utilities that accept a single string
  > argument. None of them are file-reading tools.

  It has read the placeholders' *descriptions* correctly while losing the entries at the **head**
  of the array. Other samples invented tool names absent from the request entirely, or ran to
  the token limit emitting `finish_reason: "length"` with empty content and no tool call.

Whether these are one defect with severity varying by model, or two, is **not established here**.

### Hypothesis, on a single data point — please treat as a lead, not a finding

The two failing models are **dense**; the one that passes is a **512-expert MoE**. Dense and
MoE matmuls take different paths (`mul_mat` vs `mul_mat_id`), which may be where to look. This
rests on **one** MoE observation and no second MoE was tested. It is offered as a starting
point, not a claim.

## Still present on current master

Reproduced on stock upstream **`b21e4de74567f5eef213765c9476a843c2e43f0d`** — `master`
re-fetched immediately before building — from a clean detached worktree with no local patches,
built for gfx1151 with ROCm 7.2.4.

The same result holds on **`3a653fea932e`** (12 days earlier). **The two SHAs agreeing is
expected rather than corroborating:** there are 7 commits between them and **none touch
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda` or `ggml/src/ggml-hip`**, so it simply means nothing has been attempted on
this code path in that window. It should not be read as an independent second confirmation.

### It is not `e79e4bf66` — please do not close this as a duplicate of that commit

`e79e4bf66` ("ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations", #26696) is **present in every
tested tree and does not fix this.** It is the obvious suspect and it matched on every checkable
detail:

- its message describes `-fassociative-math` reassociating FP reductions and *"can flip greedy
  argmax on **RDNA3.5** (e.g. **MTP speculative decode** diverging from the non-speculative
  baseline)"*;
- the hardware here is gfx1151, which **is** RDNA3.5;
- one of the failing workloads runs `--spec-type draft-mtp`;
- an older tree used here still carries the flag at `ggml/src/ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt:130`,
  while every tree tested above does not.

With that flag already removed, the defect reproduces at 0/16. This is either a second,
independent problem or the same one with another cause.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | stock `b21e4de74567f`; also reproduced on `3a653fea932e` |
| GPU | gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU), 128 GB unified memory |
| ROCm | 7.2.4 (hipcc 7.2.53211-97f5574fe2, AMD clang 22.0.0git roc-7.2.4) |
| OS | Linux |
| Build flags | `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/lib/llvm/bin/clang++ -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=ON` |

## Server flags — identical on both backends, only the binary differs

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on
--ctx-size 65536 --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--parallel 1 --threads 16
--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0
--ctx-checkpoints 32 --checkpoint-min-step 8192
--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
--jinja        # each model uses its own embedded chat template
```

Verified byte-identical with `diff` between the two launcher files; the only differences are a
comment header, the slot-save path, and the binary path.

## Causes eliminated, each by changing ONE variable

Listed so nobody spends replies asking. Every row was measured; all remained failing:

| varied | result |
|---|---|
| Context depth | not the cause — 1 tool at 36,335 tokens is 5/5 correct, *longer* than the failing case |
| Tool count | not the cause — 17 tools at 1,349 tokens is 6/6 correct |
| Total prompt length | not the cause — see the 36,335-token row above |
| KV cache type | `q4_0`, `q8_0`, `f16` all fail |

items.body:
## Overview The Q4_K/Q5_K scale unpack branches on a runtime value to pick between two layouts. nvcc can't fold that, so it predicates it and then repeats the whole thing for every column of the ncols_dst loop instead of doing it once. Swapping the branch for a mask select fixes it: predicated instructions at ncols_dst=8 go from 226 to 34, and the Q4_K kernel at 16 columns from 2256 to 1648. None of the other quant types have this problem, they already unpack unconditionally (Q3_K does the same 6-bit layout with plain shifts). We see perf gains from batch size >=4 on RTX 5090 and >=5 on RTX 4090 (more details in the Performance drop down), however we do not see a gain with DGX Spark, and in fact a small regression at batch sizes 4-6, which is why the change is gated off there. The most probable reason for this can be that the memory bandwidth on DGX Spark is much lower than that of RTX 4090 or 5090, and this means even with this optimization there is no effective time to save, since in the original code the unpack was already running while the kernel waits on the weight loads and so was not adding to the total time.
Performance

## Benchmarks (RTX 5090, sm_120, CUDA 12.9, driver 620.23) Both builds are from the same commit; the only difference is this patch. Batch size below refers to `ne11`, the number of columns the matmul receives in a single forward pass. It can arise in three ways, which are indistinguishable to the kernel: N concurrent requests against a server started with `-np N`, a draft block of `n_max + 1` tokens on a single slot, or `llama-bench -p N` directly. Two rows per model. `decode` is `llama-bench -p N -n 0 -embd 1 -r 40`, a single forward pass of N tokens with nothing generated, which is the decode step at batch N. `end to end` is llama-server tokens/sec, which also includes prefill, sampling and the draft model, and is therefore always lower. `*` marks a quant type this patch does not modify. ### 1. vs batch size Llama-3.1-8B, no draft model; only `-np` changes. The llama-server figures are total tokens over wall time at 256 tokens per request, temperature 0, across 3 runs alternating between the two builds. The request count is always a multiple of the batch size so that the final wave is not partially filled. | quant | metric | batch 1 | batch 2 | batch 4 | batch 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K_M** | decode | **-0.3%** | **+1.6%** | **+8.9%** | **+14.7%** | | | end to end | +0.4% | +1.1% | +7.4% | +10.8% | | **Q5_K_M** | decode | **+0.4%** | **+2.0%** | **+6.6%** | **+14.2%** | | | end to end | -0.1% | +1.5% | +5.5% | +11.4% | | **Q6_K** * | decode | **-1.2%** | **-1.1%** | **-0.8%** | **-0.9%** | | | end to end | -0.1% | +0.2% | +0.3% | +0.2% | There is no effect at batch 1, which is expected: the unpack can only be amortised once there is more than one column to share it across. ### 2. Other models Batch pinned at 4, no draft model. | model | metric | Q4_K_M | Q5_K_M | Q6_K * | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Llama-3.1-8B** | decode | **+8.9%** | **+6.6%** | **-0.8%** | | | end to end | +7.4% | +5.5% | +0.3% | | **gemma-4-12B** | decode | **+8.2%** | **+6.3%** | **+0.0%** | | | end to end | +6.8% | +6.0% | +0.1% | | **Qwen3.6-27B** | decode | **+6.2%** | **+5.1%** | **+0.3%** | | | end to end | +8.0% | +4.2% | +0.5% | ### 3. Batch from a draft block instead of concurrent requests `--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 3` on a single slot, so the target verifies 4 tokens in one pass: batch 4 obtained from a draft block rather than from concurrency. The decode rows repeat table 2 because it is the same file at the same batch; the kernel is indifferent to the source of the batch. | model | metric | Q4_K_M | Q5_K_M | Q6_K * | |---|---|---|---|---| | **gemma-4-12B-it** | decode | **+8.2%** | **+6.3%** | **+0.0%** | | | end to end | +6.3% | +6.2% | -0.7% | | **Qwen3.6-27B** | decode | **+6.2%** | **+5.1%** | **+0.3%** | | | end to end | +6.3% | +5.5% | +0.1% | ### 4. Decode over the whole batch range The same llama-bench run on `--pure` single-type models, so that every quantized `mul_mat` is the type in question. The Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M files above are mixed, with output and some attention tensors in Q6_K, which is why they report lower gains. | type | batch 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K** | +1.0% | +3.6% | +6.7% | +13.6% | +17.0% | +19.0% | +17.5% | +17.4% | | **Q5_K** | -0.6% | +2.0% | +1.7% | +9.3% | +10.3% | +16.8% | +15.9% | +17.2% | | **Q6_K** * | +0.3% | +0.4% | -1.0% | -0.5% | -0.8% | -0.4% | -1.6% | -0.6% | | **Q8_0** * | +1.1% | +0.3% | +1.0% | +1.3% | +1.0% | +1.8% | +1.9% | +1.7% | ## Benchmarks (RTX 4090, sm_89, CUDA 12.9, driver 591.86) Both builds are from the same commit; the only difference is this patch. Conventions are as above: `decode` is `llama-bench -p N -n 0 -embd 1 -r 40`, `end to end` is llama-server tokens/sec at 256 tokens per request, temperature 0. `*` marks a quant type this patch does not modify. Clocks were pinned, no interactive session was present on the machine, and the base build was run at both ends of every pass so that the noise floor is measured rather than assumed. Batch size throughout refers to `ne11`, the number of columns the matmul receives in a single forward pass. It can arise in three ways, which are indistinguishable to the kernel: N concurrent requests against a server started with `-np N`, a draft block of `n_max + 1` tokens on a single slot, or `llama-bench -p N` directly. Tables 1, 2 and 4 use the first and third; table 3 uses the second. ### 1. vs batch size Llama-3.1-8B, no draft model. Decode rows use `-p N`; end-to-end rows use `-np N` with the request count kept a multiple of N so that all slots remain occupied. | quant | metric | batch 1 | batch 2 | batch 4 | batch 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K_M** | decode | **+0.0%** |

## Overview

disable FA GQA packing for multi-token queries

## Additional information

Speculative verify runs flash attention with neq1 > 1 (several query tokens at once). Vulkan’s GQA-packed FA path treated N <= 8 as “use GQA packing,” then overwrote N with gqa_ratio and remapped workgroups as if there were a single query token. That is only valid for single-token decode, so multi-token parallel verify disagreed with sequential FA and drifted logits (e.g. wrong-draft windows with n_win >= 4)

Related to #25618

## Validation

Setup1: Qwen3-8B Q4 + DSpark n_max=7 using vulkan on strix halo
Before Fix: Diverging output as compared to just vanilla model at same seed & zero temp
After Fix: Exact Match

Setup2: Gemma-4 Q4 + MTP n_max=4
Result: Still diverging, there are other bugs as well that I plan to handle in other PRs. See #25618

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: Assisted by AI

### Models
