## Disclosure

I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, benchmarking and drafting of this PR, including this description and the commit messages. I have reviewed and validated everything myself; all measurements below were run on my own hardware and are reproducible. Flagging this explicitly per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Summary

`ggml_vk_should_use_mmvq()` returns early with *"MMVQ is generally good for batches"* for any `n > 1`. A speculative-decode step evaluates `n = 1 + n_draft` tokens, so it takes that path and enables MMVQ — bypassing the per-vendor small-`k` heuristics below it.

Those heuristics predate speculative decoding and were only ever reachable at `n == 1`. This PR raises the cutoff so decode-like `n` reaches them too. **No vendor threshold is changed** — they simply now apply at the small `n` a speculative step actually uses.

Enabling MMVQ there costs twice:

1. The Q8_1 quantization of the activations does not amortize at such small `n`.
2. It **perturbs the logits**, so the draft and the target disagree on tokens they should agree on — lowering **draft acceptance**.

The second effect is the less obvious one: MMVQ was not merely slower in the speculative path, it was degrading speculation quality.

## Commits

- `vulkan: don't use MMVQ for k-quants at small k on AMD` — AMD-specific tuning: for k-quants the Q8_1 quantization does not pay for itself at small `k`; DMMV is faster.
- `vulkan: treat a speculative-decode step as decode, not as a batch` — vendor-agnostic; raises the `n > 1` cutoff to `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N`.

## Testing

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" (gfx1151, 40 CU, RADV/Mesa), 128 GB unified memory.
Model: 35B-A3B MoE, Q6_K attention + Q4_K FFN. MTP self-speculation (`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`), ~33k context, 2 runs each, against master `7f575c39d`.

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TG, speculative | 75.2 t/s | **84.9 t/s** (+12.9%) |
| draft acceptance | 72–75% | **83–85%** |
| TG, non-speculative | 72.9 t/s | 73.9 t/s |
| PP (prefill), pp4096 | 679.4 t/s | 677.5 t/s (unchanged) |

Prefill is unaffected because `n` there is far larger — with a 2048 ubatch the per-expert token counts are ~64+, well above the cutoff, so batched MMVQ is retained.

An op-level trace of the MMVQ decisions during a speculative step on master shows the mechanism directly:

```
984x  n=3 k=2048 m=512  q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert up/gate)
492x  n=3 k=512  m=2048 q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert down)
220x  n=1 ...          q4_K -> dmmv      (plain decode, correctly bypassed)
```

## Caveats

- **I could only test gfx1151.** The second commit now applies to all vendors per review feedback, but I have no NVIDIA or Intel hardware to validate against. Numbers from someone with a dGPU would be very welcome — particularly whether MMVQ at `n = 2..8` is a win on those backends, since if so the cutoff may need to stay vendor-conditional.
- The first commit changes AMD behaviour at `n == 1` and therefore also affects **discrete** RDNA cards, which I likewise could not test. It is kept as a separate commit so it can be dropped independently.
- `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N = 8` is a bound chosen to cover common draft widths. Happy to derive it from the actual draft width instead if you'd prefer something less arbitrary.

items.body:
## Overview

Adds support for NVIDIA's Nemotron-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B (`NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM`), a hybrid mamba2/attention/MoE model with a per-layer heterogeneous MoE configuration.

Puzzle reuses the existing `nemotron_h_moe` machinery (latent MoE, relu2, routed scaling, hybrid cache) but is *heterogeneous per layer*: 88 blocks = 40 mamba2 + 8 attention (GQA 32/2, NoPE) + 40 MoE where `moe_intermediate_size` (1280–2688) and `num_experts_per_tok` (4–18) vary per block.

**Scope note:** this PR was slimmed down on request — the MTP/NEXTN draft-head support it originally carried has been removed and will come back as a separate follow-up PR once this lands, so the two can be reviewed independently. The removal covers the converter as well, not just the model code: it was emitting the `nextn` tensors, which would have produced GGUFs this loader rejects. `mtp.*` is now skipped for Puzzle. Note this is no longer the same as "what the other NemotronH variants do": #26725 landed MTP export on `NemotronHModel` after this branch was written, so the base class now keeps the head. Puzzle stays opted out explicitly (`supports_mtp_export = False`), since its head is laid out by `mtp_block_configs` rather than the `mtp.layers.*` form the base maps, and there is no Puzzle MTP inference path in tree.

Changes:

1. **Per-layer `n_ff_exp` / `n_expert_used`** — the existing GGUF keys become scalar-OR-array via `get_key_or_arr` (same pattern as `n_ff_arr`). Scalar GGUFs broadcast, so this is 100% backward compatible and adds no new keys. `build_moe_ffn` aggregation is bounded by the per-layer top-k.
2. **Mechanical rename** — `n_ff_exp` → `n_ff_exp_impl`, `n_expert_used` → `n_expert_used_impl`, in its own isolated commit. This is what makes most of the file count: the scalar accessors had to give up their names to the per-layer ones, so every arch touching them is updated in a single no-behaviour-change commit.
3. **Converter** — `NemotronHPuzzleModel` parses `block_configs`, writes the per-layer arrays, dequantizes the FP8 checkpoint (weight_scale absorption), and accepts both tensor namings in the wild: the original `backbone.*` prefix and the officially distributed BF16 upload's `model.*` (`model.layers.*`, `model.embeddings`, `model.norm_f`) with `e_score_correction_bias` instead of `e_score_correction.bias`. Also fixes a pre-existing `_experts` AttributeError on `NemotronHModel`.
4. **75B.A9B vs 120B.A12B** — both have 88 layers; a heterogeneity check on the per-layer top-k array distinguishes them. Super is uniform, so it still resolves to 120B.A12B and keeps working as before.

## Additional information

**Validation.** The full-scope version of this branch was validated end to end on Strix Halo 128GB unified / Radeon 8060S: FP8 → Q8_0 conversion (83.4G, 781 tensors) clean with metadata verified, Q8_0 load and coherent generation under `-ngl 99`, an 18K-token long-context needle retrieved, and a quant A/B (wikitext-2, 24 chunks) giving PPL 5.325 Q8_0 / 5.377 IQ4_XS-mix / 5.404 Q4_K_M at 17.7–19.9 t/s decode and 211–243 t/s prefill on ROCm.

To be straight about what the *slimmed* branch has and has not been through: it is compile-gated, not load-gated. I no longer have the Puzzle GGUF or the HF checkout on this machine, so I have not re-run a conversion or a load smoke since the split. What is verified since: the tree builds clean, every commit builds individually (bisectable), the converter is lint- and syntax-clean at every commit, the model code has zero `nextn` references left, and the converter emits exactly the 88 trunk blocks the loader expects. It has also been rebased repeatedly onto master without conflicts, most recently onto the current tip. Re-verified on the current tip: builds clean, converter flake8-clean, and the `mtp.*` handling above is fixed and covered by the class docstring.

GGUFs and a reusable imatrix: https://huggingface.co/YanissAmz/Nemotron-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B-GGUF

A separate converter extension to Nemotron-3-Super-120B has been proposed by another contributor in the comments below; it is small and independent, and best as its own PR.

Note unrelated to this diff: Vulkan (RADV gfx1151) decode collapses on 4-bit MoE quants (`mul_mat_id` path) while Q8_0 is fine — ROCm/HIP is the fast backend for this model on Strix Halo. Possibly worth a separate issue.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: **YES** — AI-assisted. I scoped the architecture, made the design decisions, reviewed every diff, and validated everything end-to-end on my hardware (Strix Halo 128GB, Vulkan/ROCm). I take full responsibility for the code and remain available for any requested change or test.

items.title: Eval bug: GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL) on Vulkan since b9318

items.body:
## Overview

`llama-server` / `llama-cli` with `--spec-type draft-mtp` aborts on the Vulkan backend (#23737, open since May 26):

```
ggml-backend.cpp:348: GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated") failed
```

backtrace: `common_prompt_checkpoint::update_dft → server_context_impl::create_checkpoint → pre_decode`. First bad commit: 6c4cbdc70 (#23646).

The k_stream/v_stream views are created **before** the k/v tensors are allocated. On allocation paths that skip `ggml_backend_view_init` (observed: the draft-MTP KV on Vulkan — debugged down to `cache_k_l64 (view)` / `cache_v_l64 (view)`, layer 64 being the nextn/draft layer), they keep `tensor->data == NULL` forever while their storage lives on `view_src`. Direct IO — the draft-mtp checkpoint serialization and stream-to-stream copies (`llama-kv-cache.cpp:846`) — then feeds those views to `ggml_backend_tensor_get/set`, which require an initialized tensor on every backend that addresses via `tensor->data` (CPU memcpy; CUDA/HIP analogous).

Fix: after the KV buffers are allocated, initialize any still-uninitialized stream view via `ggml_backend_view_init`. 20 lines, guarded to `!hparams.no_alloc`, and only touches views that are actually uninitialized (`data == NULL`, backing allocated).

The root-cause analysis originates with @Yoshi4470 (issue thread, June 6, fork commit 09c1af8dd). This PR fixes the same bug at the source rather than relaxing the ggml-backend asserts: we verified that assert relaxation alone leaves the CPU backend reading through a NULL `tensor->data` (segfault) — only backends whose get/set address via `view_src` (Vulkan) survive it.

## Reproduction / verification (gfx1151 / RADV 25.2.8, ROCm 7.2.2 for the HIP control, Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL + mmproj)

Before (stock fc35562ba): abort in 14 s at first inference.

```
./llama-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
  -fa on -ctk q5_1 -ctv q5_1 -c 1048576 --no-mmap \
  -p "Say hello in one sentence." -n 32 --temp 0 --single-turn
```

After (this branch @ 67e1862fd, rebuilt from the pushed commit):

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| CLI repro above | abort in 14 s | completes, coherent output, 31.8 t/s |
| server `-np 4 -c 1048576 --spec-type draft-mtp` | crash | 8 sequential requests OK, 0 asserts |
| `/slots` save/restore (same IO family) | crash path | save + restore + correct generation after |
| tool calling / JSON schema / vision (mmproj) + draft-mtp | — | all pass |
| HIP build, same tests | unaffected | unaffected |

A unit test would need a full `llama_kv_cache` construction (model + device context); the CLI command above is the reproducible regression check, matching the issue's reporter environment.

### Additional information

The issue has four independent reporters (Strix Halo / RADV, Radeon AI PRO r9700); the most recent crash report in the thread is from July 20. cc @cdanis @artisticMink @Andy4OS — verification on your machines welcome.

### Performance (cross-backend data taken while verifying this fix)

Measured on a tree combining #27311 (the scheduler input-ring fix — required for valid HIP numbers under `--parallel`, see #27572) and this fix; both backends built from the same source. Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL, `-fa on -ctk/-ctv q4_0 -b 1024 -ub 512`, per-slot ctx 262144, realistic corpus, temp 0, 3-run medians; server-process CPU from /proc deltas.

**Server tg t/s (draft-mtp n4 / plain), with draft acceptance medians:**

| prompt | HIP MTP | HIP acc | VK MTP | VK acc | HIP plain | VK plain |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 616 | 21.1 | 0.64 | 19.5 | 0.53 | 11.5 | 7.3 |
| 3796 | 18.0 | 0.52 | 18.1 | 0.55 | 9.6 | 6.8 |
| 7404 | 16.1 | 0.47 | 14.4 | 0.44 | 7.6 | 6.7 |
| 15681 | 14.8 | 0.45 | 16.0 | 0.50 | 6.4 | 6.5 |

VK MTP tg tracks its acceptance, not length: the 7404 dip is a less draft-predictable corpus chunk (acc 0.44 vs ~0.50 elsewhere), while VK plain decode is position-flat — HIP MTP declines on both counts (position + acceptance).

**Server pp t/s:** HIP 266–315, VK 127–233 across the same sizes.

**Position scaling (llama-bench tg32, depth fill, r1, no-warmup):**

| depth | HIP | VK |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 11.35 | 9.71 |
| 16384 | 9.75 | 9.20 |
| 32768 | 8.31 | 9.43 |
| 65536 | 6.41 | 10.28 |
| 98304 | 4.84 | 10.03 |

Vulkan decode is position-invariant (~9.2–10.3 flat) while HIP degrades linearly (-57% over 98K); crossover ~20–30K tokens. This is independent of this fix but is the reason it matters: long-context draft-mtp on Vulkan becomes reachable for the first time on this hardware class, and it is the faster backend there.

**Server-process CPU:** VK 0.6–1.0% avg (p95 2–3%) vs HIP 3.8–5.1% (p95 12–18%).

**Vision (mmproj) image encode, 640×480:** HIP 1.64 s, VK 3.60 s.

No measurable delta from this fix itself: the change only initializes views that were previously uninitialized (and aborting) — it adds no work to any steady-state path.

## Requirements

- [x] I have read and agree with the contributing guidelines
- AI usage disclosure: YES — the change and verification commands were developed with AI assistance (root-cause debugging, patch, benchmark harness); the root cause was first identified by @Yoshi4470 in the issue thread. Reviewed and verified on hardware by the PR author.

## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

items.title: Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets

items.body:
## Overview

Implements adaptive mtp with a new option `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive`

Suggested configuration to use is: `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive --spec-draft-n-max 12`

The algorithm is a counting based state machine with a climb counter and a weighted drop-pressure accumulator. The depth climbs one step after a number consecutive verifies that accepted every drafted token; any miss adds (N - acceptance) to the drop pressure and the depth drops one step once it exceeds a certain amount. High depths fall quickly (a total miss adds N), low depths hold, and at the floor no pressure accumulates at all.  The specific climb difficulty and drop pressure values were empirically determined over a wide range of tests.

`--spec-draft-n-max` bounds the upper adaptive range and both the floor and the cold-start depth default to 3.  The default floor of 3 may be adjusted  with `--spec-draft-n-min-adpative`, although in testing 3 seems to be the best value to choose here.

As higher depths are reached the barrier to climb higher is reduced.  This allows for predictive runs to quickly ascend after they've "proven" themselves.

## Latest Testing and Performance Results
_(Updated 23 Aug 2026)_

Latest performance results can be seen here: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5385811671

Extended discussion of results can be seen here: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5386016928

### Test Setup

- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (`Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf`
- Hardware: 2x AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32.6 GiB each), tensor split, Ryzen 9
  9950X3D2, ROCm, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2`, `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=0`
- Server: `llama-server` from branch `adaptive-mtp` (build 10459, 0c6426bcd,
  freshly rebuilt)
- Decode: greedy (temp 0.0, seed 675), top-k 20, top-p 0.95, min-p 0.001,
  ctx 262144, f16 KV, `--parallel 1`, mlock, reasoning on
  (`--reasoning-budget 65536 --reasoning-preserve`)
- 2 repeats per cell; tok/s = mean of `timings.predicted_per_second`
  (generation only, >= 4000 tokens per request)

 
### Configurations Tested

| ID | spec type | args |
|----|-----------|------|
| C0 | none | - |
| C1 | draft-mtp, fixed 3 | `--spec-draft-n-max 3` |
| C2 | draft-mtp, fixed 12, p-min | `--spec-draft-n-max 12 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75` |
| C3 | draft-mtp-adaptive 3..12 | `--spec-draft-n-min-adaptive 3 --spec-draft-n-max 12` |
| C4 | adaptive 3..12 + p-min | C3 + `--spec-draft-p-min 0.75` |

items.body:
## Summary

I isolated a metadata inconsistency in the official `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-Q4_0.gguf` artifact.

The affected GGUF contains Attention tensors for block 5:

* `blk.5.attn_k.weight`
* `blk.5.attn_q.weight`
* `blk.5.attn_v.weight`
* `blk.5.attn_output.weight`

It does not contain `blk.5.ssm_in.weight`.

However, its per layer `nemotron_h_moe.attention.head_count_kv` metadata is all zero. On the tested llama.cpp build, this causes block 5 to be interpreted as SSM and the loader attempts to resolve the nonexistent tensor `blk.5.ssm_in.weight`.

## Expected metadata

NVIDIA's model configuration declares `num_key_value_heads = 2` and identifies block 5 as an Attention layer.

The official ggml conversion log also first reports `key value head count = 2`, but later records a duplicate key overwrite of `nemotron_h_moe.attention.head_count_kv` with a 52 element all zero array.

## Reproduction environment

* GGUF: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-Q4_0.gguf`
* SHA256: `b1cc80f0bfa080612ac035cd54ddbe9c7c8283add596e7fe425445bfe4c5486f`
* llama.cpp: build 10626, commit `1729ed5371cd1ac6f6d6f3226f8803b080042839`
* OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4
* GPU: AMD Radeon 8060S, gfx1151
* ROCm: 7.2.53211-e1a6bc5663

## Causality test

I created a separate diagnostic copy and changed only the affected per layer KV head metadata. The original artifact was not modified.

The diagnostic copy successfully loaded and generated with:

1. CPU only execution
2. ROCm HIP partial GPU offload
3. ROCm HIP full GPU offload

This isolates the observed `blk.5.ssm_in.weight` failure to metadata driven Attention to SSM misclassification, rather than GPU memory capacity, Flash Attention, MTP, or ROCm offload in this test case.

## Requested guidance

Could maintainers confirm:

1. Whether the duplicate key overwrite is expected
2. Which component should preserve the correct per layer KV head values
3. Whether conversion or export should validate consistency among `layers_block_type`, `attention.head_count_kv`, `feed_forward_length`, and physical `attn_*` and `ssm_*` tensor namespaces before publishing

## Scope and limitations

This report concerns one official artifact identified by the SHA256 above. It does not claim that all Nemotron H GGUF files are affected, nor that ROCm has no independent Nemotron H or SSM limitations.

Technical report, raw observations, validation controls, and known good comparison artifact:

https://gist.github.com/redoracle/5928f33e31621c9ad2f451aab35d4776

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

this adds several fixes for rpc and rocm related GPU paths additional tuning and fixes crashes, prefill issues and general compatibility. Fixes #26746

### Included changes relative to upstream

#### HIP, RPC and long-context routing

- Enables hipCUB for HIP top-k and argsort, including the distributed RPC execution
  path, so these operations remain GPU-capable on ROCm.
- Adds a gfx1151-local Lightning Indexer top-k specialization for 512, 1024 and 2048
  candidates up to 8192 score entries, avoiding the expensive generic device-wide sort
  during DeepSeek-V4 long-context prefill.
- Keeps the Lightning Indexer key cache in F16 when a quantized KV cache is selected,
  where required by the DeepSeek path.
- Resolves fused operations per layer and device instead of disabling an entire graph
  on a single ROCm/RPC backend mismatch; the default fallback remains unfused GPU work,
  not CPU work.
- Fixes the HIP MMVF dispatch for MoE LoRA `MUL_MAT_ID` tensors. Rank-1 LoRA-B
  expert matrices now use the existing general GPU fallback instead of entering an
  MMVF kernel which requires an even K dimension; this prevents RPC worker crashes
  with valid DeepSeek-V4 expert LoRA adapters.

#### Strix Halo compute tuning

- Adds RDNA3.5/gfx1151 kernel and launch tuning for MMQ, MMVQ, Q8 MoE and expert MMQ.
- Caches MMVQ Q8_1 activations and partitions MMQ waves across rows and columns.
- Adds AMD WMMA Lightning Indexer support and tuned tiled Flash Attention, including a
  fix for NaNs in the compacted-tile mask path.
- Tunes Gated Delta Net and adds quantized-KV Flash Attention support for Strix Halo.
- Extends the gfx1151 MMVQ selection to the relevant Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8 and MXFP4 decode
  types, including the Q6_K VDR=2 decode kernel.
- Keeps HIP integrated-GPU host-buffer handling safe.

#### DeepSeek-V4 and speculative decoding

- Makes the grouped output-projection input contiguous for small multi-token
  DeepSeek-V4 speculative batches.
- Uses matching MMVQ and Flash-Attention kernel configurations for decode and small
  speculative/MTP verification batches, preventing numerical divergence between the
  logits used for acceptance checks.
- Keeps fused DeepSeek-V4 HC and Gated Delta Net operations on devices that support
  them while safely falling back only for mismatching layers.

#### Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 and hybrid SSM models

- Fuses SSM gate/beta projections, the SSM convolution-output L2 norm, and the SSM
  pre-scan chain (convolution, L2 norm, gate/beta).
- Folds SSM convolution-input concatenation into QKV MMVQ and fuses paired MMVQ
  matmuls that share an activation.
- Caches graph-local Q8_1 matmul inputs, folds Q8_1 quantization into RMS norm and
  gating-MUL, and fuses a matmul-plus-add-through-view sequence.
- Folds MoE top-k weights into the down projection and fuses the shared-expert output
  chain.
- Fuses IMRoPE and set-rows for BF16 KV cache use, and aligns the attention-gate
  tensor-parallel split with attention-Q.

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

tested on a halo strix cluster setup (RPC, rocm 7.14).

## Requirements

rocm 7.14, hipcub-dev (build requirements)
ROCm/HIP with hipCUB, HIP/ROCm >= 6.1.
Build for gfx1151 (-DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151).

items.body:
## Summary

On a gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU, RDNA3.5) system with ROCm 7.2.4, the **HIP/ROCm** backend
produces corrupted output where the **Vulkan** backend, running the **same weights, the same
build, and byte-identical flags on the same machine**, is correct on every attempt.

Measured on three architectures. Two fail on HIP, with **different severity**; one is
unaffected:

| model | `general.architecture` | topology | Vulkan | HIP/ROCm |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct `Q4_K_M` | `llama` | dense | **16/16** @30,516 · 6/6 @1,616 | **0/16** @30,516 · **0/6 @1,616** |
| Qwen3.8-27B `UD-Q8_K_XL` | `qwen35` | dense | **16/16** @29,355 | **0/16** @29,355 · 6/6 @1,349 |
| Ling-3.0-flash `IQ4_XS` | `bailingmoe3` | 512-expert MoE | **16/16** @29,275 | **16/16** @29,275 |

(`@N` = prompt tokens. Each cell is 8 requests run twice; the repeat is deliberate, because a
single 8/8 is not enough to call a backend clean.)

Backend and binary path were read from `/proc/<pid>/exe` on **every** run, not inferred from
the launcher — an earlier "Vulkan" result in this investigation turned out to be the HIP server
still answering after a boot script silently failed.

### Two severities, deliberately not merged

- **`llama` is broken outright on HIP** — at *every* depth tested, including a 1,616-token
  prompt. Output is degenerate word salad:
  `'for 4\n<|contextual background\nline keep track\nTheater in line while mind the material and context in'`
  The same model, flags and template on Vulkan is 6/6 shallow and 16/16 at 30,516 tokens, so
  this is not a configuration error.
- **`qwen35` is correct at shallow depth and fails past roughly 29k tokens** when the request
  also carries a moderately large tool array. Output stays fluent and well-formed; the model
  confidently mis-states **its own tool list**. With an array of `read_file`, `tool_00` …
  `tool_15`:

  > I don't have a `read_file` tool available in my current toolset. The tools I have access to
  > are `tool_01` through `tool_15`, which are placeholder utilities that accept a single string
  > argument. None of them are file-reading tools.

  It has read the placeholders' *descriptions* correctly while losing the entries at the **head**
  of the array. Other samples invented tool names absent from the request entirely, or ran to
  the token limit emitting `finish_reason: "length"` with empty content and no tool call.

Whether these are one defect with severity varying by model, or two, is **not established here**.

### Hypothesis, on a single data point — please treat as a lead, not a finding

The two failing models are **dense**; the one that passes is a **512-expert MoE**. Dense and
MoE matmuls take different paths (`mul_mat` vs `mul_mat_id`), which may be where to look. This
rests on **one** MoE observation and no second MoE was tested. It is offered as a starting
point, not a claim.

## Still present on current master

Reproduced on stock upstream **`b21e4de74567f5eef213765c9476a843c2e43f0d`** — `master`
re-fetched immediately before building — from a clean detached worktree with no local patches,
built for gfx1151 with ROCm 7.2.4.

The same result holds on **`3a653fea932e`** (12 days earlier). **The two SHAs agreeing is
expected rather than corroborating:** there are 7 commits between them and **none touch
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda` or `ggml/src/ggml-hip`**, so it simply means nothing has been attempted on
this code path in that window. It should not be read as an independent second confirmation.

### It is not `e79e4bf66` — please do not close this as a duplicate of that commit

`e79e4bf66` ("ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations", #26696) is **present in every
tested tree and does not fix this.** It is the obvious suspect and it matched on every checkable
detail:

- its message describes `-fassociative-math` reassociating FP reductions and *"can flip greedy
  argmax on **RDNA3.5** (e.g. **MTP speculative decode** diverging from the non-speculative
  baseline)"*;
- the hardware here is gfx1151, which **is** RDNA3.5;
- one of the failing workloads runs `--spec-type draft-mtp`;
- an older tree used here still carries the flag at `ggml/src/ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt:130`,
  while every tree tested above does not.

With that flag already removed, the defect reproduces at 0/16. This is either a second,
independent problem or the same one with another cause.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | stock `b21e4de74567f`; also reproduced on `3a653fea932e` |
| GPU | gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU), 128 GB unified memory |
| ROCm | 7.2.4 (hipcc 7.2.53211-97f5574fe2, AMD clang 22.0.0git roc-7.2.4) |
| OS | Linux |
| Build flags | `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/lib/llvm/bin/clang++ -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=ON` |

## Server flags — identical on both backends, only the binary differs

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on
--ctx-size 65536 --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--parallel 1 --threads 16
--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0
--ctx-checkpoints 32 --checkpoint-min-step 8192
--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
--jinja        # each model uses its own embedded chat template
```

Verified byte-identical with `diff` between the two launcher files; the only differences are a
comment header, the slot-save path, and the binary path.

## Causes eliminated, each by changing ONE variable

Listed so nobody spends replies asking. Every row was measured; all remained failing:

| varied | result |
|---|---|
| Context depth | not the cause — 1 tool at 36,335 tokens is 5/5 correct, *longer* than the failing case |
| Tool count | not the cause — 17 tools at 1,349 tokens is 6/6 correct |
| Total prompt length | not the cause — see the 36,335-token row above |
| KV cache type | `q4_0`, `q8_0`, `f16` all fail |
| Flash attention | `--flash-attn off` still fails; it changes the failure *mode*, not the failure. (Note `--flash-attn off`

items.body:
### Summary

On **gfx1151 (Strix Halo / Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Windows 11)** the **HIP backend silently corrupts inference of Qwen3.5-27B** (hybrid Gated-DeltaNet architecture, tested as VLM with mmproj): the **oldest part of the context is consistently lost** while output stays fluent and deterministic. The **Vulkan backend at the identical commit is correct**. We ran an extensive exclusion campaign (details below); every individually testable component passes, so the defect appears to live at graph-composition level of the GDN block on HIP.

### Environment

- HW: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S iGPU (**gfx1151**), 128 GB unified memory
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 26200, Adrenalin driver 32.0.31035.1003
- ROCm runtime: TheRock `therock-dist-windows-gfx1151-7.14.0rc3` (also reproduced with a different ROCm 7.x runtime DLL set)
- llama.cpp: official release zips `llama-b10453-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip` **and** `llama-b10582-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip`, **and** a self-built b10582 (e85caa81e) with the TheRock clang toolchain — **all three affected identically**
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (unsloth GGUF) + mmproj BF16
- Counter-checks: **Vulkan builds of the very same commits (b10453 and b10582) are correct**; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (pure attention, no GDN) is correct on the same HIP builds

### Reproduction (deterministic, temp 0)

Generate a synthetic 4-panel test image (no external assets needed):

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
W,H=660,640; img=Image.new('RGB',(W,H),'white'); d=ImageDraw.Draw(img)
try: fb=ImageFont.truetype('arialbd.ttf',20); fs=ImageFont.truetype('arial.ttf',14)
except: fb=fs=ImageFont.load_default()
for x,y,t,c in [(0,0,'Alpha Risk','Risk from parallel shifts of the reference rate.'),
                (330,0,'Beta Risk','Risk from non-parallel curve changes.'),
                (0,320,'Gamma Risk','Risk from embedded options, e.g. early repayment.'),
                (330,320,'Delta Risk','Risk from hedging with different rate indices.')]:
    d.rectangle([x+2,y+2,x+328,y+318],outline='black',width=2)
    d.ellipse([x+12,y+16,x+22,y+26],fill='black'); d.text((x+30,y+12),t,fill='black',font=fb)
    d.rectangle([x+30,y+50,x+290,y+200],outline='gray')
    if 'Gamma' in t:
        for i,bh in enumerate([60,90,130,100,80]): d.rectangle([x+50+i*45,y+195-bh,x+80+i*45,y+195],fill='gray')
    else: d.line([(x+40+i*25,y+190-int(12*(i**1.2))) for i in range(10)],fill='black',width=2)
    d.text((x+30,y+215),c,fill='black',font=fs)
img.save('synthetic_4panel.png')
```

```
llama-mtmd-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-BF16.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 4096 --temp 0 --seed 42 --image synthetic_4panel.png \
  -p "List ALL bold bullet headings in this image, top-left to bottom-right. Only the list."
```

- **HIP (gfx1151):** `['Beta Risk', 'Gamma Risk', 'Delta Risk']` — **top-left "Alpha Risk" (the oldest image tokens in raster order) is dropped**
- **Vulkan (same commit, same machine):** all four headings
- With a denser real-world 4-panel document scan the effect is stronger: HIP loses the entire upper half (0/4 headings) while Vulkan stays 4/4; flipping the image vertically "heals" it (the previously-top content becomes the newest tokens), which points at recency-position rather than image-coordinates.

### Exclusion campaign (everything below was tested on the same machine)

| Hypothesis | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime-DLL mismatch | official b10453 binary + clean matching TheRock 7.14 runtime | still wrong |
| Code regression / fix between builds | b10453 **and** b10582 built for **Vulkan** (same commits) | both correct → code exonerated |
| Toolchain | self-built HIP b10582 (TheRock clang) | reproduces official zips exactly |
| mtmd preprocessing | top-half crop alone is read fine; full preprocessing chain reviewed | exonerated |
| hipGraphs | `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | still wrong |
| ubatch state handoff | `-ub 128 / 512 / 8192` (whole prompt in one ubatch) | still wrong |

## Name and Version

This is reproducible with the official b10107 Windows HIP Radeon release:

```console
version: 10107 (c0bc8591e)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
```

Release asset:

```text
llama-b10107-bin-win-hip-radeon-x64.zip
SHA-256: B55E43C94C80C222DE5854DB32E6AC00E0F27CD6CBA1D41C04DE585AAB623014
```

I also reproduced the problem with b9637:

```console
version: 9637 (aedb2a5e9)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
```

## Operating Systems

Windows

```text
OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 64-bit, build 26200
GPU: AMD Radeon(TM) 860M Graphics
GPU PCI ID: 1002:1114
GPU architecture: gfx1152
Display driver: 32.0.22032.14003
CPU: AMD Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350 with Radeon 860M

HIP runtime loaded by llama.cpp:
C:\Windows\System32\amdhip64_7.dll

HIP runtime file version:
10.0.3661.0
```

## Affected Modules

* `llama-server`
* Official Windows HIP release artifact

## Command Line

Download the two GGUF files from the PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-GGUF repository and place them in the extracted b10107 directory:

```text
https://huggingface.co/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-GGUF
```

Run:

```powershell
.\llama-server.exe `
  -m .\PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-GGUF.gguf `
  --mmproj .\PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-GGUF-mmproj.gguf `
  --host 127.0.0.1 `
  --port 8112 `
  -ngl 99 `
  -c 4096 `
  -np 1 `
  --temp 0 `
  --log-colors off
```

No HTTP request is needed. With b10107, the process fails during model loading or warm-up.

## Problem Description and Steps to Reproduce

The official b10107 Windows HIP package loads the HIP runtime and detects the Radeon 860M, but the first GPU kernel launch fails with:

```console
ROCm error: invalid device function
```

The Radeon 860M is reported as `gfx1152`.

The Windows HIP release workflow for the exact b10107 commit configures the following GPU targets:

```text
gfx1150;gfx1151;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1102;gfx1030;gfx1031;gfx1032
```

`gfx1152` is absent from that list:

* [[b10107 Windows HIP target matrix](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/c0bc8591e/.github/workflows/release.yml#L1166-L1174)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/c0bc8591e/.github/workflows/release.yml#L1166-L1174)
* [The target list is passed to `GPU_TARGETS`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/c0bc8591e/.github/workflows/release.yml#L1241-L1248)

The manually triggered Windows HIP build workflow uses the same target list:

* [b10107 `build-cuda-windows.yml`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/c0bc8591e/.github/workflows/build-cuda-windows.yml#L691-L705)

The b9637 release workflow also omitted `gfx1152`:

* [[b9637 Windows HIP target matrix](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/aedb2a5e9/.github/workflows/release.yml#L1025-L1033)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/aedb2a5e9/.github/workflows/release.yml#L1025-L1033)

This appears separate from the source-level RDNA 3.5 classification:

* [[#24099](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24099)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24099) reported that `gfx1152` is RDNA 3.5.
* [[#24129](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24129)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24129) added `gfx1152` and `gfx1153` to the RDNA 3.5 source macro and was merged on 2026-06-08.
* Both b9637 and b10107 were released after that change, but their Windows HIP build target lists still omit `gfx1152`.

As an additional check, I inspected the b10107 `ggml-hip.dll`. It contains references to the targets listed above but not `gfx1152`.

The DLL inspected had SHA-256:

```text
6CC77B36B7EACB78703FB7872B55A1B2A8E51D1BCC12D5CD8CF13F8544D25E45
```

The official Windows CPU package loads the same model and serves requests on the same machine. The HIP package also detects the GPU and reports its available shared memory before the kernel failure.

This makes model-file corruption, failure to detect the GPU, and a generic `llama-server` configuration problem less likely.

## Expected Behavior

The official Windows HIP Radeon artifact should either:

1. include a code object compatible with `gfx1152`; or
2. clearly document that Radeon 860M / `gfx1152` is not supported by that artifact and provide the supported source-build configuration.

## Actual Behavior

`llama-server` exits during model initialization with:

```console
ROCm error: invalid device function
```

## First Bad Commit

Unknown.

I have confirmed that both b9637 and b10107 are affected, but I have not bisected older release artifacts.

## Relevant Log Output

```console
HIP Library Path: C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\amdhip64_7.dll
version: 10107 (c0bc8591e)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
HIP Library Path: C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\amdhip64_7.dll

0.00.698.647 I cmn  common_param: common_params_print_info: verbosity = 3

D:/a/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:106: ROCm error
```

<details>
<summary>Additional b9637 failures</summary>

One run failed during warm-up:

```console
I common_init_from_params: warming up the model with an empty run - please wait ...
D:/a/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:103: ROCm error

items.body:
### What happened

Commit `fa72aecc` (PR #26046) removed the rocWMMA FlashAttention kernel path. The replacement native `fattn-mma-f16` kernel is up to **2x slower for prompt processing at deep context** on RDNA4 (`gfx1201`). Decode (token generation) is unaffected or slightly faster.

### Environment

- **GPU:** AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (Navi 48, RDNA4, gfx1201), 32 GB VRAM
- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 7 7700 (8C/16T)
- **RAM:** 61 GB
- **ROCm:** 7.2.4
- **Model:** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Q4_K_M), f16 KV cache
- **Build flags:** `-DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1201 -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGGML_HIP_GRAPHS=ON -DGGML_HIP_NO_VMM=ON`

### Benchmark

`llama-bench -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q4_K_M.gguf -p 4096 -n 64 -d 0,16384,65536,126976 -ngl 99 -r 3`

Comparing `c588c4f` (last build with rocWMMA FA) vs `42fc2430` (current, native FA). VMM was explicitly disabled on both for a fair comparison.

| Test | `c588c4f` (rocWMMA FA) | `42fc2430` (native FA) | Delta |
|------|------------------------|------------------------|-------|
| pp4096 @ d0 | 2146.89 ± 9.90 t/s | 2036.09 ± 8.29 t/s | **-5.2%** |
| tg64 @ d0 | 68.50 ± 0.54 t/s | 68.42 ± 0.72 t/s | -0.1% |
| pp4096 @ d16384 | 1756.53 ± 4.93 t/s | 1313.27 ± 2.47 t/s | **-25.2%** |
| tg64 @ d16384 | 64.52 ± 0.32 t/s | 65.05 ± 0.31 t/s | +0.8% |
| pp4096 @ d65536 | 1121.33 ± 1.07 t/s | 645.32 ± 0.93 t/s | **-42.4%** |
| tg64 @ d65536 | 54.36 ± 0.24 t/s | 55.68 ± 0.27 t/s | +2.4% |
| pp4096 @ d126976 | **777.27 ± 0.15 t/s** | **394.81 ± 0.10 t/s** | **-49.2%** |
| tg64 @ d126976 | 45.40 ± 0.16 t/s | 47.19 ± 0.18 t/s | +3.9% |

The regression scales heavily with KV cache depth — at 127k context, prompt processing is **nearly 50% slower** (almost a 2x slowdown).

### Analysis

The native `fattn-mma-f16` kernel's tile shapes (`ncols1/ncols2`, `nbatch_fa`), LDS usage, and pipelining were likely tuned for CDNA / NVIDIA architectures. On RDNA4 with wave32 and the `V_WMMA_F32_16X16X16_F16` instruction, the native kernel appears to underutilize the matrix cores at deep context compared to the previous rocWMMA implementation.

Decode (`tg`) is slightly faster on the native kernel (+3.9% at depth), so the issue is specific to the prompt processing (prefill) path where the attention span is large.

### Workaround

I am keeping a frozen build at `c588c4f` (before the removal) for prefill-heavy workloads. This is not a long-term solution.

### Suggested investigation

- Profile both kernels with `rocprofv3` on gfx1201 to compare occupancy, VALU/WMMA utilization, and LDS pressure.
- The dispatch logic in `fattn.cu` may benefit from RDNA4-specific tile configurations.
- Entry points: `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-mma-f16.cuh`, `mma.cuh` (RDNA4 paths), dispatch in `fattn.cu`.

### Reproduction

```bash
# Build at the last rocWMMA commit
git checkout c588c4f
cmake -S . -B build-rocwmma \
  -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1201 \
  -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build-rocwmma -j8

# Build current (native FA)
git checkout master
cmake -S . -B build-native \
  -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1201 \
  -DGGML_HIP=ON \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build-native -j8

# Compare
for build in build-rocwmma build-native; do
  ./$build/bin/llama-bench \
    -m /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
    -p 4096 -n 64 -d 0,16384,65536,126976 -ngl 99 -r 3
done

## Summary

Under parallel mixed load (`-np 4 --kv-unified`), `llama-server` on an **integrated HIP GPU** (Strix Halo / gfx1151, 128 GB UMA) returns **complete responses that verbatim belong to a different, earlier request**. A large-prompt request receives, as its entire response, the literal answer text of a short request from an earlier round. We also observed a **chimeric** response fusing tokens of two different requests' expected outputs.

**Bisected to a single commit: c7d87229 "ggml-cuda : restore prop.integrated on HIP builds" (#24233).**

| build | result (validated responses, nonce-checked) |
|---|---|
| 505b1ed1 (parent window start) | clean — 0 violations / 168 |
| 5839ba35 (= parent of c7d87229) | clean — 0 / 36 |
| **c7d87229** | **cross-request replays: 3 hard / 36** |
| e8f19cc0 (window end) | cross-request replays: 7 hard + 1 chimera / 96 |

The same harness against **CPU builds** of both window endpoints shows no build-dependent difference (model-compliance noise only) — consistent with the culprit being the HIP integrated-memory path. This presumably explains why it went unnoticed: discrete GPUs are unaffected; it needs an **integrated** AMD GPU (`prop.integrated == 1`), multiple slots and concurrent mixed traffic.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), gfx1151, 128 GB unified memory, ROCm 7.14, Ubuntu 24.04
- Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++` (Release)
- Server: `llama-server -m <model> -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 4 --kv-unified --jinja --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE (Q4-class quant). First hit this in production behind LocalAI (same symptom after its vendored-llama.cpp bump crossed this commit); reproducing on vanilla `llama-server` rules the wrapper out.

## Reproduction

Load pattern per round (~30 s, script below): (B) short "repeat exactly this code: <nonce>" request → (C) large-prompt (~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce in the first line → (D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain). Every response is validated to contain its **own** nonce and no nonce of an **earlier** request.

On affected builds the round-N large-prompt request receives a literal foreign nonce as its complete response, typically from a round-(N−1) burst request. Verbatim from run logs at e8f19cc0:

```
R4/C got='pd-20260722-115649-3-d1'      (expected: reply echoing pc-...-4-c + a summary)
R5/C got='pd-20260722-115649-4-d2'
R6/C got='pd-20260722-115649-1-d1'
R7/C got='pd-20260722-115649-6-d1'
R8/C got='pd-20260722-115649-7-d1'
R3/C got='<!-- run:pc-20260722-115649-2-d0 -->'   <-- chimera: pc-...-2 stem fused with a -d0 burst suffix
```

In production we additionally observed: a poisoned slot re-serving its stored answer to unrelated requests **20+ minutes later** (the victim's `usage` then reports the foreign request's token counts), and occasional degeneration into repeated single characters (`/////...`).

items.body:
Implements #27553.

The integer-dot mmq path picks its large tile when both matmul dims exceed 64, which is every big GEMM in a dense-model prefill. On RDNA3 iGPUs (gfx1151-class, e.g. Radeon 8060S) the stock 128x128 tile at 256 threads underfills the shader cores at prefill shapes and re-reads the A weights once per 128-token slab; doubling only BN and the thread count keeps the per-thread register tiling identical while halving the A re-reads per token. No shader changes; `wg_denoms` kept in sync so dispatch and split-k see the real tile.

Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q5_K_XL-v2, RADV, `-fa 1 -b/-ub 2048`, same-binary stash A/B, r=5:

| test | stock | 128x256@512 | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| pp512 | 294.5 ±6.4 | 517.0 ±3.4 | 1.76x |
| pp4096 | 249.6 ±0.2 | 436.7 ±0.8 | 1.75x |
| pp16384 | 216.1 ±0.4 | 333.2 ±1.7 | 1.54x |
| tg128 | 10.76 | 10.82 | unchanged |

Also measured (r=3, pp4096): Q4_K_XL 465.1 ±0.8, Q6_K_XL 411.8 ±1.3 with the new tile.

Correctness and scope:
- Greedy outputs byte-identical (temp 0, diffed, `-n 120`).
- Decode and speculative-verify batches (n ≤ 64) select the small/medium tile and are structurally unaffected — verified with an MTP/DFlash2 spec-decode serving config: 28.7 t/s average decode at 64% draft acceptance, no regression vs baseline.
- Gated to `AMD RDNA3 && device->uma`; discrete GPUs, other vendors, and all `mul_mat_id` (MoE) tile families untouched.
- Neutral probes on this hardware: BM=256, 1024 threads, TM/TN/WMITER reshapings, wave32. The coopmat dequant family (iq4_xs path) measurably dislikes the doubled tile and stays stock.

## Overview

Fixes #27174.

This PR enables support for `echo=true` combined with `logprobs=N` in the `/v1/completions` endpoint without triggering memory assertions or KV cache errors. Previously, the server ignored the `echo` setting for logprobs, returning an empty list for prompt tokens and breaking downstream evaluation frameworks like `lm-eval`.

## Additional information

### Motivation
Evaluation frameworks like `lm-eval` grade a model by feeding it a specific correct answer as a prompt and adding up the logprobs for those prompt tokens to calculate a total score[cite: 1]. Because prompt scores were missing, `lm-eval` received blanks and assumed the model was randomly guessing[cite: 1]. Furthermore, naive attempts to fix this caused a `GGML_ASSERT(n_outputs_max <= cparams.n_outputs_max)` hard abort on large prompts due to buffer overflow.

### Changes
* **Dynamic Capacity Query**: Expose `llama_n_outputs_max` in the core API (`include/llama.h` and `src/llama-context.cpp`) to safely query runtime output capacity.
* **Main Loop Chunking**: Integrate chunked prompt logprob extraction directly into the main prompt processing loop in `tools/server/server-context.cpp`.
* **Memory and Cache Safety**: Bound prompt token ingestion per iteration by `llama_n_outputs_max(ctx_tgt)` when `need_prompt_logits()` is true. This prevents output buffer overflow (fixing the hard abort) and ensures the KV cache timeline advances consecutively (fixing sequence inconsistency errors).
* **Zero VRAM Bloat**: Extract logprobs within existing memory limits without requiring extra startup VRAM allocation.
* **OAI JSON Formatting**: Correctly populate `token_logprobs` and `top_logprobs` for the echoed prompt tokens, ensuring the first prompt token explicitly returns `null`.

## Requirements

- [x] I have read and agree with the contributing guidelines (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI to understand the code structure and data flow but wrote and fully understand the submitted logic myself.

**Co-author:** @simongonzalezdc

### Name and Version

`llama-server --version` → `version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10488, commit 9d77fa172)`, built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64 (the official `llama-b10488-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip`). I checked `common/chat.cpp` history through b10622: no gpt-oss/Harmony parser changes since b10488, so I believe this still reproduces on master.

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, driver 591.86, i7-13700K.

### Models

`ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF` → `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf` (sha256 `27cd6c432c7672cb812a92f611cf3ba7bbc35928262bb1e1253ff4ee6ae35901`, verified against HF LFS).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

gpt-oss-20b at the OpenAI-recommended sampling (`--temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0`; server-default top_k 40 / min_p 0.05) occasionally emits a **malformed Harmony channel header** at the start of a turn: after `<|channel|>` it produces free text, `??`, `commentary 2?`, `commentary?commentary?`, or a doubled `<|channel|>commentary to=assistant<|channel|>commentary?...` — and only then (sometimes) the well-formed `<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>...`.

`common_chat_params_init_gpt_oss` tolerates exactly one variant of this — the `stray_commentary` arm from #21286 (`<|channel|>commentary` + optional ` to=assistant`, followed immediately by a well-formed channel). Everything else fails the final PEG parse, `common_chat_peg_parse` logs `unparsed peg-native output`, and the server returns an error mid-stream: **"The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format"**. The rest of the turn — usually a perfectly good `analysis` block and a valid tool call — is discarded.

Observed rate on a production Home Assistant voice assistant (tool-calling, ~13k-token prompt, `--jinja`, reasoning_effort medium via `LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS={"reasoning_effort":"medium"}`): **3 of 72 turns** over ~48 h, 6 more in the two days before — 9 distinct garblings, listed in full below. Every one is a hard failure to the client even though the model's actual content after the bad header is intact.

Launch flags:
```
llama-server.exe --model gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf --alias qwen3.5-9b --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 -ngl 99 -c 24576 --jinja --parallel 1 -fa on --cache-reuse 256 -ub 2048 -b 2048 --metrics --no-webui --temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0
```

Steps to reproduce: run a long tool-calling conversation at temp 1.0 with the stock gpt-oss chat template and a tools array (ours is ~24 function tools); roughly 1 turn in 25 trips it. I can't force it deterministically — it is a sampling event — but the raw outputs below are exactly what the parser received.

Suggested handling (either would fix every case below): treat any `<|channel|>` prefix that is not a recognised channel name as stray text and resume at the next `<|start|>assistant<|channel|>` / `<|channel|>analysis|final|commentary<|message|>`; or, when the final parse fails but a lenient re-parse succeeds, return the lenient result instead of erroring (the lenient path already exists for `is_partial=true`). Happy to test a branch — this rig produces a hit within an hour or two of normal use.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown — the stray-header tolerance in #21286 (Apr 2026) covers one shape; these are the others. Present at b10488; no relevant parser commits since.

### Relevant log output

Nine distinct `unparsed peg-native output` lines (truncated to the header + first sentence; the trailing content in each was a normal analysis block and, where applicable, a valid `to=functions.*` tool call). Timestamps are seconds since server start.

```
10.01 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary to=assistant<|channel|>commentary?commentary=short?comment?…???<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to answer: "What causes the porch light to come on at night?" ...
346.05 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>We need to answer: Is the sump pump something I should worry about tonight? We must consider safety. ...
2750.27 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary to=assistant ...commentary?<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>The user: "ask the expert whether we should replace the roof this fall or wait until spring." ...
177.21 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary... The user asks: did the Cubs win yesterday? The sports scores result includes many games ...
177.38 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary 2? The request "turn on the light" ambiguous. We have to ask clarifying question ...
179.42 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary?commentary?We need temperature difference. Also need outside temperature. Get outdoor temperature.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>Need GetLiveContext for Outdoor Temperature.<|end|
182.48 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary says tool returned, so now respond.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>User asked: "is there a tornado risk tonight"
185.23 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>...?We need answer. The user: "did the Cubs win yesterday". It's 2026-08-21? Actually current date is 2026-08-22. ...
1.06 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>??<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We must comply with the gating rules. Input: "should I seal the driveway this weekend" ...
```

Client-side symptom (Home Assistant `llama_cpp` integration via the `openai` Python client): `openai.APIError: The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format`, raised from the SSE stream.

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-bench --version
version: b10470 (34af94cd9ab277632e27caeec2d41de2fd091b31)
built with Apple clang for arm64-apple-darwin25.6.0, -DGGML_METAL=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON
```

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core), llama-server, llama-bench, RPC backend, Metal backend

### Command line

Two Apple M4 machines, 16 GB unified memory each, connected by a Thunderbolt bridge.
Machine A is the main node, machine B runs the RPC worker.

```shell
# machine B (RPC worker)
ggml-rpc-server -H 192.168.2.1 -p 50052 -d MTL0

# machine A (main node) -- FAILS
llama-bench -m Qwen_Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS.gguf \
  --rpc 192.168.2.1:50052 -ts 0.50/0.50 -fa on -b 1024 -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128

# machine A -- IDENTICAL except for -mmp 0 -- WORKS
llama-bench -m Qwen_Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS.gguf \
  --rpc 192.168.2.1:50052 -ts 0.50/0.50 -fa on -b 1024 -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128 -mmp 0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a model is sharded across an RPC device, the main node appears to retain the entire
model in memory rather than only its own share. The effective size limit for a distributed
model therefore stays roughly equal to what a **single** node can hold, which defeats the
purpose of splitting it.

Disabling mmap (`-mmp 0`, or `--load-mode none` on `llama-server`) fixes it completely, with
no other change.

Model used: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS`, 15,761,446,528 bytes (14.68 GiB).
Metal `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize` is 13,958.64 MB on the main node and 12,713.12 MB on
the worker, so 14.68 GiB fits on neither alone but fits easily across both.

**A/B, one variable:**

| flags | result |
| --- | --- |
| default load mode | fails, `llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3` |
| `-mmp 1` (explicit) | fails, same error |
| `-mmp 0` | works: 322.75 t/s prompt, 26.12 t/s decode |

**Measured during a failing run**, sampling resident memory on both machines at the same
moment:

- main node `llama-bench` RSS: **12.15 GiB**
- RPC worker `ggml-rpc-server` RSS: **7.57 GiB**
- total resident across both: **19.7 GiB, for a 14.68 GiB model**

The worker really does receive its shard, and the main node keeps a full copy anyway.

The OOM is on the main node's local Metal device (`MTL0`), and compute buffers are far too
small to explain it:

```
sched_reserve: RPC0[192.168.2.1:50052] compute buffer size =    70.02 MiB
sched_reserve:       MTL0 compute buffer size =   493.52 MiB
sched_reserve:        CPU compute buffer size =     8.52 MiB
```

**Threshold behaviour**, all with the same two machines and default load mode:

| model | size | result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 | 11.28 GiB | works, splits correctly (5.68 GiB on the worker) |
| GLM-4.7-Flash IQ4_XS | 15.13 GiB | fails |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B IQ3_XXS | 14.68 GiB | fails |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M | 20.76 GiB | fails |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B Q3_K_S | 20.11 GiB | fails |

Everything at or below about 12 GiB works. Everything above fails. That threshold matches
the main node's own Metal working set, not the combined capacity of the two machines. With
`-mmp 0` every one of the failing models above loads and runs correctly across the split.

**Hypothesis, offered tentatively.** Metal on this build reports `use residency sets = true`
at init. If the mmapped model pages are placed in a residency set on the main node, the OS
cannot evict them, so sharding weights to the RPC device never releases the main node's
mapping. I have not read the allocator closely enough to confirm this, and the mechanism may
be different. The observation and the `-mmp 0` workaround are what I am confident about.

**Why this is easy to miss.** The failure does not look like an out of memory error from the
client side. `llama-bench` reports `failed to decode prompt batch, res = -3` and
`llama-server` reports a generic decode failure, so it reads as a model or architecture
problem rather than a memory one. I spent several hours attributing it to specific model
architectures (and wrongly concluded that three separate models were unsupported) before
finding that one flag fixed all of them.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. Observed on b10470 (`34af94c`). I do not know whether earlier versions behave
differently, and I have not tested current master.

### Relevant log output

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
test_prompt: failed to decode prompt batch, res = -3
llama_bench: error: failed to run prompt
```

## Overview This PR improves routed MoE prefill performance on RDNA3 by changing how llama.cpp chooses MMQ N-tile sizes. Instead of using the worst case expert width, it estimates the typical routed expert width and uses that when it is smaller than the RDNA3 maximum tile width. The launch grid still uses the original worst case width, so output coverage and correctness are preserved. The change is limited to host side tile selection in `mul_mat_q_case` and does not modify structs, call sites, launch parameters, or device kernels. Benchmarks on a Radeon Pro W7800/gfx1100 with ROCm 7.2.3 show large prefill gains in many routed MoE cases, while decode and non RDNA3 architectures are mostly unchanged. If maintainers or other contributors have access to NVIDIA, CDNA, RDNA2, or RDNA4 hardware, the natural follow up would be to test the same routed width picker under the corresponding MMQ/launch policy and enable it per architecture where it is beneficial. ## Benchmark Summary Hardware/software: - AMD Radeon Pro W7800, gfx1100 / RDNA3 - ROCm 7.2.3 - HIP backend, `-ngl 99` - `GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON` - `-fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv f16 -sm none -t 4 --poll 0 -r 5` The improvement depends on the physical ubatch/chunk width that reaches routed MoE MMQ, not total context length: ```text win when: ncols_typical < mmq_x_max crossover_ubatch: 128 * n_experts / n_expert_used ``` So long prompts can still benefit when they are processed in smaller ubatch chunks.
Benchmark sweep | model / quant | experts | ubatch | pp512 | pp1024 | pp2048 | pp4096 | pp8192 | tg128 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K | 256 | 2048 | +48.46% | +22.15% | +7.57% | n/a | n/a | -0.67% | | Qwen3-30B-A3B Q6_K | 128 | 512 | +35.50% | +33.79% | +32.15% | n/a | n/a | -1.11% | | Qwen3-30B-A3B Q6_K | 128 | 2048 | +36.62% | +13.90% | -0.75% | n/a | n/a | -0.89% | | Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M | 128 | 512 | +33.68% | +31.54% | +29.81% | +27.70% | +23.86% | +0.35% | | Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M | 128 | 2048 | +33.77% | +14.00% | -0.08% | -0.06% | -0.01% | -0.20% | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q3_K_M | 256 | 512 | +23.48% | +22.37% | +22.73% | +22.91% | +21.18% | -0.08% | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q3_K_M | 256 | 2048 | +22.93% | +6.99% | +4.02% | +3.92% | +3.69% | +0.15% | | Gemma-4-26B-A4B Q4_K_M | 128 | 512 | +29.53% | +28.52% | +26.65% | +25.46% | +23.19% | +0.04% | | Gemma-4-26B-A4B Q4_K_M | 128 | 2048 | +29.87% | +13.16% | +0.03% | +0.05% | +0.04% | -0.09% | | Gemma-4-26B-A4B Q6_K | 128 | 512 | +25.05% | +24.05% | +23.21% | +22.51% | +20.59% | +0.08% | | Gemma-4-26B-A4B Q6_K | 128 | 2048 | +25.53% | +11.75% | +0.11% | -0.04% | -0.00% | +0.50% | The 128 expert models show the expected crossover behavior at ubatch 2048: `pp2048` and larger are neutral because the typical width has reached `mmq_x_max = 128`. ## Overview

This adds an optional CUTLASS path for block-scaled dense GEMMs on SM120 and SM121.

NVFP4 and MXFP4 weights are repacked when loaded. Prefill uses the CUTLASS W4A4 kernel, while M=1 NVFP4 decode uses MMVQ with the repacked layout. Unsupported cases keep using the existing CUDA path.

### CUTLASS weight repacking



Existing GGUF files are loaded unchanged. When a supported dense MXFP4/NVFP4 tensor is uploaded, its FP4 values are packed row by row with K padding. The scales are stored in two layouts: a 128-row tiled layout for the SM120 CUTLASS kernel and a row-major layout for small-batch decode. Prefill and decode share the FP4 values, so only the scales are duplicated. Unsupported tensors remain in the normal CUDA buffer.


## Results

### Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4

Tested on one Pro 6000 using Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4. 

| Test | Native | Repacked | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| pp512 | 4,677.41 tok/s | 5,275.83 tok/s | +12.79% |
| pp2048 | 4,731.96 tok/s | 5,298.54 tok/s | +11.97% |
| pp8192 | 4,549.87 tok/s | 5,067.73 tok/s | +11.38% |
| tg128 | 51.7937 tok/s | 52.2284 tok/s | +0.84% |

All 10 repacked backend test cases passed.

### Qwen3.6-27B MXFP4

Tested on an Pro 6000 with the same binary.

#### Prefill

| Test | Native | CUTLASS | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| pp512 | 5,269.90 tok/s | 5,717.95 tok/s | +8.50% |
| pp2048 | 5,520.01 tok/s | 6,251.92 tok/s | +13.26% |
| pp8192 | 4,975.71 tok/s | 5,431.93 tok/s | +9.17% |

#### Decode

| Test | Native | Repacked | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| tg128 | 80.956 tok/s | 81.884 tok/s | +1.15% |

Prefill uses the cutlass path, while m=1 decode uses the repacked reader. all 12 mxfp4/nvfp4 backend correctness tests passed.

## Build

The path is disabled by default and requires CUDA 12.9 or newer.

```bash
cmake -B build \
    -DGGML_CUDA=ON \
    -DGGML_CUDA_CUTLASS=ON

cmake --build build --config Release -j
```

CUTLASS is fetched automatically by CMake at a pinned revision. An existing checkout can be used with `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_CUTLASS`.

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR has comprehensive decode-side optimizations on K-quant dense models for Adreno GPUs, including optimization for skinny GEMM that are essential for speculative decoding and MTP (multi-token prediction):
- A tiled lm_head/embed GEMV layout.
- A cooperative-K medium-batch q4_K/q6_K GEMM to lower register pressure
- A multi-row f16 decode GEMV (attention projections + lm_head) 
- A q4_K MUL_MAT+GLU decode fusion. 
- Every default is gated on measured, per-device data, and each piece has an env override.

Fleet defaults vs upstream, Adreno 840 (A8X), Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M:

| | delta | pairs | order bias |
|---|---|---|---|
| **tg128** | **+16.99%** (16.91 vs 14.45 t/s) | 4/4 | +0.03% |
| pp512 | −0.00% (neutral) | 3/4 | +0.01% |

Per switch, against the route each replaces:

| switch | A8X (840) | X2E (X2-90) |
|---|---|---|
| tiled lm_head/embed GEMV | **+11.9%** tg128 (6/6 pairs) | **+6.9%** tg128 (4/4 pairs) |
| cooperative-K medium-batch GEMM | — | **+85.8 / +84.4 / +83.6%** at pp2 / pp4 / pp8 (12/12) |

Note the wins live in the decode GEMV and the medium-batch GEMM, not long prefill. 
- This is a **K-quant dense-decode** win
- MXFP4/MoE models and Q8_0 builds are structurally untouched.

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

## Additional information
 
<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

**Gating:**

- The tiled defaults are on for X2E and A8X specifically; 
- The A7X regresses on the tiled layout and is excluded. Env forces either way.
- The q4_K split-K GEMV is X2E-only: 
  - ungated it measured 840 −1.3% / 850 −20.0%. 
  - With the gate,  both parts keep their existing path.
- The flat-GEMV large-m escape stays opt-in
  - it is slower than the multi-quad route that now covers the same long-vocab shapes (A8X -10.3%, X2E -3.7%).
  - This supersedes the routing added in #26427 rather than disabling it. 
  - With the escape off, a vocab-scale K-quant lm_head is not sent back to the old `gemv_noshuffle` path: it lands on the multi-quad GEMV, which is default-on with no device gate (`ne01 % 4 == 0`, `ne01 >= 32768`).
  - The `ne01 % 128` correctness escape is independent of the opt-in and still fires first.

**Correctness ordering.** 
- The `ne01 % 128` escape guards a layout bug, not a performance choice:
   - the noshuffle layout packs two rows per 32-bit texel and the GEMV reads it with a `ne01/2` texel stride under an exact-cover dispatch with no store guard, so `ne01 % 128 != 0` misaligns every odd column and writes past the end of `dst`. 
   - It now precedes the opt-in gate, so it stays reachable in the default configuration. 
   - Order is: tiled deferral, correctness escape, opt-in, size heuristics.

**Which models see the gain.** 

Gated on a q4_K/q6_K lm_head/embed (tiled additionally needs vocab ≥ 32768, ne00 ≥ 512, and for q6_K vocab % 128 == 0; the cooperative-K GEMM needs a q4_K GEMM at n_q ∈ [2..8]). 

Scanned over a 108-GGUF local model set: **65 eligible, 43 not.**
- *Benefits:* 
  - Q4_0/Q4_K_M quants of Qwen3 (1.7B/4B), Qwen3.5-4B (incl. MTP), 
  - gemma-4  (E2B/E4B/12b/26B-A4B), gemma-3n-E4B, 
  - Llama-3/3.2, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen — the mainstream dense-decode set.
- *Does not benefit:*
  - every `-Q8_0` build (24 — the lm_head stays Q8_0); 
  - F16/BF16/Q4_0/F32  lm_heads (7, including **both gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 builds — gpt-oss gets none of this**, it contains zero q4_K/q6_K tensors); 
  - q6_K vocab not a multiple of 128 (6, e.g. gemma-3-4b at  262208); 
  - vocab < 32768 (3); ne00 < 512 (2).  

**Intel NEO GPU** 
- The rms+rope fusion precondition also fixed a previously-undetected garbage path on Intel NEO: `RMS_NORM_MUL_ROPE` 8/72 → 72/72. 
- This is not an Adreno-only cleanup.

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR widens kernel selection to the shapes that were falling through, speeds up the cluster
kernel, and moves gemma-4's DK=512 decode onto the GPU via FA on. Massive gains on TG are observed:
a number of models now run faster with FA on than off.

### Issues
The Adreno decode flash-attention path selected its multi-query (MQ) and cluster kernels for a narrow set of shapes; everything else fell back to the `q1`/`q1_split` kernels. Those fallbacks are bad in two specific ways:
- **Register pressure.** `flash_attn_f32_f16_q1_split` reports 1168 bytes of private memory per work item (the q8_0 twin 1664, the DV=512 `q1` 2048) against the ~512-byte budget where this compiler stops spilling; their workgroup cap drops to 192.
- **Redundant traffic.** They run one workgroup per *query* head, so every head in a GQA group re-reads the same K and V rows. The MQ kernels read each row once per KV head.

### Solutions
**Commit 1 - coverage and cluster performance.**
- Adds `MQ_GQA=2/3` programs at head_dim 128, an `MQ_GQA=8`/`FA_CL_C=16` cluster at head_dim 64 (the stock GQA=8 width fails the `DK_VEC % FA_CL_C` check there), and the same cluster for q8_0 KV, which previously had no MQ route at all. - Four performance changes follow:
  -  pooling the flash-decoding partials buffer (it was a `clCreateBuffer` per attention layer per token);
  -  folding the per-head cluster reductions into one halving butterfly (32 `sub_group_shuffle_xor` per KV row down to 15, bit-identical)
  - a head split that runs an `MQ_GQA = gqa/N` program on N workgroups per KV head.
  - a 64-thread workgroup for it.

**Commit 2 - gemma-4 DK=512 decode.**
- gemma-4 interleaves DK=256 sliding-window layers with DK=512 global ones. `supports_op` declined FLASH_ATTN_EXT for DK=512 at decode, so every global layer became a CPU island: 17 graph splits against 3, with that layer's K and V views (8.4 MB each at n_kv=4096) copied device-to-host every token.
- Declining was nevertheless the better trade, because the only DK=512 decode kernel was the 2 KB/work-item `q1` - forcing that back onto the GPU measures 27% *slower* than paying for the CPU islands.

The shared DK=512 program is built `-D FA_DECODE_MINIMAL` (dropping `q1_vec`) to stay under the shader compiler's host-memory ceiling, so that spilled fallback was all those layers had. Two new single-kernel programs fix that, the way `FA_PREFILL_ONLY` already isolates the BM tile:
- `FA_VEC_ONLY` builds `q1_vec` alone (2 KB -> 192 B per work item) and `FA_MQ_SPLIT_ONLY` builds`q1_vec_mq_split` alone. The same narrow build also serves DK=256 GQA=8, whose stock kernel requests a 192-thread workgroup that the X2-90 refuses per-kernel - it registered as compiled and then never dispatched.
- These shapes carry their own `n_kv` floor, since gemma-4's window caps n_kv at 1024/256, below the split-tuned `FD_MIN_N_KV`; the floor is scoped to shapes that have a narrow kernel, so no other model's decode routing changes.

### Results

tg32 at depth 4096 against the same tree with the new paths disabled, as base/patched/patched/base
sequences with a clock proxy sampled per arm.

| model | shape | X2-90 | X1-85 | Adreno 840 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 | dk 64, GQA 8 | +7.7% (+19.8% at d16384) | - | +8.3% |
| Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M | dk 128, GQA 4 | +4.8% (+5.9% at d16384) | +18.0% | +61% |
| Llama-3-8B Q4_0 | dk 128, GQA 4 | +3.2% | - | +42% |
| Mistral-7B v0.3 Q4_K_M | dk 128, GQA 4 | - | - | +33% |
| gemma-4 E4B Q4_0 | dk 512 + dk 256 | +44.5% (+59.6% at d8192) | +21…37% | +34…36% |
| gemma-4 E2B Q4_0 | dk 512 + dk 256 | +53.9% (+60.1% at d8192) | +17…45% | +96% |

Two notes:

- On the Adreno 840, GQA=4 at head_dim 128 previously ran *slower* with flash attention than
  without.
   - FA-on now beats FA-off by 9-13% on all three GQA=4 models there, so the "use `-fa 0` on  this device" workaround is no longer needed for that shape.
   - GQA=3 still trails FA-off by ~10% and is not addressed here.
- On gemma-4, `-fa auto` previously resolved to **disabled**, because the DK=512 decline fired at the `n_q == 1` probe shape. It now resolves to **enabled**. Users who never passed `-fa` will see this change.

## Additional shapes and kernel improvements

Four further gaps in the same routing table, added after the first review pass.

### Head size 128: the head split, and an `n_kv` floor of its own

**The head-split program was never built at head size 128.** It was fenced to head size 64, and the
narrow multi-query builder to head sizes 256 and 512, so a GQA-8 shape at 128 — Qwen3-30B-A3B's
decode shape — had no head-split form to route to and ran one work-group per KV head. Building it
there is worth, per-op on `test-backend-ops` at KV 4096 and 8192 with the split off then on:
+49.9% / +51.8% on an Adreno X2-90, +82.1% / +55.3% on an Adreno 840, and +112.4% / +119.3% on an
X1-85. Three generations, no inversion. End to end on Qwen3-30B-A3B that is +23.5% and +28.8% tg at
4096 and 8192 tokens of depth.

**The multi-query routes inherited the flash-decoding split's `n_kv` floor**, which answers a
different question — whether splitting the KV range across work-groups pays — and at 2048 it meant
the MQ routes did not engage at all below that length. Giving them their own floor at 32 gains, at
depth 0 and 1024: +12% / +63% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, +10% / +43% on Qwen3-4B, +1% / +8% on gpt-oss-20b,
and neutral on gemma-4-26B. Depth 4096 is flat everywhere, which is the control — above the old
floor the routing does not change, and it does not move.

`FLASH_ATTN_EXT` in `test-backend-ops`: 5117 and 2696 cases OK, 0 FAIL, unchanged from the
unpatched baseline build on the same device.

### GQA ratio 16

gemma-4-12B has 16 query heads over a single KV head on its 8 global-attention layers, i.e.
DK=DV=512 at GQA ratio 16. The narrow multi-query decode gate admits ratios 4, 8 and 2, so that

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Issues: 
- The gpt-oss MoE FFN applies its three per-expert biases as three separate `ADD_ID` ops. 
- Each is an **in-place** read-modify-write of a `[n_ff, n_expert_used, n_tokens]` f32 tensor - 23.6 MB read and 23.6 MB written per layer to perform one add per element
- In every case the very next operation reads that same memory again.

This optimization folds them into the ops that already read the tensor:
- **gate and up biases** are folded into `swiglu_oai`, in a new kernel  `kernel_add_id_add_id_swiglu_oai`  `kernels/moe_add_id_glu.cl`). Six passes over the tensor become two reads and one write.
- **the down bias** is folded into the MoE combine, via a sibling kernel `kernel_moe_combine_bias_f32` so the existing unfused combine is left untouched.

Both matmuls keep their own dispatches. Only the epilogue collapses, so the change is independent of the expert weight type and does not touch the vendor GEMM.

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->
Adreno X2-90, `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-q8attn.gguf`, `-fa 1 -ngl 99`, f16 KV, with Adreno binary (QPM) kernels, matched pairs with alternating lead:

| test | before | after | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| pp512 | 683.93 / 683.73 | 706.89 / 707.82 | **+3.36% / +3.52%** |
| pp2048 | 626.52 / 624.84 | 645.26 / 645.30 | **+2.99% / +3.27%** |
| tg32 | 37.69 / 37.64 | 37.91 / 37.71 | +0.58% / +0.19% |

Adreno 840, `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf`: **+1.08%** (gate/up fold) and **+0.54%** (down fold), each the mean of 4 matched pairs with every pair agreeing in sign.

Per-fusion attribution, measured by toggling the opt-outs on one binary: gate/up fold **+2.25%**, down fold **+1.26%**. Control with both disabled returns to baseline at **-0.24%**.

Verified **not** to fire on gemma-4-26B-A4B, which has no per-expert biases and fuses gate and up into a single `ffn_gate_up_exps` tensor: measured +0.12% / +0.19%, i.e. noise. Models outside the pattern decline cleanly and are unaffected.

### Correctness

Output is byte-identical to the unfused path for each fusion independently.
