### Name and Version

version: b10349 (62bf73d25, includes the #26841 merge)
Built from source (CUDA, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86;120`) in a local Docker image.
Hardware: RTX 3090 + RTX 5060 Ti.

### Operating systems

Linux (Docker container on a Windows host)

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Models

- **Target (FAILS):** [meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF) → `muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-dynamic.gguf`
- **Draft:** same repo → `dflash-kquant.gguf`
- **Target (WORKS):** [unsloth/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF) with the exact same drafter

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Binding the DFlash drafter (`--spec-type draft-dflash`) crashes at load time when the **target** GGUF encodes `muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window_pattern` as an **array**, which is how the model creator's own official GGUF (`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF`) encodes it:

```
llama-server -m muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-dynamic.gguf \
    -md dflash-kquant.gguf --spec-type draft-dflash -fa on --jinja
```

crashes with:

```
vector::_M_range_check: __n (which is 1) >= this->size() (which is 1)
```

The exact same drafter file binds and runs fine when the target is the unsloth conversion of the same model, whose `muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window_pattern` is encoded as a **scalar** (`UINT32 = 4`).

Both target GGUFs load and generate fine **without** the drafter — `src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp` accepts both encodings (scalar period → `set_swa_pattern()`, array → per-layer `is_swa_impl`). The crash only happens on the DFlash bind path, which inherits the target's config and apparently only handles the scalar form. Note the irony: the model creator's official GGUF is the one that cannot bind the official drafter shipped in the same repo, while a third-party conversion can.

**Validated workaround:** copying the target GGUF with gguf-py `copy_with_new_metadata`, rewriting `muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window_pattern` to scalar `UINT32 = 4`. With that single metadata change the drafter binds and runs (~137 t/s on the RTX 3090).

**Suggested fix:** when the DFlash path inherits the target's config, accept both encodings of `<arch>.attention.sliding_window_pattern`, mirroring what `src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp` already does at target load. Possibly related: the scalar overload `llama_model_loader::get_key_or_arr(enum llm_kv, uint32_t &, bool)` in `src/llama-model-loader.cpp` returns `false` (non-required) or throws when the key is an array, so any call site expecting a scalar silently takes the wrong branch on array-encoded GGUFs.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected — observed on b10349 (62bf73d25). Possibly present since the DFlash path landed.

### Relevant log output

```
vector::_M_range_check: __n (which is 1) >= this->size() (which is 1)
```

items.body:
`common_speculative_init_result` computes the draft model path, logs it, and then passes the **target** model path to `llama_model_load_from_file`:

```cpp
model_path = params.speculative.draft.mparams.path;
LOG_INF("%s: loading draft model '%s'\n", __func__, model_path.c_str());

llama_model * model_dft = llama_model_load_from_file(params.model.path.c_str(), mparams);
```

So with `-md <draft.gguf> --spec-type draft-dflash` (or any draft-based spec type routed through this init), the target model is silently loaded a second time as the "draft". Depending on available memory this either:

- fails draft context creation and **silently disables speculative decoding** (generation proceeds at baseline speed with no indication beyond a fitting-time warning), or
- doubles the target model's memory footprint.

The log line above makes it look like the correct file was loaded, which makes the no-op hard to notice — we only caught it because with/without `-md` benchmarked identically.

## Fix

Load the draft path that was computed on the line above (one line).

## Validation

Muse-Glimmer-30B-UD-Q3_K_XL + `dflash-kquant.gguf` (unsloth GGUFs), Apple M5 24 GB, Metal backend, `llama-server --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15`:

| | draft_n / draft_accepted | generation |
|---|---|---|
| before | absent (spec silently off); t/s identical with and without `-md` | 3.5–5 t/s |
| after | e.g. 2067 / 461 (chat, 22%) up to 735 / 548 (code continuation, 75%) | up to 19.5 t/s on high-acceptance workloads |

Acceptance-rate range is workload-dependent as expected for a block drafter; the point of the table is that draft stats exist at all and the speedup appears only after the fix.

items.body:
## Describe the bug

A significant performance regression occurs between builds b10356 and b10359/b10360/b10369 on RTX 5080 (Blackwell, compute capability 12.0). The regression affects both prompt processing and generation speed, and appears to worsen with each new build.

## Environment

- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 5080 (16GB, Blackwell, compute capability 12.0)
- **Driver:** 610.62, CUDA 13.3
- **OS:** Windows 11 x64
- **Model:** Muse-Glimmer-30B-UD-IQ2_M.gguf (11.4 GB, IQ2_M quantization, `muse-glimmer` architecture)
- **Draft model:** dflash-kquant.gguf (DFlash speculative decoding)

## Full build comparison (4 builds tested)

| Build | Prompt processing | Generation (peak) | Generation (avg) | DFlash mean len |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **b10356** (best) | 1029-1271 tok/s ✅ | 62 tok/s | ~53 tok/s | 2.3-3.5 |
| b10359 | 834 tok/s ❌ (−34%) | 37 tok/s ❌ (−40%) | ~32 tok/s | 2.2-3.0 |
| b10360 | 740-914 tok/s ❌ (−30%) | 83 tok/s ✅ (+34%) | ~68 tok/s | 2.4-3.7 |
| **b10369** (worst) | 413-534 tok/s ❌❌ (−60%) | 49 tok/s ❌ | ~38 tok/s | 2.2-3.5 |

**Key finding:** The regression is getting **worse with each build**. b10369 is the worst of all four — prompt processing dropped to 413 tok/s on the first task (vs 1029 on b10356), a **−60% regression**.

## Reproduction

```bash
llama-server \
  -m Muse-Glimmer-30B-UD-IQ2_M.gguf \
  -ngl all -c 60000 -np 1 \
  -fa on --kv-unified \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 2048 \
  --spec-type draft-dflash \
  --spec-draft-model dflash-kquant.gguf \
  --spec-draft-p-min 0.2 --spec-draft-n-max 3 \
  --jinja --no-ui
```

All builds are official prebuilt `llama-bXXXX-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip` (Clang 20.1.8).

## Sample timings

### b10356 (best — baseline)

```
prompt eval time = 5387 ms / 6195 tokens → 1149 tok/s
eval time = 6655 ms / 365 tokens → 54.8 tok/s
draft acceptance = 0.694, mean len = 3.08
```

### b10359 (regression — both metrics slower)

```
prompt eval time = 38292 ms / 31965 tokens → 834 tok/s  (−27%)
eval time = 2109 ms / 78 tokens → 36.9 tok/s  (−33%)
draft acceptance = 0.693 (identical → regression is NOT in speculative decoding)
```

### b10360 (mixed — generation improved, prefill worse)

```
prompt eval time = 1599 ms / 1385 tokens → 865 tok/s  (−25%)
eval time = 14026 ms / 1166 tokens → 83.1 tok/s  (+51%)
draft acceptance = 0.879, mean len = 3.63
```

### b10369 (worst — severe prefill regression)

```
prompt eval time = 14999 ms / 6198 tokens → 413 tok/s  (−64% vs b10356)
eval time = 2068 ms / 86 tokens → 41.6 tok/s  (−24%)
draft acceptance = 0.667, mean len = 3.00
```

Later tasks in same session:
```
prompt eval time = 22368 ms / 11953 tokens → 534 tok/s  (still degraded)
eval time = 23841 ms / 792 tokens → 33.2 tok/s
draft acceptance = 0.440, mean len = 2.29
```

## Analysis

Two separate regressions identified:

### 1. Prefill/prompt processing regression (affects b10359, b10360, b10369 — getting worse)

Prompt processing speed has degraded progressively:
- b10356: ~1200 tok/s
- b10359: ~834 tok/s (−30%)
- b10360: ~830 tok/s (−30%)
- b10369: **~470 tok/s (−60%)** ← severe

This suggests a **compounding issue** in the prefill kernels for Blackwell (sm_120). Each build makes it slightly worse.

### 2. DFlash mean acceptance length is low on stock builds

DFlash mean acceptance length is consistently 2.2-3.7 across all official builds. Community members report that **custom Blackwell-optimized builds** achieve mean acceptance lengths of 6-8 (peak 14.4), which would roughly **double or triple** the generation speed.

This suggests the stock CUDA kernels for Blackwell are not optimized for the DFlash verification path, limiting speculative decoding efficiency.

## Impact

For agentic workloads with large prompts (20-60k tokens common in code review and agent loops):
- b10356 is the only usable build (~1200 tok/s prefill)
- b10369 is nearly unusable (413 tok/s on first task — a 60k token prompt would take 145s just for prefill)

**Workaround:** Reverting to b10356 restores acceptable performance, but this is not sustainable as newer builds contain important bugfixes and model architecture support.

## Additional context

- The regression appears specific to **Blackwell (sm_120)** — consistent across multiple sessions and workloads
- Both batch_size (2048) and ubatch_size (2048) are used
- The model uses GQA (32 query heads / 8 KV heads, 16:1 ratio)
- Related issue: #26873 (mmproj loading causes persistent performance degradation on Muse Glimmer)
- The `muse-glimmer` architecture support was added in PR #26841 (merged between b10344 and b10356)

## Overview

This changes how experts are chunked and queued into the llama-quantize process

This does **NOT** speed up running models, so don't get excited.. But MoE model creation speed does go up by a good margin with identical sha256sum

In ideal scenarios, we can see a 5x speedup in creation time for the particularly tricky tensor types when using 192 threads on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B:

| type | master (s) | PR (s) | difference |

| IQ3_S | 578.11 | 126.46 | -451.65 (-78.1%) |

| Q3_K_M | 200.14 | 56.10 | -144.04 (-72.0%) |
| Q3_K_L | 203.06 | 56.79 | -146.27 (-72.0%) |
| IQ4_NL | 372.72 | 96.15 | -276.57 (-74.2%) |
| IQ4_XS | 370.21 | 94.87 | -275.34 (-74.4%) |
| Q4_K_S | 268.32 | 76.46 | -191.86 (-71.5%) |
| Q4_K_M | 250.21 | 72.93 | -177.28 (-70.9%) |
| Q5_K_S | 275.51 | 80.41 | -195.10 (-70.8%) |
| Q5_K_M | 256.68 | 75.99 | -180.69 (-70.4%) |
| Q6_K | 162.85 | 53.28 | -109.57 (-67.3%) |
| Q8_0 | 156.70 | 52.10 | -104.60 (-66.8%) |

At 48 threads on 24 cores the numbers are more modest, somewhere more like 1.5-2x increase

CPU usage goes from ~60-80% on each provided core to 100%

## Additional information

The main change is that we no longer spin up a single thread per-expert, now it handles the whole 3D tensor in one threaded pass

`this_nrow = min(nrows - local_row, nrows_per_chunk)` guarantees that chunks get truncated at the end of its expert so we don't span expert boundaries (which would have different imatrix data)

`ggml_quantize_chunk` now receives `start = 0` for every call here, instead of using `first_row * n_per_row`. Since we need the per-expert base pointers anyways, we just increment them all ahead of time.

It also uses better logic for deciding the threads to use per expert, if the matrices were small we'd end up with a low thread count, now it's based on the size of the whole tensor.

Checked the sha256sum of every file with and without this PR and they're identical, also checked on a dense model for sanity and it was the same.

Also compared this PR vs master with a single thread (since it's a different path) and also same sha256sum on https://huggingface.co/hf-internal-testing/Mixtral-tiny (can't afford the days it would take to quantize a 35B on a single thread..), time is same because this is a multi-threaded improvement.

## Overview

Fixes #26220 

After the removal of rocWMMA Flash Attention kernel path, the replacement had slower prompt processing at deep context on RDNA 4. The regression was caused by WMMA tensor cores not being used at all for head dim 256.

This PR widens `flash_attn_ext_f16` device guard to unblock MMA at head dim 256. Without it, the tile kernel is used instead which works, but slows down with more context.  The config table also needed a precision fix for DKQ=256. `nbatch_combine` was too small, causing multi-pass FP16 accumulation errors in test-backend-ops.

Additionally, for DKQ>128 on WMMA K/V is loaded directly from VRAM instead of going through LDS. Without it, MMA is actually slower than the tile kernel.

Below are benchmark numbers to confirm no regressions and the speedup. It's worth to mention that, while prompt processing is faster than current master(a7a6d0d2), it's still about 12-20% slower the old rocWMMA kernel depending on context size. There's definitely room for further improvement.

### Command line

```shell
./build/bin/llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-APEX-I-Compact.gguf --jinja -c 4096 --port 18081

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18081/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France? One word."}],
  "chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false},
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"assist","description":"web research","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string"}},"required":["query"]}}}],
  "tool_choice":"required","temperature":0,"max_tokens":600}'
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With a Qwen3-family chat template (Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE, embedded GGUF template, handled by the auto-parser path) and `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, the `tool_choice: "required"` constraint (and likewise a named function `tool_choice`) is **not enforced**: the model free-runs plain prose until `max_tokens` (`finish_reason: "length"`), returns no `tool_calls`, and `content` stays empty when the run ends inside what the parser treats as reasoning.

Control experiments on the same build and GGUF, changing exactly one variable each:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| same request, thinking **enabled** (omit the kwarg) | tool call correctly forced ✓ |
| same request, **Gemma-3-family** GGUF/template | tool call correctly forced ✓ |
| same schema via `response_format: json_schema` instead of tools | grammar correctly enforced ✓ |
| `tool_choice: "auto"` | behaves as expected (model may answer) ✓ |

So the grammar machinery itself is fine — the combination *Qwen3 template + `enable_thinking: false` + forced tool choice* is what loses the constraint. `stop` sequences are unrelated (reproduced with and without).

At temperature 0 the failure is fully deterministic. Practical impact: OpenAI-compatible agent frameworks that force the selected tool via named `tool_choice` (to generate its arguments) silently break on these very common Qwen3 no-think setups — the doomed generation runs to the token cap on every decision.

Happy to provide full server logs or test other template families if useful.

*Disclosure: this report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude); the bisection across the three builds and all control experiments were run and verified by hand on real hardware.*

items.body:
## Overview

DFlash2 adds two more modules compared to DFlash, grouped dynamic depthwise convolution and candidate selector. 

The formula is for reference. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`. `base` is the static kernel, `δ` is the dynamic part predicted from the input.`x` is divided into groups `g(c)` and `δ` is shared across a group. Another one is `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`. `A`/`B` are the codebooks for the predecessor and the candidate. This position's hidden is projected by `project(h)`to the same rank to multiply `A`. And `unary[c]` is the draft's own score for `c`.  

DFlash2 is enabled when the checkpoint is DFlash2; no need to use extra flag.

We evaled `Qwen3.8-27B` at `Q4_K_M`on Apple M5 Pro 64 GB. And the test data is first 8 problems of GSM8K.
Concurrency is set to 1 and temperature is 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20. We use default `xhigh` reasoning and set
2,048 maximum new tokens.

| Method | Draft quant | Block | Decode TPS | Decode speedup | Acceptance | Normal stops |
|--------|------|--:|------:|------:|-----:|---|
| Autoregressive | — | — | 10.42 | 1.00× | — | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | BF16 | 8 | 19.31 | 1.85× | 4.92 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q8_0 | 8 | 18.43 | 1.77× | 5.08 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q4_K_M | 8 | 18.89 | 1.81× | 5.03 | 8/8 |

items.body:
Summary

On b9870, the server starts and loads the model successfully but crashes on the first inference request with a CUDA resource allocation failure in cublasCreate_v2. The same command and model work correctly on b9553.

Environment

| Attribute | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **OS** | Fedora Linux (kernel 7.0.14-201.fc44.x86_64) |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop GPU — 8 GB VRAM |
| **CUDA** | (check yours with `nvidia-smi`) |
| **Working version** | b9553 (9e3b928fd) |
| **Broken version** | b9870 (2d973636e) |

Model

- File: Qwopus3.6-35B-A3B-v1-MTP-IQ4_XS.gguf (Qwen3-based MoE, 19 GB, IQ4_XS quant)
- --n-cpu-moe 45 used to offload MoE expert layers to CPU

Command

llama serve \
  -m /path/to/Qwopus3.6-35B-A3B-v1-MTP-IQ4_XS.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -dev CUDA0 \
  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --no-mmap \
  -t 12 -c 128000 \
  --parallel 1 -ub 1024 -b 1024 \
  --cache-ram 24576 --cache-reuse 512 \
  --n-cpu-moe 45 \
  --port 8080 --host 127.0.0.1 --slots

Server output on b9870

0.11.622.432 W srv    load_model: cache_reuse is not supported by this context, it will be disabled
0.11.809.210 I srv    load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 128000, kv_unified = 'false'
0.11.838.745 I srv          init: chat template supports preserving reasoning, consider enabling it via --reasoning-preserve
0.11.838.757 I srv  llama_server: model loaded
0.11.838.759 I srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
0.16.471.781 I slot get_availabl: id  0 | task -1 | selected slot by LRU, t_last = -1
0.16.471.856 I slot launch_slot_: id  0 | task 0 | processing task, is_child = 0
ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:104: CUDA error
0.16.501.475 E CUDA error: the resource allocation failed
0.16.501.478 E   current device: 0, in function cublas_handle at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/../ggml-cuda/common.cuh:1477
0.16.501.479 E   cublasCreate_v2(&cublas_handles[device])

dmesg

llama[...]: segfault at 8 ip ...10ec965... error 4 in llama[...]

Same offset every crash — deterministic null pointer dereference triggered by the cuBLAS failure.

Analysis

The cuBLAS handle in cublas_handle (common.cuh:1477) is initialized lazily on first inference rather than at model load time. On an 8 GB GPU with a large MoE model and --n-cpu-moe, model weights fill the available VRAM during loading. When the first request arrives and cublasCreate_v2 attempts to allocate its workspace, no VRAM remains, causing the failure and subsequent crash.

On b9553 the same model and command work correctly on the same hardware, suggesting cuBLAS handle lifecycle or VRAM reservation changed between the two builds.

Steps to reproduce

1. Load a large MoE model with --n-cpu-moe on a GPU where VRAM is near-full after model load
2. Start the server — it reports model loaded and listening successfully
3. Send any inference request
4. Server crashes with cublasCreate_v2 resource allocation failure

Expected behaviour

cuBLAS handle is either pre-allocated at init time (before VRAM is fully committed to model weights), or the allocation failure is handled gracefully without crashing the server.

Workaround

Downgrade to b9553:
curl -L https://huggingface.co/buckets/ggml-org/install.sh/resolve/b9553/x86_64/linux/cuda/89/llama-app.zst | zstd -d > ~/.llama-app/llama && chmod +x ~/.llama-app/llama && ln -sf ~/.llama-app/llama ~/.local/bin/llama

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-bench --version
version: b10470 (34af94cd9ab277632e27caeec2d41de2fd091b31)
built with Apple clang for arm64-apple-darwin25.6.0, -DGGML_METAL=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON
```

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core), llama-server, llama-bench, RPC backend, Metal backend

### Command line

Two Apple M4 machines, 16 GB unified memory each, connected by a Thunderbolt bridge.
Machine A is the main node, machine B runs the RPC worker.

```shell
# machine B (RPC worker)
ggml-rpc-server -H 192.168.2.1 -p 50052 -d MTL0

# machine A (main node) -- FAILS
llama-bench -m Qwen_Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS.gguf \
  --rpc 192.168.2.1:50052 -ts 0.50/0.50 -fa on -b 1024 -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128

# machine A -- IDENTICAL except for -mmp 0 -- WORKS
llama-bench -m Qwen_Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS.gguf \
  --rpc 192.168.2.1:50052 -ts 0.50/0.50 -fa on -b 1024 -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128 -mmp 0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a model is sharded across an RPC device, the main node appears to retain the entire
model in memory rather than only its own share. The effective size limit for a distributed
model therefore stays roughly equal to what a **single** node can hold, which defeats the
purpose of splitting it.

Disabling mmap (`-mmp 0`, or `--load-mode none` on `llama-server`) fixes it completely, with
no other change.

Model used: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS`, 15,761,446,528 bytes (14.68 GiB).
Metal `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize` is 13,958.64 MB on the main node and 12,713.12 MB on
the worker, so 14.68 GiB fits on neither alone but fits easily across both.

**A/B, one variable:**

| flags | result |
| --- | --- |
| default load mode | fails, `llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3` |
| `-mmp 1` (explicit) | fails, same error |
| `-mmp 0` | works: 322.75 t/s prompt, 26.12 t/s decode |

**Measured during a failing run**, sampling resident memory on both machines at the same
moment:

- main node `llama-bench` RSS: **12.15 GiB**
- RPC worker `ggml-rpc-server` RSS: **7.57 GiB**
- total resident across both: **19.7 GiB, for a 14.68 GiB model**

The worker really does receive its shard, and the main node keeps a full copy anyway.

The OOM is on the main node's local Metal device (`MTL0`), and compute buffers are far too
small to explain it:

```
sched_reserve: RPC0[192.168.2.1:50052] compute buffer size =    70.02 MiB
sched_reserve:       MTL0 compute buffer size =   493.52 MiB
sched_reserve:        CPU compute buffer size =     8.52 MiB
```

**Threshold behaviour**, all with the same two machines and default load mode:

| model | size | result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 | 11.28 GiB | works, splits correctly (5.68 GiB on the worker) |
| GLM-4.7-Flash IQ4_XS | 15.13 GiB | fails |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B IQ3_XXS | 14.68 GiB | fails |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M | 20.76 GiB | fails |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B Q3_K_S | 20.11 GiB | fails |

Everything at or below about 12 GiB works. Everything above fails. That threshold matches
the main node's own Metal working set, not the combined capacity of the two machines. With
`-mmp 0` every one of the failing models above loads and runs correctly across the split.

**Hypothesis, offered tentatively.** Metal on this build reports `use residency sets = true`
at init. If the mmapped model pages are placed in a residency set on the main node, the OS
cannot evict them, so sharding weights to the RPC device never releases the main node's
mapping. I have not read the allocator closely enough to confirm this, and the mechanism may
be different. The observation and the `-mmp 0` workaround are what I am confident about.

**Why this is easy to miss.** The failure does not look like an out of memory error from the
client side. `llama-bench` reports `failed to decode prompt batch, res = -3` and
`llama-server` reports a generic decode failure, so it reads as a model or architecture
problem rather than a memory one. I spent several hours attributing it to specific model
architectures (and wrongly concluded that three separate models were unsupported) before
finding that one flag fixed all of them.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. Observed on b10470 (`34af94c`). I do not know whether earlier versions behave
differently, and I have not tested current master.

### Relevant log output

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
test_prompt: failed to decode prompt batch, res = -3
llama_bench: error: failed to run prompt
```

items.body:
## Overview IQ quants are particularly slow on CPU at large batch sizes (what you'd see for imatrix and perplexity) Part of this comes from the fact that during a 512-token batch, every weight in the model is decoded 512 times from the associated lookup table This change introduces a GEMM panel, `block_iqp_x8`, which is 8 weight rows x 256 columns: ``` struct block_iqp_x8 { float dfac[8]; // per row: the float part of the scale (d * 2^-k) int32_t bias[8]; // per row: unsigned-activation correction int8_t iscales[16 * 8]; // per (sub-block, row): the integer part of the scale int8_t qs[256 * 8]; // the decoded weights, interleaved }; ``` Now, instead of decoding each weight 512 times at batch 512, we decode 8 rows at a time into a cache-sized `int8` tile and run integer GEMM over it. For dense models, this is a huge increase, up to 10x For MoE it's more modest, more like 2x, but still quite good PPL shifts a tiny bit, only ~0.24%, aka margin of error
Design details from Claude Four design details make it work: 1. Interleaving 8 rows. qs[sb*128 + g*32 + row*4 + k] holds column sb*16 + g*4 + k. So one 32-byte load pulls 4 consecutive columns for each of 8 rows — exactly the operand shape _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 wants against a broadcast int32 of 4 activations. Eight output rows advance per instruction. 2. Sub-blocks of 16, not 32. iq2_xs/iq2_s take a group of 32 weights' scale from two nibbles, one per half. One scale per 32 couldn't represent them exactly, so 16 is used uniformly for all eight types → one kernel. 3. Split scale = float × integer (this is commit 4f7e113af). Every supported type's sub-block scale factors as (d · 2⁻ᵏ) · small_int — e.g. iq2_xs is d·(0.5+ls)·0.25 = (d/8)·(2ls+1). So dfac holds the float, iscales the integer. The kernel then applies sub-block scales in integer (mullo_epi32), accumulates the whole 256-weight super-block exactly in int32, and touches float exactly once per (row, super-block). That's 16 float roundings → 1. A float64 reference harness measured the result as 12–22% more accurate than upstream vec_dot (the previous float-scale version had been 2.6× less accurate). 4. The bias trick. VNNI's dpbusd needs unsigned × signed, but both operands here are signed. Instead of fixing that with _mm256_sign_epi8 per operand, activations are fed as y ^ 0x80 (i.e. y + 128), and the resulting spurious 128·Σw term — a per-row, per-super-block constant — is precomputed into bias at decode time and subtracted with one int32 op. Non-VNNI AVX2 builds fall back to the sign trick with bias disabled, because the maddubs int16 accumulator would overflow with unsigned operands.
## Additional information On dense models, this only kicks in when batch >= ~~32~~ **8** columns, less than that was found to have lower performance, set with `GGML_IQP_MIN_BATCH` in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqp.h` (edit: lowered to 8 with a better kernel) for MoE, it instead gates per-expert, and only works when needs to see ~~16~~ **8** columns to route through the new panel, otherwise old performance is better, set with `GGML_IQP_MIN_BATCH_ID` in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqp.h`. (edit: also lowered to 8 with better kernel) Can be disabled with `GGML_NO_IQ_PANEL=1` Confirmed with tests that setting `GGML_NO_IQ_PANEL=1` returns original performance and PPL completely, as well as when using a lower batch size (`-ub 16`). At `-ub 16`, there is still an ~80% speed up in performance on dense ## Benchmark numbers I ran PPL against master and this PR to get speed and numbers on `--chunks 50` for Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on EPYC 9654 using 24 threads Created pure `IQ1_S`, `IQ1_M`, `IQ2_XXS`, `IQ2_XS`, `IQ2_S`, `IQ3_XXS`, `IQ3_S`, and `IQ4_XS`. Made pure to make sure each tensor type is fully exercised. items.title: Eval bug: llama-server crashes on CUDA with Qwen3.6-27B

items.body:
# RCA: Whole-Host Lock During MTP Prefill

**Model:** Qwopus3.6-27B-Fusion-Q5_K_M on dual RTX 3090 (tensor split) 
(tested with multiple models and they all do it. This is not a bug in a particular model's mtp head as detailed below.)

**Context:** llama.cpp b9745, speculative decoding via MTP

**Impact:** Full host lock requiring power cycle during long-prompt prefill with MTP active.

I have read and agree with the contributing guideline =  Yes
AI usage disclosure = Yes
---

## Summary

Huge prefills (100k+ tokens) reliably locked the system within a short period when MTP speculative decoding was enabled. MTP-off completed identical requests fine (~295 s).

Root cause: MTP draft catch-up queued two GPU graphs against the same mutable KV cache without waiting for either to finish. Under prolonged tensor-split prefill, the overlapping work hit a dependency error inside the CUDA/meta backend and at least one GPU entered a non-completing kernel. 

Note: **The issue inside the backend is still unknown.** I spent probably 6 hours and a dozen of hard-wedges solving the sync issue. I'm spent. Additionally, I didn't want to mix a speculative CUDA fix into a concrete MTP repair.

Fix: serialize MTP ubatches so each finishes before the next starts.

---

## How it was finally pinpointed and reproduced reliably

Added explicit `llama_synchronize(ctx_dft)` after the catch-up call. The host locked at that synchronize confirming the failing work lives inside the draft context, not the target.

Both draft ubatches had already logged success (`CTX-COMPUTE-EXIT status=0`, `AR-EXIT ok=1`) because the API accepts queued work without waiting for GPU completion.

To confirm serialization alone was the cure, I added per-ubatch synchronization inside `llama_context::decode()` no eval callback, normal graph UID reuse. I then ran three consecutive high-prefill sweeps (100k-180k). Each completed successfully, zero failures. Great success.

Earlier tests using scheduler eval callbacks succeeded too, including a terminal-only callback creating no interior graph cut which rules out theories about K/V or attention boundaries being required.

None of these fixes were necessary when MTP was off. I can say with confidence that it is a race issue on systems with multiple GPUs and MTP.

---

## Other theories disproven

Disabling CUDA graphs, switching to fallback/butterfly allreduce, disabling ASPM L1, reverting from kernel 7.0.0-29 to 7.0.0-28. None of these prevented the wedge. Memory and VRAM remained available throughout. Failure position varied from ~78k to ~143k tokens with no deterministic boundary. 

These results narrow the failure to the overlap condition itself.

---

## When the code was introduced

PR #22673 added `llama_decode(ctx_dft, batch)` for MTP catch-up on May 16, 2026 without synchronization between internally split ubatches. Has been there since MTP support was added to llama.cpp. Short-context operations fit in one ubatch so they never triggered it. This workload guarantees multiple ubatches (2048 batch vs. 1024 ubatch). This bug has been present since MTP support was added to llama.

---

## Fix

Synchronize after each internal ubatch for MTP contexts:

```cpp
bool mtp_multi_ubatch = false;
do {
    const auto & ubatch = mctx->get_ubatch();
    // ... process ...
    bool has_next = mctx->next();
    mtp_multi_ubatch |= has_next;
    if (cparams.ctx_type == LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP && mtp_multi_ubatch) {
        synchronize();
    }
} while (has_next);
```

Only activates for MTP contexts with multiple ubatches. Target decode, non-MTP speculative decoding, and short MTP drafts pass through unchanged.

---

## Regression test

The upstream-ready checkout adds `test-mtp-ubatch-sync` to `tests/test-llama-archs.cpp`.

The test builds a tiny synthetic Qwen3.5 model with one MTP layer and runs a four-token MTP batch on CPU:
- `n_batch=4`, `n_ubatch=2`: two internal ubatches. The test requires synchronization before the second ubatch starts.
- `n_batch=4`, `n_ubatch=4`: one internal ubatch. The test verifies that this path remains asynchronous.

The CPU abort callback runs while each graph is executing. `synchronize()` accounts the queued tokens in `llama_perf_context`, so the callback on the second ubatch can tell whether the first ubatch was synchronized. This tests ordering inside the actual decode loop without requiring CUDA or reproducing a host lock in CI.

Before:

```text
MTP ubatches were not synchronized
test-mtp-ubatch-sync: Failed
```

After:

```text
test-mtp-ubatch-sync: Passed (0.02 s)
```


## Upstream issue

The existing report that most closely matches this failure is [#23210: llama-server crashes on CUDA with Qwen3.6-27B](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/23210). It includes Qwen3.6, CUDA, MTP, long-context prefill, multi-GPU configurations, and hard GPU/host hangs. No open PR matching the ubatch serialization fix was found.

Issue #26558 is a different MTP crash involving CUDA graph-cache growth and an invalid cuBLAS stream. Its `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` workaround did not fix this reproducer in two controlled atts. I wanted to note it anyway for reviewers looking at the PR.

# Disclosure Note
Investigative analysis was done manually and in conjunction with GPT 5.6 Sol. I sign off on the code used to patch llama. It is the proper chokepoint for the repair. I explored a bunch of different approaches and this was the right one as it does not have a performance impact in day-to-day usage and fixes the issue as close to the root (without getting into repairing the backend) as possible.
items.title: fix(mtp): serialize multi-ubatch decode execution

items.body:
## Overview

f16 KV layout does not engage all memory channels. This PR engages all channels by copying each layers f16 KV once into a scratch so that the KV cache reads are sequential. Reuse of scratch introduced in PR #25494 

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->
Gating set to AMD where effect was measured, RTX 3070 did not benefit, Intel and any other vendor have not been tested.

Consecutive KV rows of one head are read `n_kv_heads × head_dim × 2` bytes apart. Typical model KV geometry spacing is an even multiple of the 256B channel-interleave block that Mesa documents, causing only a subset of memory channels to engage. 
| KV geometry (heads × head_dim) | example models | row spacing | ÷ 256 B | channels engaged (of 16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 × 128 | small GQA-heavy models | 512 B | 2 | 8 |

items.title: vulkan: add f16 B-type matmul pipelines and warp tile size tuning for Intel coopmat1

items.body:
### Name and Version

fox@ubuntu-llm:~/kitsu$ llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server --version
version: 9893 (d75936111)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL --fit-target 512 --n-gpu-layers 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -np 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### TL;DR

When running with `--fit-params` enabled and without specifying a `--ctx-size`, `load_model` overestimates the memory footprint of any mtp/draft context. It uses `n_ctx_train` to estimate the speculative component's size, rather than the actual context size, which is not determined until after fit is run for the draft/mtp context.

On my 32 GB VRAM machine, I found that `fit-params` was overestimating qwen3.6's MTP context by ~500 MiB.

### Examples

After identifying this bug, I tested loading models when `fit-params` was enabled and disabled, and provide outputs below to show that the speculative context footprint is significantly overestimated. Each of these outputs are taken (and condensed for brevity) from llama-server logs run with the base command included above. I'm running this on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB VRAM). The only variation is in the `--ctx-size` passed in.

1. No `--ctx-size` specified (Estimated: 1672 MiB | Actual: 1189 MiB)

```ini
# MTP (Estimated):
[spec] estimated memory usage of MTP context is 1672.03 MiB
# ...
projected to use 34125 MiB of device memory vs. 31003 MiB of free device memory
# ...
context size reduced from 262144 to 179712 -> need 5313 MiB less memory in total

# MTP (Actual):
creating MTP draft context against the target model 'Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf'
# ...
llama_kv_cache:      CUDA0 KV buffer size =              702.00 MiB
sched_reserve:        CUDA0 compute buffer size =   487.03 MiB
```

2. `--ctx-size 179712` (Estimated: 1189 MiB | Actual: 1189 MiB)

```ini
# MTP (Estimated):
[spec] estimated memory usage of MTP context is 1189.03 MiB
# ...
projected to use 28812 MiB of device memory vs. 31003 MiB of free device memory
will leave 2190 >= 1701 MiB of free device memory, no changes needed

# MTP (Actual):
creating MTP draft context against the target model 'Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf'
# ...
llama_kv_cache:      CUDA0 KV buffer size =              702.00 MiB
sched_reserve:        CUDA0 compute buffer size =   487.03 MiB
```

_Here I saw I could push ctx higher, so I found the highest ctx value I could while still leaving enough memory to satisfy `fit-target 512`_

3. `--ctx-size 186600` (Estimated: 1229 MiB | Actual: 1229 MiB)

```ini
# MTP (Estimated):
[spec] estimated memory usage of MTP context is 1229.53 MiB
#...
projected to use 29257 MiB of device memory vs. 31003 MiB of free device memory
will leave 1745 >= 1741 MiB of free device memory, no changes needed

# MTP (Actual):
creating MTP draft context against the target model 'Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf'
# ...
llama_kv_cache:      CUDA0 KV buffer size =              729.00 MiB
sched_reserve:        CUDA0 compute buffer size =   500.53 MiB
```

### First Bad Commit

I think this has been around since MTP was introduced

### Relevant log output

See above

### Conclusion

This issue exists because of the way fit is calculated in `load_model`. 

The fit process is performed separately between the `mmproj`, `spec/mtp`, and main model/ctx. However, the best fit for one component clearly depends on the fit results for the others. The proper fix for this is likely to pull "fit" out of the `common_init_result` constructor and into a dedicated library that performs fit for all loaded components, together.
items.title: Misc. bug: fitting params to memory overallocates speculative context when ctx-size is unspecified

items.body:
## Overview

When running with `--fit-params` enabled and without specifying a `--ctx-size`, `load_model` overestimates the memory footprint of any draft/mtp context. It uses `n_ctx_train` to estimate speculative context size, rather than the actual context size. This is due to the fact that `n_ctx` is not determined until after the main model fit is run.

As a result, speculative contexts take up more VRAM than they should. On my 32 GB machine, I found that `--fit-params` was overestimating qwen3.6's MTP context by ~500 MiB.

Fixes #25408 

## Additional information

In this PR:
- a helper method now splits speculative context fit into two parts: a fixed component, and a per-ctx component
- the main model fit now uses the per-ctx overhead when calculating n_ctx
- n_ctx is now persisted after main model fit and used to init speculative context

**Results** I ran the same command on both master and this branch:

`llama-server -m Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL --fit-target 512 --n-gpu-layers 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -np 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`

* On master: fit gives `n_ctx: 184320`

## Overview

llama-server crashed with **Assertion 'found' failed** in **llama_sampler_dist_apply** when using mtp speculative decoding _--spec-type draft-mtp_ on long contexts, 30k+ tokens in my cases. 
Reproduction environment: _ryzen 5700X + radeon rx6800xt ROCm HIP_ with _qwen3.6:35b-a3b q4_K_M_ with partial offloading to ram, arch Linux (up-to-date at the time of writing), _--batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 512_. Without MTP everything is stable.

Root cause is the dist sampler could not handle a degenerate distribution. When the MTP draft head produced only -inf logits, the softmax turned them into NaN, the token selection loop could not find a candidate, and assert(found) terminated the process with SIGABRT.

The crash occurred with the official Arch Linux package (llama-cpp build with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=None), which keeps asserts enabled. I build same flags for testing and working. The regression test covers was tested after all day working normaly,  arch official package still crashing if i downgrade. It fails before the fix (same Assertion 'found' failed, SIGABRT) and passes after. The crash only happens in builds with asserts enabled (CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=None - the **official Arch package**  or Debug). With -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (NDEBUG) the assert is removed so there is no crash - the sampler silently picks the last candidate instead. 

## Additional information

Fixes: #26648 (my issue for this PR)
Related: #22136 (looks similar but closed, i have my issue not sure its same)

## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

Vulkan

items.body:
## Overview

Tesla P100's get a nice (~20%) pp speedup by using mmq even without native dp4a. For `-sm tensor` configurations with multiple cards, this increases to around a +100% pp speedup (for 2 cards, possibly more with more cards).

This PR is similar to, but inverse of, it's inspiration: #24588, where gfx900 had mmq always turned on even without dp4a, and kept mmq for MoE. sm_60 will now use mmq, but only for MoE.

This might be relevant for even older NVidia hardware as well, but I only have access to a 4GB Quadro that might not be a good reference point (and no models that come to mind). For now it's gated to only the P100.

## Additional information

Tests are on two P100 cards (powerlimited to 150W, connected via PCIe 3.0 x8). See comments below for tests for each quantization type (exps quantized to type tested, all other tensors Q4_0).

items.body:
## Overview The Q4_K/Q5_K scale unpack branches on a runtime value to pick between two layouts. nvcc can't fold that, so it predicates it and then repeats the whole thing for every column of the ncols_dst loop instead of doing it once. Swapping the branch for a mask select fixes it: predicated instructions at ncols_dst=8 go from 226 to 34, and the Q4_K kernel at 16 columns from 2256 to 1648. None of the other quant types have this problem, they already unpack unconditionally (Q3_K does the same 6-bit layout with plain shifts). We see perf gains from batch size >=4 on RTX 5090 and >=5 on RTX 4090 (more details in the Performance drop down), however we do not see a gain with DGX Spark, and in fact a small regression at batch sizes 4-6, which is why the change is gated off there. The most probable reason for this can be that the memory bandwidth on DGX Spark is much lower than that of RTX 4090 or 5090, and this means even with this optimization there is no effective time to save, since in the original code the unpack was already running while the kernel waits on the weight loads and so was not adding to the total time.
Performance

## Benchmarks (RTX 5090, sm_120, CUDA 12.9, driver 620.23) Both builds are from the same commit; the only difference is this patch. Batch size below refers to `ne11`, the number of columns the matmul receives in a single forward pass. It can arise in three ways, which are indistinguishable to the kernel: N concurrent requests against a server started with `-np N`, a draft block of `n_max + 1` tokens on a single slot, or `llama-bench -p N` directly. Two rows per model. `decode` is `llama-bench -p N -n 0 -embd 1 -r 40`, a single forward pass of N tokens with nothing generated, which is the decode step at batch N. `end to end` is llama-server tokens/sec, which also includes prefill, sampling and the draft model, and is therefore always lower. `*` marks a quant type this patch does not modify. ### 1. vs batch size Llama-3.1-8B, no draft model; only `-np` changes. The llama-server figures are total tokens over wall time at 256 tokens per request, temperature 0, across 3 runs alternating between the two builds. The request count is always a multiple of the batch size so that the final wave is not partially filled. | quant | metric | batch 1 | batch 2 | batch 4 | batch 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K_M** | decode | **-0.3%** | **+1.6%** | **+8.9%** | **+14.7%** | | | end to end | +0.4% | +1.1% | +7.4% | +10.8% | | **Q5_K_M** | decode | **+0.4%** | **+2.0%** | **+6.6%** | **+14.2%** | | | end to end | -0.1% | +1.5% | +5.5% | +11.4% | | **Q6_K** * | decode | **-1.2%** | **-1.1%** | **-0.8%** | **-0.9%** | | | end to end | -0.1% | +0.2% | +0.3% | +0.2% | There is no effect at batch 1, which is expected: the unpack can only be amortised once there is more than one column to share it across. ### 2. Other models Batch pinned at 4, no draft model. | model | metric | Q4_K_M | Q5_K_M | Q6_K * | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Llama-3.1-8B** | decode | **+8.9%** | **+6.6%** | **-0.8%** | | | end to end | +7.4% | +5.5% | +0.3% | | **gemma-4-12B** | decode | **+8.2%** | **+6.3%** | **+0.0%** | | | end to end | +6.8% | +6.0% | +0.1% | | **Qwen3.6-27B** | decode | **+6.2%** | **+5.1%** | **+0.3%** | | | end to end | +8.0% | +4.2% | +0.5% | ### 3. Batch from a draft block instead of concurrent requests `--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 3` on a single slot, so the target verifies 4 tokens in one pass: batch 4 obtained from a draft block rather than from concurrency. The decode rows repeat table 2 because it is the same file at the same batch; the kernel is indifferent to the source of the batch. | model | metric | Q4_K_M | Q5_K_M | Q6_K * | |---|---|---|---|---| | **gemma-4-12B-it** | decode | **+8.2%** | **+6.3%** | **+0.0%** | | | end to end | +6.3% | +6.2% | -0.7% | | **Qwen3.6-27B** | decode | **+6.2%** | **+5.1%** | **+0.3%** | | | end to end | +6.3% | +5.5% | +0.1% | ### 4. Decode over the whole batch range The same llama-bench run on `--pure` single-type models, so that every quantized `mul_mat` is the type in question. The Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M files above are mixed, with output and some attention tensors in Q6_K, which is why they report lower gains. | type | batch 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K** | +1.0% | +3.6% | +6.7% | +13.6% | +17.0% | +19.0% | +17.5% | +17.4% | | **Q5_K** | -0.6% | +2.0% | +1.7% | +9.3% | +10.3% | +16.8% | +15.9% | +17.2% | | **Q6_K** * | +0.3% | +0.4% | -1.0% | -0.5% | -0.8% | -0.4% | -1.6% | -0.6% | | **Q8_0** * | +1.1% | +0.3% | +1.0% | +1.3% | +1.0% | +1.8% | +1.9% | +1.7% | ## Benchmarks (RTX 4090, sm_89, CUDA 12.9, driver 591.86) Both builds are from the same commit; the only difference is this patch. Conventions are as above: `decode` is `llama-bench -p N -n 0 -embd 1 -r 40`, `end to end` is llama-server tokens/sec at 256 tokens per request, temperature 0. `*` marks a quant type this patch does not modify. Clocks were pinned, no interactive session was present on the machine, and the base build was run at both ends of every pass so that the noise floor is measured rather than assumed. Batch size throughout refers to `ne11`, the number of columns the matmul receives in a single forward pass. It can arise in three ways, which are indistinguishable to the kernel: N concurrent requests against a server started with `-np N`, a draft block of `n_max + 1` tokens on a single slot, or `llama-bench -p N` directly. Tables 1, 2 and 4 use the first and third; table 3 uses the second. ### 1. vs batch size Llama-3.1-8B, no draft model. Decode rows use `-p N`; end-to-end rows use `-np N` with the request count kept a multiple of N so that all slots remain occupied. | quant | metric | batch 1 | batch 2 | batch 4 | batch 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K_M** | decode | **+0.0%** |

### Name and Version

version: 9967 (4f37f5197)

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Linux / CUDA / 4× Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB (sm_60), dual Xeon, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 12.4. Tested on Ubuntu Server 26.04.

### Models

Qwen3.6-27B Q6_K (22,523,238,624 bytes) for the quality panel; Qwen3.6-4B dense and Darwin-36B-A3B (Qwen3.5-MoE arch) Q6_K for the speed legs.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

SM_60 currently gets put into a hardware accelerated fast-path by default, which uses a FP16 hardware accelerator. The problem is that some FP32 math is silently getting truncated to FP16 that shouldn't be, causing significant accuracy deviations from baseline (0.002298 median KL divergence vs FP32 reference/1-in-29 flipped top tokens).

The fix for this is to carve out SM_60 the same way SM_61 already is, bypassing the Fast Path gate, and keeping FP32 math at 32 bits as it should be.

## How to Fix

261- #if defined(FP16_AVAILABLE) && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 610
261+ #if defined(FP16_AVAILABLE) && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 610 && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 600

305-        (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && fp16_available(cc) && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 610) ||
305+        (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && fp16_available(cc) && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 610 && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 600) ||

311-    return (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && cc >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL && cc != 610) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_AMD(cc) ||
311+    return (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && cc >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL && cc != 610 && cc != 600) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_AMD(cc) ||

TheTom (Tom Turney) has shipped: https://github.com/TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant/releases/tag/tqp-v0.3.0 
https://github.com/TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant/pull/212 
spiritbuun has merged: https://github.com/spiritbuun/buun-llama-cpp/pull/80


## Steps to Reproduce:

1. Build stock llama.cpp using  `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=60`.
2. Generate the truth base, run `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base out.kld` with fp32 KV, FA off,
   on a patched build (fp32 arithmetic) — this is the step everyone skips.
3. Compare the stock vs patched runs against that base with `--kl-divergence`, 2048 ctx, 32 chunks.
4. Speed: `llama-bench` pp8192/tg32 @ d8192, patched vs unpatched, same host, nothing else
   on the GPUs.



### First Bad Commit

We followed the 610-only exemptions in their present form back through the 2024-era commits dc685be46 (#7188, FP32 FA vec kernel), 9b596417a (#7527, quantized KV for FA vec), and a818f3028 (#8075, MMQ-by-default) — sm_60 has been on the fast path the whole time,  no bisect needed.

### Relevant log output

What's below: same weights, f32 KV, FA is off on both sides; the only difference is stock fp16 arithmetic vs patched fp32 arithmetic, so it separates the arithmetic cost alone.

**Cell 0 (arithmetic-only delta, fp16 math vs fp32 math):**
median KLD **0.004962**, mean 0.023987, 99.9% 4.91, max 23.7, max Δp 98.9%,
**same-top 95.002%** — the arithmetic mode alone flips 1 in 20 greedy tokens, and about 1/1000
tokens gets its distribution basically replaced. This component is ~2× the attention-path
effect and was invisible to every prior measurement. 


Accuracy:
**Cells 1–3 **

| rung | unpatched median KLD | patched median KLD | same-top: unpatched → patched |
|---|---|---|---|
| f16-faoff | 0.002298  | **0.000001** | 96.47% → **99.89%** |
| f16-faon  | 0.002127 | **0.000000** | 96.45% → **99.93%** |
| q8-faon   | 0.002164 | **0.000005** | 96.52% → **99.80%** |


Performance:
pp8192 @ d8192, tg32 @ d8192, 4× P100 layer-split, same model:

| config | patched | unpatched | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| f16 KV prefill | 318.53 ± 0.53 t/s | 318.60 ± 0.35 t/s | **tie** |

items.body:
### Summary

On **gfx1151 (Strix Halo / Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Windows 11)** the **HIP backend silently corrupts inference of Qwen3.5-27B** (hybrid Gated-DeltaNet architecture, tested as VLM with mmproj): the **oldest part of the context is consistently lost** while output stays fluent and deterministic. The **Vulkan backend at the identical commit is correct**. We ran an extensive exclusion campaign (details below); every individually testable component passes, so the defect appears to live at graph-composition level of the GDN block on HIP.

### Environment

- HW: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S iGPU (**gfx1151**), 128 GB unified memory
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 26200, Adrenalin driver 32.0.31035.1003
- ROCm runtime: TheRock `therock-dist-windows-gfx1151-7.14.0rc3` (also reproduced with a different ROCm 7.x runtime DLL set)
- llama.cpp: official release zips `llama-b10453-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip` **and** `llama-b10582-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip`, **and** a self-built b10582 (e85caa81e) with the TheRock clang toolchain — **all three affected identically**
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (unsloth GGUF) + mmproj BF16
- Counter-checks: **Vulkan builds of the very same commits (b10453 and b10582) are correct**; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (pure attention, no GDN) is correct on the same HIP builds

### Reproduction (deterministic, temp 0)

Generate a synthetic 4-panel test image (no external assets needed):

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
W,H=660,640; img=Image.new('RGB',(W,H),'white'); d=ImageDraw.Draw(img)
try: fb=ImageFont.truetype('arialbd.ttf',20); fs=ImageFont.truetype('arial.ttf',14)
except: fb=fs=ImageFont.load_default()
for x,y,t,c in [(0,0,'Alpha Risk','Risk from parallel shifts of the reference rate.'),
                (330,0,'Beta Risk','Risk from non-parallel curve changes.'),
                (0,320,'Gamma Risk','Risk from embedded options, e.g. early repayment.'),
                (330,320,'Delta Risk','Risk from hedging with different rate indices.')]:
    d.rectangle([x+2,y+2,x+328,y+318],outline='black',width=2)
    d.ellipse([x+12,y+16,x+22,y+26],fill='black'); d.text((x+30,y+12),t,fill='black',font=fb)
    d.rectangle([x+30,y+50,x+290,y+200],outline='gray')
    if 'Gamma' in t:
        for i,bh in enumerate([60,90,130,100,80]): d.rectangle([x+50+i*45,y+195-bh,x+80+i*45,y+195],fill='gray')
    else: d.line([(x+40+i*25,y+190-int(12*(i**1.2))) for i in range(10)],fill='black',width=2)
    d.text((x+30,y+215),c,fill='black',font=fs)
img.save('synthetic_4panel.png')
```

```
llama-mtmd-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-BF16.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 4096 --temp 0 --seed 42 --image synthetic_4panel.png \
  -p "List ALL bold bullet headings in this image, top-left to bottom-right. Only the list."
```

- **HIP (gfx1151):** `['Beta Risk', 'Gamma Risk', 'Delta Risk']` — **top-left "Alpha Risk" (the oldest image tokens in raster order) is dropped**
- **Vulkan (same commit, same machine):** all four headings
- With a denser real-world 4-panel document scan the effect is stronger: HIP loses the entire upper half (0/4 headings) while Vulkan stays 4/4; flipping the image vertically "heals" it (the previously-top content becomes the newest tokens), which points at recency-position rather than image-coordinates.

### Exclusion campaign (everything below was tested on the same machine)

| Hypothesis | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime-DLL mismatch | official b10453 binary + clean matching TheRock 7.14 runtime | still wrong |
| Code regression / fix between builds | b10453 **and** b10582 built for **Vulkan** (same commits) | both correct → code exonerated |
| Toolchain | self-built HIP b10582 (TheRock clang) | reproduces official zips exactly |
| mtmd preprocessing | top-half crop alone is read fine; full preprocessing chain reviewed | exonerated |
| hipGraphs | `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | still wrong |
| ubatch state handoff | `-ub 128 / 512 / 8192` (whole prompt in one ubatch) | still wrong |
| GATED_DELTA_NET kernel | `test-backend-ops -o GATED_DELTA_NET`, **including added prefill-scale cases** (n_seq_tokens 64/256/1024 at the real 32x128 geometry, v_repeat 2, and K=4/8 snapshot slots — upstream currently tests max n_seq_tokens=4 and K>1 only with tiny shapes) | **43/43 pass at NMSE 1e-7** |
| Any other op in the graph | per-op sweep: SSM_CONV, CUMSUM, L2_NORM, RMS_NORM, EXP, SIGMOID, SOFT_MAX, ADD, MUL, SCALE, CPY, SET_ROWS, GET_ROWS, ROPE, FLASH_ATTN_EXT, GLU, SUM_ROWS, TRI, MUL_MAT_ID, MUL_MAT (>6400 cases total) | all pass |

Test-case additions we used (happy to open a PR):

```diff
     test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 64, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 256, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1024, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 256, 1, 2));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 256, 1, 1, false, false, 4));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1024, 1, 1, false, false, 4));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1024, 1, 2, false, false, 8));
```

### Possibly related observations (same machine, can file separately)

1. `test-backend-ops -o SOLVE_TRI` crashes on this HIP setup with `rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidImage'` / "device kernel image is invalid" after 6 passing cases — this also makes the **unfused** gated-delta-net graph path unusable on HIP, so we could not A/B fused vs. unfused. (Filed separately.)
2. `llama-mtmd-cli` dies silently (no error output after "llama threadpool init") whenever CPU layers participate (`-ngl < 99` and `-ngl 0`), on our HIP **and** Vulkan self-builds — this blocked partial-offload bisection.

### Ask

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Off-topic comments and AI slop/spam in this thread will be deleted. Keep the discussion focused.

---

Draft. Adds support for `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` (HF `model_type: qwen4_exp`, `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`): converter, text graph, sparse attention, vision, and three quantizer fixes the model needs. Opening as a draft because the weights are not public yet, so the accuracy numbers below cannot be reproduced from outside at the moment.

## Architecture

| subsystem | how it is handled |
|---|---|
| Gated delta net (3 of every 4 layers) | subclasses the existing delta-net base; the only delta from Qwen3.5 is a sigmoid output gate instead of silu |
| MoE, 512 experts, top-10, gated shared expert | `build_moe_ffn`, unchanged |
| Interleaved mrope, partial rotary 64/256 | `ggml_rope_multi` with `LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_IMROPE`, unchanged |
| Hyper-connections (`hc_count = 4`, low rank) | self-contained in `qwen4exp.cpp`; `deepseek4.cpp` is untouched |
| Per-layer embeddings, 97.7 GiB n-gram hash table | host-side row indices in a `set_input`, then `ggml_get_rows` |
| QSA sparse attention (budget 2048, ratio 4) | new graph plus an optional third cache in `llama_memory_hybrid` |
| Vision | stock Qwen3-VL ViT through the existing clip path |

`git diff master --stat -- ggml/` is empty: no new ggml op, and no change to any existing one.

## Correctness, against the reference implementation

| check | result |
|---|---|
| wikitext-2 perplexity, 145 chunks at ctx 2048 | 4.0068 +/- 0.02271 vs 4.0126 for the reference |
| top-1 agreement, 512 tokens of prose | 98.0 percent |
| QSA vs dense below the budget | bit identical, max logit delta 0.0 over all 2051 rows |
| QSA vs dense above the budget, 8192 tokens | diverges on 3 percent of positions |
| indexer selection vs the reference | 0.975 mean jaccard against a 0.991 precision floor |
| `test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` | OK on CPU (0.00e+00) and CUDA (8.00e-08), roundtrip OK |

The bit-identical result below the budget is the useful one: QSA is dense by construction under `indexer_top_k + compress_ratio - 1` cached tokens, so it is a free oracle on the whole selection and masking path.

## Effect on other architectures

Six shared files contain deletions rather than pure additions:

- `llama-quant.cpp`: three fixes, each byte-exact against the parent commit. `tensor_type_fallback` had no case for 32-block types, so a tensor whose ncols is not divisible by 32 aborted instead of falling back; `--tensor-type` could not name `per_layer_token_embd` because `--token-embedding-type` returned first; and the `work` buffer was sized `nelements * 4` as an upper bound on a value already known exactly, which is 150 GB per process on a model with a 51.2 G element tensor. Six A/B cases, six matching md5s.
- `llama-graph.cpp`: `build_attn_mask_top_k` lifted verbatim out of the DSA `build_attn` overload so both share it. The node construction sequence is identical after splicing the helper back into its call site, and `deepseek32` and `glm-dsa` both pass at 0.00e+00 on CPU.
- `llama-memory-hybrid.cpp`: the new `filter_idx` defaults to `nullptr` and every use is guarded.
- `llama-model-loader.cpp`: adds a `GGUF_TYPE_UINT64` case to a type check that previously threw.
- `llama-hparams.cpp`, `llama-model.cpp`: new fields and new switch cases.

A shared hyper-connection base with `deepseek4` was considered and rejected: the two formulations agree on the residual layout and nothing else (full-rank projection with Sinkhorn normalisation there, low-rank silu gate and a mean collapse here), so factoring it out would touch DSV4's hot path to share about ten lines.

## Note for reviewers

This branch was developed against a snapshot and rebased onto current master. Two rebase conflicts were resolved by hand, both additive: `test-llama-archs.cpp` where master had added a `LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4` condition to a line this port also edits, and `llama-model-saver.cpp` where master reworked the DSV4 key block. Worth a close look, since the local build was against the pre-rebase tree.

Used Claude and Local Models for testing, iteration and code design - manual verification of model / PR usage

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

On the ROCm backend, using any q5_0 KV cache type (either K or V) causes the compute graph to fragment from 2 splits into 34 splits. This pushes ~550-580 MiB of compute to the CPU host buffer and causes a ~68% regression in prompt processing throughput.

The issue is **specific to the ROCm backend**. The same build on Vulkan handles q5_0 KV cache correctly (2 splits, no regression). A fork of llama.cpp (build 11429) also handles it correctly on ROCm.

## Environment

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), 24 GB VRAM
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7900X
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL (16.34 GiB, 27.32 B params)
- Flash attention: enabled (`-fa 1`)

## Benchmark results

| KV Cache | graph splits | GPU compute buf | CPU compute buf | pp512 | tg128 |
|----------|:-----------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|:-----:|:-----:|
| q8_0 / q8_0 (ROCm) | 2 | 786.53 MiB | 161.53 MiB | 957.11 t/s | 37.53 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **551.28 MiB** | **300.10 t/s** | **27.96 t/s** |
| q5_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **580.53 MiB** | **302.49 t/s** | **28.39 t/s** |
| q8_0 / q8_0 (Vulkan, same build) | 2 | 270.53 MiB | 158.53 MiB | 771.39 t/s | 37.17 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (Vulkan, same build) | **2** | **295.03 MiB** | **183.03 MiB** | **762.60 t/s** | **37.01 t/s** |

The trigger is q5_0 in the KV cache. It does not matter whether it's used for K, V, or both. The broken GPU compute buffer size is identical (122.28 MiB) in both q8_0/q5_0 and q5_0/q5_0 cases, confirming it's the same code path.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build llama.cpp with ROCm support (or use a prebuilt ROCm binary)
2. Run `llama-bench -m <model.gguf> -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` (or `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0`)

4. Compare with the same build on Vulkan — no regression

## Expected behavior

q5_0 KV cache should perform similarly to q8_0 KV cache (within a small margin) when using flash attention, as it does on Vulkan and on the beellama fork (build 11429).

The main model's `sched_reserve` output:

## Bug report: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp) garbage output on SM110 (Jetson Thor) when >8 layers offloaded to GPU

**Hardware**: NVIDIA Jetson Thor (SM110, Blackwell), aarch64, 122GB unified memory, CUDA 13.0
**llama.cpp**: master `035e227` (llama: hold the qwen4exp indexer cache in a new llama_memory_hybrid_idx), built with:
`-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=110 -DGGML_CUDA_FA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON -DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=ON`
**Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS (93.7GB, 3 split shards, qwen4exp arch)

### Symptom
- `llama-cli -ngl 8` (layers 0-7 on GPU): output is **fully coherent** ✅
- `llama-cli -ngl 9` or more (layers 0-8+ on GPU): output is **garbage** (incoherent token salad) ❌
- `llama-cli -ngl 0` (pure CPU): fully coherent ✅
- Same model works coherently on CPU; prefill/decode rates are sane in all cases (no crashes, no CUDA errors logged)

### What was excluded (all still garbage at `-ngl 999`)
- flash attention on/off
- `--no-mmap`
- PLE table forced to CPU (`--override-tensor per_layer_token_embd=CPU`)
- `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1`
- rebuild with `-DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=OFF`
- `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1`
- layers 8-9 pinned to CPU via `--override-tensor` (blk.8.*/blk.9.*) while all other layers on GPU

### Additional data points
- The exact same build flags run **Ling-3.0-tiny** (a different MoE/linear-attention arch) on this same box at 88-90 tok/s with fully coherent output — so SM110 CUDA generally works.
- The qwen4exp garbage appears from the first generated token, and (without EOS) generation loops indefinitely writing huge logs.
- Threshold is exactly at the 9th offloaded layer (index 8); `-ngl 8` stable, `-ngl 9` always broken across many attempts.

### Suspected area
A scale-dependent CUDA path in the qwen4exp hybrid memory / QSA indexer (the recently refactored `llama_memory_hybrid_idx`), or a kernel launch path that corrupts silently once GPU-resident layers exceed ~8.

Happy to run any additional diagnostics or test candidate fixes on this hardware.

# [draft-mtp] Draft acceptance collapses to 0.0 under `-np N` with multi-ubatch batches — async `t_h_nextn` device→host copy race

## Summary

Self-speculative decoding (`--spec-type draft-mtp`) silently breaks under parallel slots (`-np 4`): as soon as concurrent requests carry long prompts (decode batches spanning multiple ubatches), draft acceptance drops from a healthy **0.48–0.85** to **exactly 0.00000** on all slots, generation falls back below no-MTP speed, and consumers of the endpoint see empty `message.content` completions (`finish_reason=stop` after a handful of `reasoning_content` tokens).

The trigger is a race between the **async device→host copy of `t_h_nextn`** (the MTP draft's input hidden states) and **any later graph that reuses the `t_h_nextn` extra buffer** — the next ubatch within the same `decode()`, or the next `decode()` call under `-np N` continuous batching. When the copy loses, the MTP draft conditions on NaN `h` rows, its logits go NaN, and every draft is rejected.

Verified at [`f5b9bd39b`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/f5b9bd39b) (build 10176), HIP backend. The same binary is correct at `-np 1` and for single-ubatch batches.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| llama.cpp | [`f5b9bd39b`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/f5b9bd39b) (b10176), HIP build, `AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151` |
| ROCm | 7.2.2 (pinned; gfx1151 native) |
| GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo, gfx1151), 256 GB unified |
| Model | [unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF) `UD-Q4_K_XL` + `mmproj-F16` (`qwen35` hybrid: Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention, embedded nextn/MTP layer) |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.17 |

Server flags:

```bash
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf --jinja \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9999 -ngl all -fit off -np 4 \
  -c 1048576 -n 131072 -b 1024 -ub 256 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 \
  --load-mode dio --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 -rea on \
  --reasoning-format deepseek --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0 --metrics
```

## Reproduction

Self-contained script (stdlib only, no client framework needed) — it fires 4 concurrent chat completions, each with a ~19k-token system prompt, and prints per-request `OK`/`EMPTY` plus finish reasons.

<details>
<summary>repro_mtp_np4.py (click to expand)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce the draft-mtp acceptance collapse under -np N concurrent load."""
import json, sys, threading, time, urllib.request

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:9999/v1/chat/completions"
N_CONC = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 4
TARGET_TOKENS = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 19000

unit = ("### Skill {i}: skill_{i} handles topic {i}. Steps: analyze, plan, "
        "execute, report. Constraints: verify outputs, cite sources.\n")
SYS = "You are an agent. Available skills:\n" + "".join(
    unit.format(i=i) for i in range(TARGET_TOKENS // 9))

def one(idx, results):
    body = {"model": "local_llm", "max_tokens": 1200, "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": SYS},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"[{idx}] Say hello and list what you can help with, one line."}]}
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1200))
        c = r["choices"][0]
        content = (c["message"].get("content") or "").strip()
        results.append((idx, "OK" if content else "EMPTY", c["finish_reason"],
                        r["usage"]["completion_tokens"], time.time() - t0))
    except Exception as e:
        results.append((idx, "ERROR", type(e).__name__, 0, time.time() - t0))

def round_test(round_n):
    results = []
    ts = [threading.Thread(target=one, args=(i, results)) for i in range(N_CONC)]
    for t in ts: t.start()
    for t in ts: t.join()
    empty = sum(1 for r in results if r[1] != "OK")
    for r in results:
        print(f"  round {round_n} req{r[0]}: {r[1]:5s} finish={r[2]:6s} ct={r[3]:5d} {r[4]:7.1f}s")
    print(f"  round {round_n}: empty {empty}/{N_CONC}")
    return empty

if __name__ == "__main__":
    total = sum(round_test(n + 1) for n in range(2))
    print(f"TOTAL empty: {total}/{2 * N_CONC}")
```

</details>

### Expected output on an affected build

Server log (`--metrics`, per slot, at task end):

```
slot print_timing: id 0 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 1 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 2 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 3 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
```

The same server, **sequential** single request on a cold slot:

```
slot print_timing: id 3 | draft acceptance = 0.57865 (  206 accepted /   356 generated), mean len = 3.31
```

Client side, affected requests return `finish_reason=stop` with empty content after a few reasoning tokens, or run away in reasoning until the token cap — both surface as "empty completion" to an agent/chat client.

### What does *not* trigger it

- `-np 4` with short prompts (single-ubatch batches): 0/12 failures over 3 rounds
- Long prompts processed **sequentially** (one slot active): healthy acceptance
- Warm prefix cache (prefill mostly cached): healthy
- `-np 1` with MTP: always healthy

→ the failure requires **concurrent** requests producing decode calls whose batches split across ubatches (long prompts), under multi-slot continuous batching.

## Root-cause analysis

Instrumentation adds two probes (patch inlined at the end of this section):

1. In `llama_context::decode()`'s per-ubatch `t_h_nextn` extraction: after the async copy, `ggml_backend_sched_synchronize()` then compare the **device tensor** contents (via synchronou

## Overview

DFlash2 adds two more modules compared to DFlash, grouped dynamic depthwise convolution and candidate selector. 

The formula is for reference. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`. `base` is the static kernel, `δ` is the dynamic part predicted from the input.`x` is divided into groups `g(c)` and `δ` is shared across a group. Another one is `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`. `A`/`B` are the codebooks for the predecessor and the candidate. This position's hidden is projected by `project(h)`to the same rank to multiply `A`. And `unary[c]` is the draft's own score for `c`.  

DFlash2 is enabled when the checkpoint is DFlash2; no need to use extra flag.

We evaled `Qwen3.8-27B` at `Q4_K_M`on Apple M5 Pro 64 GB. And the test data is first 8 problems of GSM8K.
Concurrency is set to 1 and temperature is 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20. We use default `xhigh` reasoning and set
2,048 maximum new tokens.

| Method | Draft quant | Block | Decode TPS | Decode speedup | Acceptance | Normal stops |
|--------|------|--:|------:|------:|-----:|---|
| Autoregressive | — | — | 10.42 | 1.00× | — | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | BF16 | 8 | 19.31 | 1.85× | 4.92 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q8_0 | 8 | 18.43 | 1.77× | 5.08 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q4_K_M | 8 | 18.89 | 1.81× | 5.03 | 8/8 |

items.body:
## Overview

Make `test-save-load-state` run across **all supported architectures** in ctest, instead of only the single `llama` arch (the downloaded `tinyllamas/stories15M` model).

- Add a `--models DIR` mode to `test-save-load-state` that runs the full save/load suite (tests 1-5) over every `*.gguf` in a directory, reporting per-model PASS/FAIL and exiting non-zero if any model fails.
- Replace the old single-model ctest with one that runs over all architectures using the existing `generate-models` fixture (`test-llama-archs -o <dir>`), mirroring how `test-recurrent-state-rollback` is wired. The single-model `-m` mode is preserved (still used by `ci/run.sh`).
- Bump the dummy-model training context from 128 to 256 in `test-llama-archs` so the per-sequence context (padded up to a multiple of 256) no longer exceeds `n_ctx_train` and triggers the "possible training context overflow" warning.

Running the suite over all architectures surfaced a few real save/load bugs, all fixed here:

- `context`: the on-device state seq copy required the write-side and read-side chunking to match 1:1, which diverged for non-contiguous sources; copy the flat write-side data into the read-side targets with a byte cursor across both tensor lists so the chunking no longer needs to match (fixes `memory buffer mismatch` on the gemma2 / gpt-oss / lfm2 device seq copy).
- `tests`: the dsv4 KV cache keeps per-sequence streams even in unified mode, so the baseline state save and the seq-copy loads now agree on `n_seq_max` (fixes the deepseek4 host seq-copy `n_stream` mismatch).
- `model`: `llm_graph_input_la` (minimax-01) stored a reference to the `llm_graph_params` temporary in `llama_context::process_ubatch`, which dangled on graph reuse and read destroyed stack memory in the state-load decode path; store a copy like the other graph input classes (fixes the minimax-01 state-load crash).
- `tests`: dummy DSA indexer heads now match the fused Lightning Indexer kernel (fixed NH=64) so the op runs on-device instead of falling back to CPU.

The full suite currently passes for all 109 generated architectures.

## Additional information

- The `test-save-load-state` ctest is now labeled `main` (it uses the generated dummy models, no download needed) and requires the `generate-models` fixture.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. pi:llama.cpp/Qwen3.8-27B
