## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR adds support for MTP (Multi Token Prediction) heads. I tested this on Qwen3.6 27B and Qwen3.6 35BA3B but in principle it should work for any MTP model. I've posted the detailed results below, but typically I see a steady-state acceptance of around 75% with 3 draft tokens, which is more than >2x speed-up over baseline. The design decisions I took to get to this stage are as follows:

- The MTP model is a separate model which loads from the same GGUF, the idea is that MTP should automatically start and we shouldn't need to distribute the MTP gguf separately but also it has it's own context/kv-cache etc. 
- I saw a problem in #18039 where the hidden features weren't propagated correctly across multiple ubatches, so this PR adds a separate "hook" for the MTP to consume after each `ubatch`
- The MTP speculative class is fairly trivial (although it does depend on #22400, but could work without it)

> [!TIP]
> MTP is compatible with Vision input and Tensor/Pipeline Parallelism

> [!NOTE]
> Prompt processing (PP) speed typically takes a negative hit when MTP is enabled mainly due to Device-To-Host (D2H) embedding transfers. It's something to be optimized in the future.

> [!NOTE]
> Parallel decoding with MTP is supported, but not fully optimized yet.

## Performance
 
A simple bench for testing various prompts is here: https://gist.github.com/am17an/228edfb84ed082aa88e3865d6fa27090. Posting the results below:

items.body:
## Overview

Fixes a regression after #24233, which restored HIP integrated GPU detection. On my AMD APU, this also made the ROCm host-buffer path available for HIP integrated GPUs. With that path enabled, prompt input appears corrupted: chat templates and system prompts can be ignored, and generated output becomes garbage.

This change keeps integrated GPU detection/reporting intact, but disables direct ROCm_Host compute on HIP integrated GPUs. The fix does not disable host-buffer exposure entirely, pinned buffers remain available to preserve functionality, while only the problematic direct compute path is blocked.

## Additional information

Tested locally on gfx1151 / RDNA3.5 APU with ROCm 7.14. The corrupted input/output issue is fixed with this patch.
The issue appeared in external harnesses like Pi and OpenCode. It can also be reproduced in the built-in web UI with a sufficiently large combined first input. For example, gemma-4-26B-A4B with 4676 tokens of context or more outputs `<unused49>` indefinitely. Other models can be way more resilient and their output starts by saying 'Based on the text provided, which appears to be a corrupted or "hallucinated" version of a Wikipedia article'.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistance to review and patch the relevant code. I tested and reviewed the final change myself.

items.title: Eval bug: Fit parameter for MiMo V2.5 GGUF is over-allocating ROCm device

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 9960 (a935fbffe)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000099 for Darwin arm64
```

Homebrew build, Metal backend.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.5.1, build 25F80), Apple M5, 24 GB unified memory.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Ornith-1.0-35B-UD-Q3_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 262144 -np 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa auto --port 8080
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a Metal allocation fails during init, the server logs the failure, logs that the
backend is unrecoverable, and then finishes starting up anyway. It prints `model loaded`,
binds the port, and answers `/health` with `{"status":"ok"}`. Every completion request
after that returns HTTP 500.

The per-request errors are reported correctly, so this isn't silent corruption. The
problem is that startup completes and `/health` reports ready for a process that can
never serve a request. Anything using `/health` as a readiness probe treats it as up.

I should say up front that `-ngl 99` disabled the auto-fit that would otherwise have
prevented this:

```
W common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99, abort
```

So the OOM itself is arguably my own fault. The part I think is still a bug is what
happens afterwards — the backend reports itself unrecoverable and the server starts
anyway.

Steps:

1. Pick a context size where the allocation cannot fit. On a 24 GB M5 the Metal device
   reports 18186 MiB, and this model at `-c 262144` needs 19005 MiB. llama.cpp's own
   memory breakdown says so directly:
   ```
   cmn  common_param:   - MTL0    : Apple M5 (18186 MiB, 18185 MiB free)
   load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 15897.19 MiB
   llama_kv_cache:       MTL0 KV buffer size =  2720.00 MiB
   common_memory_breakdown_print: |   - MTL0 (Apple M5)    | 18186 = ... + (19005 = 15897 +    2782 +     325) +         398 |
   ```
   At `-c 65536` the KV cache drops to ~680 MiB and it fits.
2. Start the server with the command line above.
3. 15 `Insufficient Memory` errors during init, then the backend declares itself
   unrecoverable and the decode fails.
4. Server prints `model loaded` and `listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080`.
5. `/health` → 200 `{"status":"ok"}`.
6. Any completion request → 500, and the OOM count roughly doubles.
7. Re-run at `-c 65536` and the same model starts and serves normally.

### What I'd expect

Exit non-zero at startup, the way other unrecoverable init failures already do — a
quantized V cache without flash attention returns `nullptr` and the server refuses to
start (b9960 `src/llama-context.cpp:3518`; on master the same check is at `:3602`,
reworded to `quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled`).

Failing that, `/health` should reflect it. It currently returns `{"status":"ok"}`
unconditionally once the model is marked loaded (b9960
`tools/server/server-context.cpp:4322`, master `:4448`); the only gate is the
server-state middleware, which fires solely on `!is_ready`.

### Relevant log output

Init (timestamps and log-level prefixes trimmed):

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
   ... 15 occurrences ...
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
cmn  common_conte: llama_decode() failed: -3
srv  llama_server: model loaded
srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

One completion request afterwards:

```
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
srv        decode: Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 2048, ret = -3
srv    send_error: task id = 0, error: Compute error.
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: Compute error.
```

Observed from the client:

```
$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/health
{"status":"ok"}
200

$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/completion \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"prompt":"int add(int a,int b){","n_predict":20,"temperature":0}'
{"error":{"code":500,"message":"Compute error.","type":"server_error"}}
500
```

`Insufficient Memory` count: 15 after init, 28 after one request, 29 including shutdown.

### Notes

Reproduced on b9960 (`a935fbffe`). I haven't run master, but both relevant paths look
unchanged there: the init probe still treats a failed `llama_decode` as non-fatal and
continues (master `common/common.cpp:1576`, b9960 `:1497`), and `/health` is still
unconditional. Worth confirming against master before acting on it.

One model, one machine, Metal only. Speculative decoding was not involved
(`speculative decoding not supported by this context` appears in the log).
items.title: Misc. bug: server reports "model loaded" and binds the port after a fatal Metal OOM during init; every request then 500s

items.body:
## Bug Description

GLM-5.2 crashes deterministically when attempting distributed inference across multiple DGX Spark nodes via ggml-rpc. The crash occurs during graph computation with `invalid data ptr` on the worker side and `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` abort on the orchestrator side. This appears analogous to #26424 (DeepSeek V4, Metal) but affects CUDA (sm_121).

## Environment

- **Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified memory each)
- **OS:** DGX OS (Ubuntu-based, aarch64)
- **CUDA:** sm_121 native build
- **llama.cpp:** master `5788b510a` (ggml 0.18.1), built with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON`
- **Network:** 1Gbit Ethernet between nodes
- **Model:** GLM-5.2 UD-IQ4_NL (also reproduced with UD-Q4_K_M), unsloth GGUF split files

## Setup

**Workers (3 nodes):**

```
./build/bin/ggml-rpc-server -c --host 192.168.1.XXX --port 50052
```

**Orchestrator (1 node):**

```
./build/bin/llama-server \
  -m ~/models/gguf/glm-5.2/UD-IQ4_NL/GLM-5.2-UD-IQ4_NL-00001-of-00009.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -ngl 999 -c 4096 \
  --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 \
  --rpc 192.168.1.121:50052,192.168.1.111:50052,192.168.1.128:50052
```

## Expected Behavior

Model loads across 4 nodes and serves inference (works with Gemma-4-26B, Qwen3.6-35B, Mistral-Small-3.2 on identical setup).

## Actual Behavior

Weights distribute successfully (~113GB cache per worker), but crashes during graph_compute:

**Worker output:**

[create_node] invalid data ptr[graph_compute] failed to create graph node 30 (id=197768091778640)
Client connection closed

**Orchestrator output:**

ggml-rpc.cpp:519: Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)

Stack trace: `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` → `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` → `ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async` → `llama_context::graph_compute` → `llama_context::decode` (during `common_init_from_params`).

## Reproducibility

- 100% deterministic — same worker, same graph node (30)
- Reproduced with UD-IQ4_NL (~348GB) and UD-Q4_K_M (~434GB)
- Reproduced with `-c 4096` and `-c 131072`
- Reproduced with and without `--no-warmup`
- All 4 nodes on identical commit (`5788b510a`, fresh pull)

## What Works

- Single-node llama.cpp on same hardware (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral)
- 2-node llama.cpp RPC with smaller models (Gemma-4-26B, ~51.8 tok/s)
- GLM-5.2 on single-node (4×RTX 6000, Ollama, Note: Different machine! But same model GLM 5.2 UD-IQ4_NL)

## Related

- #26424 — DeepSeek V4 Flash RPC crash (Metal, similar MoE/MLA architecture)
- GLM-5.2 uses IndexShare and MTP/NextN layers — likely unsupported ops in RPC graph distribution

## Logs

Full orchestrator and worker terminal output, dmesg are attached.

[glm-rpc-orch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708516/glm-rpc-orch.log)

[glm-rpc-worker3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708521/glm-rpc-worker3.log)

[glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708525/glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log)

items.body: This PR adds a new `--numa mirror` option which mirrors model weights to each Numa node on the system, and uses a thread-local var in the OMP threadpool to select the correct mirror copy local to the thread at runtime, to eliminate cross-socket traffic. Build instructions: ``` apt-get update apt-get install -y libnuma-dev libgomp1 cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-march=native" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-march=native" -DGGML_OPENMP=ON cmake --build build --parallel ``` To test: ```bash # No mirroring: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf # Numa mirroring of model weights to every node: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --numa mirror ``` Test system is a two-socket Xeon 6238R Cascade Lake, with 768GB of DDR4-2933 (6 channels per socket). Without `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ./.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 20.99 ± 0.01 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 1.91 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` With `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m . /.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf --numa mirror | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 21.36 ± 0.11 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 2.70 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` Intel PCM tool during mirror inference showing both sockets using local mem: There's still a bit of cross-socket traffic (5%) because only model weights are mirrored, not tensors created at inference time. I'll play with that, maybe mirroring those aggressively will help too, or maybe not. Right now anything created at inference time just gets set to live on Node 0.

items.body:
## Overview

**cuda: fuse MoE weighted expert reduction**

Fuses the MoE expert-combine tail on the CUDA backend into one reduction kernel, removing the intermediate tensor traffic between its stages.

After `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID`, the combine is a per-expert scale/weight multiply plus an ordered left-to-right `VIEW`+`ADD` chain that sums the `k = n_expert_used` experts. Those are logical nodes: the backend already fuses consecutive MULs/ADDs, so for the common top-k = 8 case it runs as **two physical `k_bin_bcast` kernels** (fused two-MUL + fused seven-ADD) with the full weighted-expert tensor `[n_embd, k, n_tokens]` written out and read back between them. This PR replaces that with **one kernel** that reads each expert row once and writes the `[n_embd, n_tokens]` result once:

```
dst[t,c] = sum_e ((experts[t,e,c] * expert_scale[t,e]) * weight[t,e])
```

The sum keeps the original left-to-right order. **The primary benefit is reduced global-memory traffic** (the eliminated intermediate tensor)

**Matching** is purely structural (op / shape / stride / view offset / add-chain / closure / aliasing) — never the quant or model. Two shapes: short (`experts * router_weight`) and long (`(experts * expert_scale) * router_weight`). The long form appears whenever a per-expert broadcast scale is applied before the router weight (e.g. the NVFP4 `scale_2` output scale, but the same graph slot can carry other scales); the matcher keys only on that second MUL's presence.

**Kernels:** unrolled templates for `k = 2..8`, one runtime-`k` kernel for `k = 9..15`, a `float4` path when `n_embd % 4 == 0` and aligned (scalar fallback), and an optional per-expert scale via a template flag. The `k <= 15` cap is `ggml_can_fuse_subgraph`'s 31-node limit on the long form (`2*k + 1 <= 31`); larger `n_expert_used` falls back.

**Correctness:** full-model WikiText-2 perplexity is unchanged (**5.8857 ± 0.03661**, on vs off) and `test-backend-ops` passes; the reduction keeps the original left-to-right order. Guards: `weights`/`expert_scale` are copied to scratch when they overlap `dst` (read while writing `dst`); fusion is skipped when `experts` overlaps `dst`; view offsets/strides and the add-chain are validated before fusing.

**Fallback / kill switch:** any unsupported top-k or failed structural/layout/closure/alias check leaves the graph unchanged and runs the per-op path. Enabled by default; `GGML_CUDA_MOE_WEIGHTED_REDUCTION=0` forces the reference path.

## Additional information


**Performance** — prefill `t/s`, default-ON vs `=0`, same binary, mean-vs-mean:

| Hardware | Model | Quant | pp2048 | pp8192 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +3.6% | +3.6% |
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Q4_K_M | +4.1% | +3.9% |
| RTX 5090 | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | NVFP4 | +4.3% | +4.3% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +5.4% | +5.4% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | Q4_K_M | +7.1% | +6.2% |

**Testing** (both modes, same binary): `test-backend-ops` **13,178/13,178** pass; CTest **42/42** pass; CPU-vs-CUDA compared; WikiText-2 PPL identical **5.8857 ± 0.03661**; `llama-cli` output unchanged. CUDA backend only; no changes to weights or numerics.

### Name and Version

### Description

I'm observing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF with DSpark speculative decoding enabled. After each PP+TG (prefill + generate) cycle, VRAM usage increases by approximately **10 MB**, and this accumulation continues until the process eventually runs out of memory (OOM).

This issue does **not** occur with:
- Step 3.7 + DSpark
- Qwen3.8-27B + DSpark

Both of the above maintain stable VRAM usage across multiple cycles.

### Environment
- Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731 version) GGUF + DSpark
- Framework: llama.cpp
- Issue: VRAM leak, ~10 MB per PP+TG cycle

### Suspected Root Cause

I suspect this is a **Draft KV Cache leak** specific to the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 model when used with DSpark. Specifically:

1. **KV cache positions** are written during every draft step but are **never compacted or properly reclaimed**, leading to continuous VRAM growth[reference:0]. A similar issue has been reported in related forks where "positions are written every tree step but never compacted," causing OOM under sustained traffic[reference:1].

2. **DSpark draft KV-cache group poisoning**: The DSpark draft model's KV cache is flagged as an "eagle group" (same as EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash)[reference:2]. The multi-group cache-hit lookup requires **every** KV-cache group to report a nonzero hit for cache reuse to succeed — any single group reporting zero short-circuits the entire request's lookup[reference:3].

3. **Sparse and discontinuous draft KV**: DSpark's draft-layer KV is recomputed from the target model's real hidden state every decode step, meaning it has **no cross-request reuse value**[reference:4]. Its stored blocks are sparse and discontinuous (e.g., `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]`)[reference:5], never satisfying the consecutive-hit window required for cache lookup[reference:6].

4. **"One-vote veto" effect**: This permanently poisons the AND-combination lookup for the entire request[reference:7], even though the model's real KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently have a working hit rate around 89%[reference:8]. As a result, the prefix caching mechanism is effectively disabled — every new request cannot reuse historical caches and must recompute and write new KV cache entries, causing VRAM to grow until exhaustion.

A similar fix has been proposed in vLLM where DSpark draft KV-cache groups are excluded from the cache-hit lookup poisoning mechanism[reference:9]. The same root cause likely applies to llama.cpp.

### Why Step 3.7 and Qwen3.8-27B Are Not Affected

These models likely have different DSpark implementations or KV cache structures that do **not** trigger this cache lookup conflict, allowing normal cache reuse and stable VRAM usage.

### Suggested Fix Direction

- Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache groups from the prefix caching lookup's "all-groups-must-hit" requirement, similar to the approach taken in vLLM PR #47891[reference:10].
- Alternatively, ensure DSpark draft KV cache positions are properly compacted or reclaimed after each generation cycle, as addressed in PR #23461 for draft/MTP resources.

### Additional Context

There have been related reports of DeepSeek V4 KV cache not being reclaimed on slot release, and DSpark-specific KV cache issues with offloading connectors[reference:13]. This may share a root cause with the hybrid-attention KV handling.

Please let me know if additional logs or reproduction steps would be helpful.

Thanks!

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ ./llama-cli --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 599, commit ad1de39)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Also observed on `4f31eed` and `6b4344e` (llama-server and llama-cli).

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

AMD Radeon 890M iGPU (gfx1150, RADV 26.1.2, Mesa), Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 32 GB LPDDR5 unified with 16 GiB firmware VRAM carve-out + 32 GiB GTT aperture. Debian 13, kernel 7.1.3. Kernel params include `ttm.pages_limit=8388608`.

### Models

`Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` + `mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf` (also crashed with GLM-OCR Q8 + mmproj; the specific model does not appear to matter - the crash happens at projector load).

### Command line

```bash
./llama-cli -m Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf \
  --image ui.png -p "What is the dialog title?" \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --temp 0.1 -no-cnv -n 30
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On this iGPU class, loading ANY mmproj-bearing model balloons GPU-side (GTT/TTM) allocations until the kernel's global OOM killer fires - **at projector load time, before any image is processed**. The process is killed within seconds; with other services resident, the OOM kill cascades (we observed two full-host watchdog resets before isolating it).

Clean single-process repro (no other GPU consumers; process wrapped with `choom -n 1000` so the OOM killer prefers it):

VmSize timeline from `/proc/<pid>/status` sampling:

```
0s VmSize=18184kB    VmRSS=7420kB
2s VmSize=4119524kB  VmRSS=150708kB
4s VmSize=32033928kB VmRSS=28652kB
```

Kernel (verbatim):

```
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,nodemask=(null),cpuset=...,global_oom,task_memcg=/system.slice/uit2-repro.scope,task=llama-cli,pid=77433,uid=0
Out of memory: Killed process 77433 (llama-cli) total-vm:33279112kB, anon-rss:4kB, file-rss:52kB, shmem-rss:0kB, UID:0 pgtables:1436kB oom_score_adj:1000
```

Note `total-vm: 33.2 GB` vs `anon-rss: 4 kB` - the memory is almost entirely driver-side, invisible to memory cgroups. We confirmed a `systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=6G` wrapper does **not** contain it (the OOM still fires as `CONSTRAINT_NONE` global; TTM/GTT kernel pages bypass the cgroup). With slower leak progression (CPU projector via `--no-mmproj-offload`) the driver log fills with repeated:

```
radv/amdgpu: Failed to allocate a buffer:
    size      : 1073741824 bytes
    alignment : 262144 bytes
    domains   : 4
```

(1 GiB GTT allocation attempts, `domains: 4`.)

For contrast: the identical artifacts + fixtures run cleanly on a discrete RTX 3090 (Vulkan not involved; CUDA) - this appears iGPU/GTT-specific.

Related prior art: #24626 (absolute per-device memory budget for `--fit` on UMA), #26447 (iGPU Vulkan device-lost at large contexts).

### Suggested fix / ask

Bound or chunk vision-context allocations on UMA/iGPU devices (or document a safe configuration for this class). As-is, every mmproj model is a potential host-crasher on Radeon iGPU systems.

---

*Disclosure: this report was assembled with AI assistance from measurements captured directly on the affected host (VmSize sampling script, kernel journal, RADV logs quoted verbatim above). All data points are from real runs, not generated.*

items.body:
### Name and Version

Environment

GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage), 32GB VRAM
OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-22-generic (xe driver)
oneAPI / Level Zero: Unified Runtime over Level-Zero V2, 20.2.0 [1.15.38308+1]
llama.cpp commit: 7dad2f1a17d65b5e2034c277125bc9f97573a779 (build b9660, 2026-06-15) for the SYCL repro; current master built locally with -DGGML_VULKAN=ON for the Vulkan comparison run
Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE), Q4_K_M, GGUF

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
SYCL launch command

llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --device SYCL0 \
  --ctx-size 32768 \
  --parallel 1 \
  --n-gpu-layers 99 \
  --jinja \
  --no-mmap \
  --reasoning-budget 0 --reasoning off

Env: UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1, GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_FLASH_ATTN=1, ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**Summary**

When the underlying GPU resets an engine mid-job (kernel-level xe driver "Timedout job" / "Engine reset" — see companion kernel-level report, link TBD), the SYCL backend never detects it. The server hangs forever, busy-waiting in sched_yield() inside the Level-Zero adapter, with /health still responding but /slots and /v1/chat/completions timing out indefinitely. There is no log output at the point of failure and no way to recover short of SIGKILL.

By contrast, on the same hardware, same model, same kind of underlying GPU reset, the Vulkan backend (ggml-vulkan / Mesa ANV) correctly detects device loss and the driver returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST to the application. (llama.cpp itself doesn't catch this exception today and the process aborts — see note at the end — but the detection is correct, which is the point of this report: SYCL has no equivalent detection at all.)

We believe the root cause of the GPU reset itself is upstream of llama.cpp (kernel drm/xe driver / GuC firmware level — filing separately here > https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/xe/kernel/-/work_items/8390), but regardless of that root cause, the SYCL backend hanging forever instead of failing visibly is a real gap worth closing on its own.

**What's been ruled out (from earlier isolated testing against the SYCL server)**

A tools array present without being invoked — no hang
A single forced tool call — no hang, sub-1s
Six simultaneous tool definitions with a genuine call — no hang, sub-1s
Context size from 32768 up to 262144 — hangs occur across the whole range, no clear correlation with size
One hang occurred at only ~2,048 prompt tokens, partway through generation (not during prefill)

These rule out grammar-constrained tool-call generation and large-context prefill as the trigger in isolation. Root cause now appears to be a GPU/kernel-level engine timeout under sustained load (separate report filed against drm/xe), reproducible regardless of which backend is driving the GPU — this report is scoped specifically to SYCL's lack of any detection/recovery path for that event.

Ask

Does the SYCL backend have (or could it have) any equivalent to Vulkan's device-loss detection — checking Level-Zero/SYCL exception state or a result code after a submission/wait, rather than spinning indefinitely?
At minimum, a bounded wait with a clear error/log output on timeout would let an operator's process supervisor recover automatically, instead of requiring an external watchdog to detect a silent hang via a secondary symptom (/slots timing out while /health stays fast).

Happy to test patches — this reproduces reliably under real agentic tool-calling load (multiple times per hour), so turnaround on verification should be fast.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

SYCL symptom: indefinite hang, no error

GPU power draw stays elevated (~98W) for the duration — confirms the GPU is actively spinning, not idle/crashed/waiting on I/O. gdb backtrace captured live while wedged, all threads idle except one spinning in the Level Zero adapter's USM memcpy path:

Thread 1 (LWP 25923) "llama-server":
#0  __GI_sched_yield ()
#1  ... libze_intel_gpu.so.1
...
#14 ggml_sycl_mul_mat_id(ggml_backend_sycl_context&, ggml_tensor*) () from libggml-sycl.so.0
#15 ggml_backend_sycl_graph_compute_impl(...)
#16 ggml_backend_sycl_graph_compute(...)
#17 ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async()
#18 llama_context::graph_compute(...)
#19 llama_context::process_ubatch(...)
#20 llama_context::decode(...)
#21 llama_decode()
#22 server_context_impl::update_slots()
#23 server_queue::start_loop(...)
#24 llama_server(...)

Notably: at the kernel level (dmesg -T), this exact PID (25923) has a corresponding entry showing the GPU driver itself reset the engine and declared the job timed out, before this backtrace was captured:

xe 0000:03:00.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs, logical_mask: 0x1, guc_id=2, state=0x249
xe 0000:03:00.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Timedout job: seqno=4294967200, lrc_seqno=4294967200, guc_id=2, flags=0x20 in llama-server [25923]

i.e., the SYCL/Level-Zero stack is busy-waiting on a GPU job the kernel has already torn down. It never finds out, and never times out on its own.

Vulkan Crash:
0.00.018.537 I log_info: verbosity = 3 (adjust with the `-lv N` CLI arg)
0.00.018.539 I device_info:
0.00.018.655 I   - Vulkan0 : AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (RADV RAPHAEL_MENDOCINO) (15732 MiB, 15695 MiB free)

### Name and Version

$ llama-cli --version
version: 0 (unknown)
built with IntelLLVM 2026.0.0 for Linux x86_6

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Hardware

Intel Core Ultra 7 258v + Intel Arc 140v

### Models

https://huggingface.co/OBLITERATUS/Gemma-4-12B-OBLITERATED both Q8 and Q5 (llama-quantize)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

First try with -ngl 99 -fit off -c 8192 -ub 256 (needed -fit off to get past an unrelated crash in the params-fit step): error 39 UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY, Error OP MUL_MAT (ggml-sycl.cpp:5177) with 27GB free. Added UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1: MUL_MAT now passes, but get error 40 UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES on FLASH_ATTN_EXT (same line).
Added -fa off: plain attention passes, and get error 40 on GLU, the fused FFN gate (same line).
Added GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_GRAPH=1: same error 40, just caught at a different site (ggml-sycl.cpp:3656, no op name printed).
Dropped -ub to 128: no change.

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Adds support for MiniMax-M3, a 60-layer / 128-expert MoE (3 dense + 57 MoE layers) using MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA): a GQA block-sparse attention where a lightweight per-GQA-group indexer scores the visible causal context, max-pools the scores into 128-token key blocks, and selects the top-16 blocks (the query's local block is always force-included). The main attention then runs only over the selected blocks (16*128 = 2048 KV per query), independent of context length, so decode attention cost stops scaling with context.

Implements the architecture from the MSA paper (arXiv:2606.13392v2) and follows the transformers reference (modular_minimax_m3_vl) for the indexer construction, selection semantics, and RoPE. MTP heads are not present in the released weights. Vision support is a separate PR (#25113).

Note that MSA is not an optional speed optimization, as the model is trained with sparse attention, so block selection is part of the model's semantics. Running dense attention is an out-of-distribution approximation that degrades output quality. The dense path exists only as a fallback for configurations that can't run MSA.

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

### Implementation
Batch and decode implement the same block-scoring and selection semantics, block scores bs = maxpool_128(idx_q*idx_k^T + causal mask) plus a host-provided local-force bias (large positive bias on each query's local block), ranked together for top-k. Selection is per GQA group (4 indexer heads, one per group, shared across the group's 16 query heads).

Within each stream, the four GQA groups are mapped onto the FA mask's ne[3] broadcast dimension and executed in one grouped flash-attention call.

- Batch (n_tokens_per_stream > 1, ie. prefill): a small CPU op turns block scores into a block-level 0/-inf mask, then the token-level expansion and combination with the causal mask happens on the GPU, and masked FA runs over the full cache views.

- Decode (1 token per stream): batched top_k on the GPU, index arithmetic expands block ids to flat (token, kv-head) row ids, one ggml_get_rows each gathers the selected K/V/mask, and FA runs over just the 2048 gathered tokens. 

Multi-stream (--parallel N) is supported whenever the KV cache is per-sequence (so kv_unified is false). In that configuration each stream's slots are then position-aligned, which MSA's slot-anchored block selection requires. 

The indexer also needs its own per-layer key cache. It is allocated F32 on the same backend buffer as the main K/V cache. Context-shift is not supported, since shifting would desynchronize the index cache.

### Requirements and fallbacks

- Flash attention required. Both batch and decode call ggml_flash_attn_ext directly and assume the non-transposed V layout that llama.cpp only provides with FA on. FA off uses dense build_attn (no sparsity) with a one-time warning that output quality may be degraded. 

- Unified KV cache with multiple sequences (--kv-unified + -np > 1) would silently break block anchoring so it also falls back to dense with a one-time warning. 

### Limitations

- Block selection is anchored to absolute KV slots. Erasing a prefix or middle of a sequence's history (llama_memory_seq_rm of a partial range) breaks selection silently. Removing whole sequences, trimming the suffix and reusing server slots is fine.
 
- Main KV cache: F16/BF16 are tested. Quantized KV-cache types are not yet validated.

### Quantization

Quants should keep the indexer projections (index_{q,k}_proj) at high precision(F32 ideally) since they drive block selection, so quant error there changes which blocks are read (a discrete retrieval loss), unlike a value projection. The cost is ~1 GB and these are some of the highest-value tensors in the model.

### Conversion

GGUFs must be converted with this branch and must keep the indexer tensors, weights with the indexers stripped will not work. 

### Performance

My tested config is expert-offload  bound.  MSA decode is essentially flat with context (7.7 tok/s at 5k -> 7.67 at 62k), prefill is roughly ~420-480 tok/s at 62k with -b and -ub 2048. Compute buffer at -ub 2048 / 62k ctx is ~4.6 GiB.

### How to test

As mentioned GGUFs converted with this PR are necessary, other's will fail to load. You can either convert one yourself, or you can use [this](https://huggingface.co/Serpen/Minimax-M3-MSA-GGUF/tree/main/Q4_K_M) Q4KM one (graciously provided by @AesSedai). 

CUDA build assumed (`-DGGML_CUDA=ON`), but in theory other backends with flash_attn_ext support for head-dim 128 should work (dense fallback otherwise), ROCm/HIP, Vulkan, Metal untested, reports welcome.

- Feed a ~4k and a ~30k+ prompt and generate. Decode throughput should stay roughly flat with context (fixed 2048-KV budget).

- Multi-stream: llama-server --parallel 2 (or 4) with concurrent requests of different prompt lengths.

### Credits

The initial MiniMax-M3 scaffolding was based on work by @danielhanchen. The sparse-attention indexer, the unified batch/decode MSA graphs, the KV-cache index handling, FA gating, and multi-stream support in this PR are new work.

## Requirements

<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES, Claude Opus was used to help write the initial test code, was used to help debug a speed related issue concerning the allocation of the indexer cache, helped prototype the architecture of the current unified MSA graph implementation, assisted writing validation code, and further helped debug performance issues (compute-buffer sizing, graph reuse). <!-- mention: YES / NO - if yes, describe how AI was used -->

### Name and Version

llama-b10639-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64
build: 5e6a37cb1 (10639)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64


### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0

or

llama-bench.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

On the ROCm backend, using any q5_0 KV cache type (either K or V) causes the compute graph to fragment from 2 splits into 34 splits. This pushes ~550-580 MiB of compute to the CPU host buffer and causes a ~68% regression in prompt processing throughput.

The issue is **specific to the ROCm backend**. The same build on Vulkan handles q5_0 KV cache correctly (2 splits, no regression). A fork of llama.cpp (build 11429) also handles it correctly on ROCm.

## Environment

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), 24 GB VRAM
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7900X
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL (16.34 GiB, 27.32 B params)
- Flash attention: enabled (`-fa 1`)

## Benchmark results

| KV Cache | graph splits | GPU compute buf | CPU compute buf | pp512 | tg128 |
|----------|:-----------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|:-----:|:-----:|
| q8_0 / q8_0 (ROCm) | 2 | 786.53 MiB | 161.53 MiB | 957.11 t/s | 37.53 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **551.28 MiB** | **300.10 t/s** | **27.96 t/s** |
| q5_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **580.53 MiB** | **302.49 t/s** | **28.39 t/s** |
| q8_0 / q8_0 (Vulkan, same build) | 2 | 270.53 MiB | 158.53 MiB | 771.39 t/s | 37.17 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (Vulkan, same build) | **2** | **295.03 MiB** | **183.03 MiB** | **762.60 t/s** | **37.01 t/s** |

The trigger is q5_0 in the KV cache. It does not matter whether it's used for K, V, or both. The broken GPU compute buffer size is identical (122.28 MiB) in both q8_0/q5_0 and q5_0/q5_0 cases, confirming it's the same code path.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build llama.cpp with ROCm support (or use a prebuilt ROCm binary)
2. Run `llama-bench -m <model.gguf> -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` (or `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0`)
3. Observe ~68% pp512 regression vs. q8_0/q8_0
4. Compare with the same build on Vulkan — no regression

## Expected behavior

q5_0 KV cache should perform similarly to q8_0 KV cache (within a small margin) when using flash attention, as it does on Vulkan and on the beellama fork (build 11429).

## Key log evidence

## Overview

DFlash2 adds two more modules compared to DFlash, grouped dynamic depthwise convolution and candidate selector. 

The formula is for reference. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`. `base` is the static kernel, `δ` is the dynamic part predicted from the input.`x` is divided into groups `g(c)` and `δ` is shared across a group. Another one is `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`. `A`/`B` are the codebooks for the predecessor and the candidate. This position's hidden is projected by `project(h)`to the same rank to multiply `A`. And `unary[c]` is the draft's own score for `c`.  

DFlash2 is enabled when the checkpoint is DFlash2; no need to use extra flag.

We evaled `Qwen3.8-27B` at `Q4_K_M`on Apple M5 Pro 64 GB. And the test data is first 8 problems of GSM8K.
Concurrency is set to 1 and temperature is 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20. We use default `xhigh` reasoning and set
2,048 maximum new tokens.

| Method | Draft quant | Block | Decode TPS | Decode speedup | Acceptance | Normal stops |
|--------|------|--:|------:|------:|-----:|---|
| Autoregressive | — | — | 10.42 | 1.00× | — | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | BF16 | 8 | 19.31 | 1.85× | 4.92 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q8_0 | 8 | 18.43 | 1.77× | 5.08 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q4_K_M | 8 | 18.89 | 1.81× | 5.03 | 8/8 |

## Overview

This PR implements Speculative Prefill, based on the ICML 2025 paper: *"Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation"* by Jingyu Liu, Beidi Chen, Ce Zhang ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02789), [GitHub](https://github.com/Jingyu6/speculative_prefill))

> [!NOTE]
> In contrast to speculative decoding, this is not lossless and can cause model performance degradation.

### Approach
In long-context inference, prefill TTFT scales quadratically with prompt length. Speculative prefill reduces this compute by using a smaller draft model to estimate which context tokens are most relevant to the query before evaluating the main target model:

1. **Draft lookahead**: The draft model prefills the prompt and generates $K$ lookahead tokens (default: 8).
2. **Attention extraction**: Softmax attention matrices (`kq_soft_max`) are captured during draft generation via an evaluation callback.
3. **Importance pooling & chunking**: Attention scores are smoothed with a 1D average-pooling filter ($W = 13$), max-reduced across heads/layers, and aggregated into contiguous chunks ($C = 32$).
4. **Sparse target prefill**: Only the top-$p$ fraction of chunks (plus BOS and prompt boundary tokens) are fed into the target model's KV cache.
5. **Generation**: The target model generates tokens autoregressively as normal.

### Benchmarks & Performance Evaluation

All benchmarks were run natively on Vulkan (`AMD Radeon 8060S`, RADV STRIX_HALO, 128 GiB unified LPDDR5X) using **Qwen3.8-27B (Q6_K_XL)** as target and **Qwen3.5-2B (Q4_K_XL)** as the primary draft model (unless noted otherwise).

#### 1. Draft Model Sizing & Context Scaling

**Draft Model Comparison** ($N = 1609$, $p = 0.15$):

| Configuration | Draft Eval Latency | Target Prefill | Total TTFT | Target Compute | End-to-End Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Baseline (27B alone)** | — | 5,300.8 ms | 5,300.8 ms | 1.00x | 1.00x |
| **27B Target + 27B Draft** | 5,836.5 ms | 789.2 ms | 7,597.2 ms | 6.72x faster | 0.70x (draft overhead) |
| **27B Target + 9B Draft** | 1,486.7 ms | 781.2 ms | 2,505.7 ms | 6.79x faster | 2.12x |
| **27B Target + 2B Draft** | 333.9 ms | 788.8 ms | 1,196.4 ms | 6.72x faster | **4.43x** |

**Context Length Scaling** (27B Target + 2B Draft):

| Keep Ratio ($p$) | $N = 803$ tokens | $N = 1607$ tokens | $N = 3212$ tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 2,882.0 ms (1.00x) | 5,324.6 ms (1.00x) | 10,787.7 ms (1.00x) |
| **50%** | 1,795.3 ms (1.61x) | 3,273.8 ms (1.63x) | 6,174.8 ms (1.75x) |
| **30%** | 1,026.3 ms (2.81x) | 2,045.3 ms (2.60x) | 4,004.3 ms (2.69x) |
| **15%** | **685.1 ms (4.21x)** | **1,615.7 ms (3.30x)** | **2,418.1 ms (4.46x)** |

#### 2. Synthetic Retrieval & QA Benchmarks

* **Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH)**: 100.0% retrieval accuracy across depths (20%, 50%, 80%) down to $p = 0.15$ (298 / 2,058 tokens kept, 1,798.0 ms vs 6,863.2 ms baseline, **3.82x speedup**).
* **RULER Suite**: 100.0% accuracy across Single Needle (25%, 75%), Multi-Key Retrieval, and Variable Tracking at $p = 0.15$ (**4.11x speedup**, 1,930.7 ms vs 7,925.4 ms). One miss at $p = 0.50$ (depth-75% needle; that row 75.0%).
* **LongBench QA Latency** (HotpotQA, Qasper, 2WikiMQA): Latency reduced from 4,821.5 ms baseline to 1,313.7 ms at $p = 0.15$ (**3.67x speedup**).

### Failure Mode Analysis & Operational Limits

Because speculative prefill drops tokens permanently from target prefill, accuracy drops when the token budget ($p \cdot N$) cannot contain all non-redundant evidence across separate chunks.

#### 1. Draft Model Comparison on Stress Tests (2B vs. 9B)

**High-Entropy Multi-Key Retrieval** (5 keys across 5 sections, ~1,100 tokens):

| Keep Ratio ($p$) | Tokens Kept | Qwen 2B Draft | Qwen 9B Draft | Observed Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 971 / 971 | **PASS (5/5)** | **PASS (5/5)** | All keys present and retrieved correctly |
| **50%** | 491 / 971 | FAIL (0/5) | FAIL (2/5) | Partial chunk pruning causes model hesitation/evasion |
| **30%** | 299 / 971 | **PASS (5/5)** | FAIL (2/5) | 2B focused on all 5 nodes; 9B diffused attention |
| **15%** | 140 / 971 | FAIL (0/5) | FAIL (3/5) | Budget allows ~4 chunks (5 needed) $\to$ information loss |
| **8%** | 76–98 / 971 | FAIL (2/5) | FAIL (1/5) | Severe pruning $\to$ both models hallucinate fake IDs |

**Distributed Summation** (Box A: 15 + Box B: 25 + Box C: 60 = 100):

| Keep Ratio ($p$) | Tokens Kept | Qwen 2B Draft | Qwen 9B Draft | Status / Observed Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 796 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — All 3 box chunks retained |
| **50%** | 412 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — All 3 box chunks retained |
| **30%** | 252 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — All 3 box chunks retained |
| **15%** | 125 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — Boundary + 3 box chunks fit in 125 tokens |
| **8%** | 61 / 796 | `40 units` | `77 units` | **FAIL** — Box C (`60`) pruned $\to$ silent partial calculation |

**Non-Parametric Multi-Hop QA** (Target Year: `2348`, 12 non-redundant documents):

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 473 / 473 | `2348` | `2348` | **PASS** — Both clue documents retained |
| **50%** | 249 / 473 | `2348` | Refusal / Evasion | **PASS (2B)** / **FAIL (9B)** — 9B lookahead diverted to distractor |
| **30%** | 153 / 473 | `2348` | `2348` | **PASS** — Both clue documents retained |

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

### Flash Attention (Intel Xe)

- New Vulkan shaders: single-phase prefill (`flash_attn_hdim64/96/128`) and two-phase split prefill/decode variants
- Pipelines keyed by `(head_dim, gqa_ratio)` for runtime dispatch across various GQA ratios without combinatorial pipeline proliferation
- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning
- Two-phase decode splits softmax reduction across subgroups; shared QK state copy (`fa_copy_qstate`) between prefill phases

### Performance (Panther Lake B390 + Windows OS)

## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

this adds several fixes for rpc and rocm related GPU paths additional tuning and fixes crashes, prefill issues and general compatibility. Fixes #26746

### Included changes relative to upstream

#### HIP, RPC and long-context routing

- Enables hipCUB for HIP top-k and argsort, including the distributed RPC execution
  path, so these operations remain GPU-capable on ROCm.
- Adds a gfx1151-local Lightning Indexer top-k specialization for 512, 1024 and 2048
  candidates up to 8192 score entries, avoiding the expensive generic device-wide sort
  during DeepSeek-V4 long-context prefill.
- Keeps the Lightning Indexer key cache in F16 when a quantized KV cache is selected,
  where required by the DeepSeek path.
- Resolves fused operations per layer and device instead of disabling an entire graph
  on a single ROCm/RPC backend mismatch; the default fallback remains unfused GPU work,
  not CPU work.
- Fixes the HIP MMVF dispatch for MoE LoRA `MUL_MAT_ID` tensors. Rank-1 LoRA-B
  expert matrices now use the existing general GPU fallback instead of entering an
  MMVF kernel which requires an even K dimension; this prevents RPC worker crashes
  with valid DeepSeek-V4 expert LoRA adapters.

#### Strix Halo compute tuning

- Adds RDNA3.5/gfx1151 kernel and launch tuning for MMQ, MMVQ, Q8 MoE and expert MMQ.
- Caches MMVQ Q8_1 activations and partitions MMQ waves across rows and columns.
- Adds AMD WMMA Lightning Indexer support and tuned tiled Flash Attention, including a
  fix for NaNs in the compacted-tile mask path.
- Tunes Gated Delta Net and adds quantized-KV Flash Attention support for Strix Halo.
- Extends the gfx1151 MMVQ selection to the relevant Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8 and MXFP4 decode
  types, including the Q6_K VDR=2 decode kernel.
- Keeps HIP integrated-GPU host-buffer handling safe.

#### DeepSeek-V4 and speculative decoding

- Makes the grouped output-projection input contiguous for small multi-token
  DeepSeek-V4 speculative batches.
- Uses matching MMVQ and Flash-Attention kernel configurations for decode and small
  speculative/MTP verification batches, preventing numerical divergence between the
  logits used for acceptance checks.
- Keeps fused DeepSeek-V4 HC and Gated Delta Net operations on devices that support
  them while safely falling back only for mismatching layers.

#### Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 and hybrid SSM models

- Fuses SSM gate/beta projections, the SSM convolution-output L2 norm, and the SSM
  pre-scan chain (convolution, L2 norm, gate/beta).
- Folds SSM convolution-input concatenation into QKV MMVQ and fuses paired MMVQ
  matmuls that share an activation.
- Caches graph-local Q8_1 matmul inputs, folds Q8_1 quantization into RMS norm and
  gating-MUL, and fuses a matmul-plus-add-through-view sequence.
- Folds MoE top-k weights into the down projection and fuses the shared-expert output
  chain.
- Fuses IMRoPE and set-rows for BF16 KV cache use, and aligns the attention-gate
  tensor-parallel split with attention-Q.

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

tested on a halo strix cluster setup (RPC, rocm 7.14).

## Requirements

rocm 7.14, hipcub-dev (build requirements)
ROCm/HIP with hipCUB, HIP/ROCm >= 6.1.
Build for gfx1151 (-DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151).

- AI usage disclosure: <!-- mention: YES / NO - if yes, describe how AI was used --> YES

OpenAI Codex GPT 5.6 Terra for tracing affected crash paths. Adding GPU fallback, instead of adding CPU fallback.

### Sources and provenance

- [@ggml-org](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) provides the upstream base. This
  branch is rebased on the exact upstream commit stated above.
- [@Patt92](https://github.com/Patt92/llama.cpp) maintains this integration branch and
  supplies the HIP RPC top-k/argsort patch, including the current HIP-only rank-1 MoE
  LoRA MMVF dispatch fix.
- [@Geramy](https://github.com/Geramy/llama.cpp) is the provenance for the original
  hipCUB/CUB-on-HIP top-k and argsort approach. Its useful HIP content was rebased
  into the Patt92 RPC patch; no older branch is required at build time.
- [@Nathanw1014](https://github.com/Nathanw1014/llama.cpp) supplies the selected
  Strix Halo/RDNA3.5 HIP tuning, DeepSeek-V4, Flash-Attention, MMQ/MMVQ and

items.title: ROCm/HIP: optimize Strix Halo inference, RPC and DeepSeek/Qwen paths

items.body:
## Summary

On a gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU, RDNA3.5) system with ROCm 7.2.4, the **HIP/ROCm** backend
produces corrupted output where the **Vulkan** backend, running the **same weights, the same
build, and byte-identical flags on the same machine**, is correct on every attempt.

Measured on three architectures. Two fail on HIP, with **different severity**; one is
unaffected:

| model | `general.architecture` | topology | Vulkan | HIP/ROCm |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct `Q4_K_M` | `llama` | dense | **16/16** @30,516 · 6/6 @1,616 | **0/16** @30,516 · **0/6 @1,616** |
| Qwen3.8-27B `UD-Q8_K_XL` | `qwen35` | dense | **16/16** @29,355 | **0/16** @29,355 · 6/6 @1,349 |
| Ling-3.0-flash `IQ4_XS` | `bailingmoe3` | 512-expert MoE | **16/16** @29,275 | **16/16** @29,275 |

(`@N` = prompt tokens. Each cell is 8 requests run twice; the repeat is deliberate, because a
single 8/8 is not enough to call a backend clean.)

Backend and binary path were read from `/proc/<pid>/exe` on **every** run, not inferred from
the launcher — an earlier "Vulkan" result in this investigation turned out to be the HIP server
still answering after a boot script silently failed.

### Two severities, deliberately not merged

- **`llama` is broken outright on HIP** — at *every* depth tested, including a 1,616-token
  prompt. Output is degenerate word salad:
  `'for 4\n<|contextual background\nline keep track\nTheater in line while mind the material and context in'`
  The same model, flags and template on Vulkan is 6/6 shallow and 16/16 at 30,516 tokens, so
  this is not a configuration error.
- **`qwen35` is correct at shallow depth and fails past roughly 29k tokens** when the request
  also carries a moderately large tool array. Output stays fluent and well-formed; the model
  confidently mis-states **its own tool list**. With an array of `read_file`, `tool_00` …
  `tool_15`:

  > I don't have a `read_file` tool available in my current toolset. The tools I have access to
  > are `tool_01` through `tool_15`, which are placeholder utilities that accept a single string
  > argument. None of them are file-reading tools.

  It has read the placeholders' *descriptions* correctly while losing the entries at the **head**
  of the array. Other samples invented tool names absent from the request entirely, or ran to
  the token limit emitting `finish_reason: "length"` with empty content and no tool call.

Whether these are one defect with severity varying by model, or two, is **not established here**.

### Hypothesis, on a single data point — please treat as a lead, not a finding

The two failing models are **dense**; the one that passes is a **512-expert MoE**. Dense and
MoE matmuls take different paths (`mul_mat` vs `mul_mat_id`), which may be where to look. This
rests on **one** MoE observation and no second MoE was tested. It is offered as a starting
point, not a claim.

## Still present on current master

Reproduced on stock upstream **`b21e4de74567f5eef213765c9476a843c2e43f0d`** — `master`
re-fetched immediately before building — from a clean detached worktree with no local patches,
built for gfx1151 with ROCm 7.2.4.

The same result holds on **`3a653fea932e`** (12 days earlier). **The two SHAs agreeing is
expected rather than corroborating:** there are 7 commits between them and **none touch
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda` or `ggml/src/ggml-hip`**, so it simply means nothing has been attempted on
this code path in that window. It should not be read as an independent second confirmation.

### It is not `e79e4bf66` — please do not close this as a duplicate of that commit

`e79e4bf66` ("ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations", #26696) is **present in every
tested tree and does not fix this.** It is the obvious suspect and it matched on every checkable
detail:

- its message describes `-fassociative-math` reassociating FP reductions and *"can flip greedy
  argmax on **RDNA3.5** (e.g. **MTP speculative decode** diverging from the non-speculative
  baseline)"*;
- the hardware here is gfx1151, which **is** RDNA3.5;
- one of the failing workloads runs `--spec-type draft-mtp`;
- an older tree used here still carries the flag at `ggml/src/ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt:130`,
  while every tree tested above does not.

With that flag already removed, the defect reproduces at 0/16. This is either a second,
independent problem or the same one with another cause.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | stock `b21e4de74567f`; also reproduced on `3a653fea932e` |
| GPU | gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU), 128 GB unified memory |
| ROCm | 7.2.4 (hipcc 7.2.53211-97f5574fe2, AMD clang 22.0.0git roc-7.2.4) |
| OS | Linux |
| Build flags | `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/lib/llvm/bin/clang++ -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=ON` |

## Server flags — identical on both backends, only the binary differs

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on
--ctx-size 65536 --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--parallel 1 --threads 16
--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0
--ctx-checkpoints 32 --checkpoint-min-step 8192
--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
--jinja        # each model uses its own embedded chat template
```

Verified byte-identical with `diff` between the two launcher files; the only differences are a
comment header, the slot-save path, and the binary path.

## Causes eliminated, each by changing ONE variable

Listed so nobody spends replies asking. Every row was measured; all remained failing:

| varied | result |
|---|---|
| Context depth | not the cause — 1 tool at 36,335 tokens is 5/5 correct, *longer* than the failing case |
| Tool count | not the cause — 17 tools at 1,349 tokens is 6/6 correct |
| Total prompt length | not the cause — see the 36,335-token row above |
| KV cache type | `q4_0`, `q8_0`, `f16` all fail |
| Flash attention | `--flash-attn off` still fails; it changes the failure *mode*, not the failure. (Note `--flash-attn off`

## Overview

disable FA GQA packing for multi-token queries

## Additional information

Speculative verify runs flash attention with neq1 > 1 (several query tokens at once). Vulkan’s GQA-packed FA path treated N <= 8 as “use GQA packing,” then overwrote N with gqa_ratio and remapped workgroups as if there were a single query token. That is only valid for single-token decode, so multi-token parallel verify disagreed with sequential FA and drifted logits (e.g. wrong-draft windows with n_win >= 4)

Related to #25618

## Validation

Setup1: Qwen3-8B Q4 + DSpark n_max=7 using vulkan on strix halo
Before Fix: Diverging output as compared to just vanilla model at same seed & zero temp
After Fix: Exact Match

Setup2: Gemma-4 Q4 + MTP n_max=4
Result: Still diverging, there are other bugs as well that I plan to handle in other PRs. See #25618

## Overview

This is an attempt to reduce the amount of matrix multiplication shaders we need by using a spec constant for the type of the A input, similar to how it works for KV cache types in Flash Attention. Additionally, it replaces the current static s, m and l shapes with a map and allows improved tuning through more shapes and a custom selection function, which should help with work like #24407.

It's still draft because currently it regresses Nvidia, because for dynamic type selection all quants with shared memory requirements must also be available. I thought it would eliminate those that are not used, this works on AMD, but not on Nvidia. @jeffbolznv Do you know why? There are other ways to resolve this, hopefully I'll find something that works.

items.body:
### Summary

On **gfx1151 (Strix Halo / Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Windows 11)** the **HIP backend silently corrupts inference of Qwen3.5-27B** (hybrid Gated-DeltaNet architecture, tested as VLM with mmproj): the **oldest part of the context is consistently lost** while output stays fluent and deterministic. The **Vulkan backend at the identical commit is correct**. We ran an extensive exclusion campaign (details below); every individually testable component passes, so the defect appears to live at graph-composition level of the GDN block on HIP.

### Environment

- HW: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S iGPU (**gfx1151**), 128 GB unified memory
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 26200, Adrenalin driver 32.0.31035.1003
- ROCm runtime: TheRock `therock-dist-windows-gfx1151-7.14.0rc3` (also reproduced with a different ROCm 7.x runtime DLL set)
- llama.cpp: official release zips `llama-b10453-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip` **and** `llama-b10582-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip`, **and** a self-built b10582 (e85caa81e) with the TheRock clang toolchain — **all three affected identically**
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (unsloth GGUF) + mmproj BF16
- Counter-checks: **Vulkan builds of the very same commits (b10453 and b10582) are correct**; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (pure attention, no GDN) is correct on the same HIP builds

### Reproduction (deterministic, temp 0)

Generate a synthetic 4-panel test image (no external assets needed):

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
W,H=660,640; img=Image.new('RGB',(W,H),'white'); d=ImageDraw.Draw(img)
try: fb=ImageFont.truetype('arialbd.ttf',20); fs=ImageFont.truetype('arial.ttf',14)
except: fb=fs=ImageFont.load_default()
for x,y,t,c in [(0,0,'Alpha Risk','Risk from parallel shifts of the reference rate.'),
                (330,0,'Beta Risk','Risk from non-parallel curve changes.'),
                (0,320,'Gamma Risk','Risk from embedded options, e.g. early repayment.'),
                (330,320,'Delta Risk','Risk from hedging with different rate indices.')]:
    d.rectangle([x+2,y+2,x+328,y+318],outline='black',width=2)
    d.ellipse([x+12,y+16,x+22,y+26],fill='black'); d.text((x+30,y+12),t,fill='black',font=fb)
    d.rectangle([x+30,y+50,x+290,y+200],outline='gray')
    if 'Gamma' in t:
        for i,bh in enumerate([60,90,130,100,80]): d.rectangle([x+50+i*45,y+195-bh,x+80+i*45,y+195],fill='gray')
    else: d.line([(x+40+i*25,y+190-int(12*(i**1.2))) for i in range(10)],fill='black',width=2)
    d.text((x+30,y+215),c,fill='black',font=fs)
img.save('synthetic_4panel.png')
```

```
llama-mtmd-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-BF16.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 4096 --temp 0 --seed 42 --image synthetic_4panel.png \
  -p "List ALL bold bullet headings in this image, top-left to bottom-right. Only the list."
```

- **HIP (gfx1151):** `['Beta Risk', 'Gamma Risk', 'Delta Risk']` — **top-left "Alpha Risk" (the oldest image tokens in raster order) is dropped**
- **Vulkan (same commit, same machine):** all four headings
- With a denser real-world 4-panel document scan the effect is stronger: HIP loses the entire upper half (0/4 headings) while Vulkan stays 4/4; flipping the image vertically "heals" it (the previously-top content becomes the newest tokens), which points at recency-position rather than image-coordinates.

### Exclusion campaign (everything below was tested on the same machine)

| Hypothesis | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime-DLL mismatch | official b10453 binary + clean matching TheRock 7.14 runtime | still wrong |
| Code regression / fix between builds | b10453 **and** b10582 built for **Vulkan** (same commits) | both correct → code exonerated |
| Toolchain | self-built HIP b10582 (TheRock clang) | reproduces official zips exactly |
| mtmd preprocessing | top-half crop alone is read fine; full preprocessing chain reviewed | exonerated |
| hipGraphs | `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | still wrong |
| ubatch state handoff | `-ub 128 / 512 / 8192` (whole prompt in one ubatch) | still wrong |
| GATED_DELTA_NET kernel | `test-backend-ops -o GATED_DELTA_NET`, **including added prefill-scale cases** (n_seq_tokens 64/256/1024 at the real 32x128 geometry, v_repeat 2, and K=4/8 snapshot slots — upstream currently tests max n_seq_tokens=4 and K>1 only with tiny shapes) | **43/43 pass at NMSE 1e-7** |
| Any other op in the graph | per-op sweep: SSM_CONV, CUMSUM, L2_NORM, RMS_NORM, EXP, SIGMOID, SOFT_MAX, ADD, MUL, SCALE, CPY, SET_ROWS, GET_ROWS, ROPE, FLASH_ATTN_EXT, GLU, SUM_ROWS, TRI, MUL_MAT_ID, MUL_MAT (>6400 cases total) | all pass |

Test-case additions we used (happy to open a PR):

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

# ROCm/HIP Backend: Native gfx1031 (RX 6700 XT) Support + Flash-Attention Assert Fix

## TL;DR

On RDNA2 (gfx1031 / RX 6700 XT), the ROCm/HIP backend currently requires **two workarounds** to become usable for long-context inference: a runtime GFX-version override (masquerading as gfx1030) and a manual source patch that silences a flash-attention assert of unknown correctness impact. Once running, ROCm delivers a **~85% prefill speedup** over Vulkan at 8K context, translating to a **~23% net wall-clock win** over a full prefill+decode cycle — despite a 15–18% decode-speed deficit. This makes ROCm the clearly superior backend for this hardware *if* the build/runtime friction is resolved. This report asks for two specific fixes; a separate, still-in-progress investigation into a decode-time sampler gap (`TOP_K` unsupported on ROCm in `llama-server`) will be filed independently once sufficient data is collected.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (gfx1031, RDNA2, Navi22) |
| CPU | Intel Core i5-11400F |
| RAM | 16GB DDR4 @ 3200 MT/s (XMP) |
| OS | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS |
| llama.cpp commit | `0a50d9909` (build 10108) |
| ROCm version | 7.1.52801-9999 |
| Compiler | clang / hipcc (`CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang`, `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=hipcc`) |

GPU tuned via LACT (Performance level: Manual, Power Profile: Compute, power limit 182/223W, core voltage offset -90mV, VRAM 1900MHz) — same tuning applied for both backends under test, no backend-specific tuning.

## Why this matters (benchmark data)

Model: `gemma-4-12b-it-IQ4_NL.gguf` (6.24 GiB, 11.91B params). Test: `llama-bench --n-prompt 8192 --n-gen 512 --batch-size 1024 --ubatch-size 1024 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --n-gpu-layers 99 --flash-attn on`. 3 runs per backend, both with flash-attention enabled and identical batch/cache settings — the only variable changed is the backend.

| Backend | pp8192 (t/s) | tg512 (t/s) |
|---|---|---|
| ROCm (avg of 3) | 653.9 | 34.60 |
| Vulkan (avg of 3) | 354.4 | 40.92 |
| **Δ** | **+84.5%** | **-15.4%** |

Converting to wall-clock for a full 8192-prefill + 512-generate cycle:

| Backend | Prefill time | Decode time | **Total** |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROCm | 12.5s | 14.8s | **27.3s** |
| Vulkan | 23.1s | 12.5s | **35.6s** |

**ROCm wins net wall-clock by ~23%**, despite losing on raw decode throughput, because prefill dominates the cycle at this context depth. The crossover point (below which Vulkan is net-faster) is roughly ~1,760 prompt tokens — meaning ROCm is the better backend for effectively all long-context workloads on this hardware, once it can be built and run without manual intervention.

*(Decode-side deficit is currently under separate investigation — a `TOP_K` sampler op is reported unsupported on the ROCm device in `llama-server`, but this has not yet been confirmed as the cause of the `llama-bench` decode gap, since `llama-bench` explicitly excludes sampling time from its measurements. That will be reported separately once isolated.)*

## Issue 1 — gfx1031 has no working native target; requires runtime override

**Attempted:** building with `-DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1031 -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1031` directly.
**Result:** fails to run correctly on this hardware without the runtime workaround below — confirmed, not assumed.

**Current workaround:**
```bash
cmake -S ~/Projects/llama2 -B ~/Projects/llama2/build-rocm \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=hipcc \
  -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1030 -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1030
cmake --build ~/Projects/llama2/build-rocm -j"$(nproc)"

# at runtime, gfx1031 must masquerade as gfx1030:
HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0 ./build-rocm/bin/llama-bench ...
```

**Ask:** native `gfx1031` target support that runs correctly without `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION`, so RX 6600/6700-series (Navi22) users don't need to build for a neighboring architecture and override the GFX version at runtime.

## Issue 2 — Flash-attention assert crash on this backend/target combo

**Location:** `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-common.cuh` — `GGML_ASSERT(max_blocks_per_sm > 0);`

**Current workaround (patches source, correctness impact unknown):**
```bash
sed -i 's/GGML_ASSERT(max_blocks_per_sm > 0);/if (max_blocks_per_sm <= 0) { max_blocks_per_sm = 1; }/g' \
  ~/Projects/llama2/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-common.cuh
```

**Why this can't just stay disabled:** turning flash-attention off is not a viable fallback for this use case —

## Summary

Under parallel mixed load (`-np 4 --kv-unified`), `llama-server` on an **integrated HIP GPU** (Strix Halo / gfx1151, 128 GB UMA) returns **complete responses that verbatim belong to a different, earlier request**. A large-prompt request receives, as its entire response, the literal answer text of a short request from an earlier round. We also observed a **chimeric** response fusing tokens of two different requests' expected outputs.

**Bisected to a single commit: c7d87229 "ggml-cuda : restore prop.integrated on HIP builds" (#24233).**

| build | result (validated responses, nonce-checked) |
|---|---|
| 505b1ed1 (parent window start) | clean — 0 violations / 168 |
| 5839ba35 (= parent of c7d87229) | clean — 0 / 36 |
| **c7d87229** | **cross-request replays: 3 hard / 36** |
| e8f19cc0 (window end) | cross-request replays: 7 hard + 1 chimera / 96 |

The same harness against **CPU builds** of both window endpoints shows no build-dependent difference (model-compliance noise only) — consistent with the culprit being the HIP integrated-memory path. This presumably explains why it went unnoticed: discrete GPUs are unaffected; it needs an **integrated** AMD GPU (`prop.integrated == 1`), multiple slots and concurrent mixed traffic.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), gfx1151, 128 GB unified memory, ROCm 7.14, Ubuntu 24.04
- Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++` (Release)
- Server: `llama-server -m <model> -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 4 --kv-unified --jinja --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE (Q4-class quant). First hit this in production behind LocalAI (same symptom after its vendored-llama.cpp bump crossed this commit); reproducing on vanilla `llama-server` rules the wrapper out.

## Reproduction

Load pattern per round (~30 s, script below): (B) short "repeat exactly this code: <nonce>" request → (C) large-prompt (~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce in the first line → (D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain). Every response is validated to contain its **own** nonce and no nonce of an **earlier** request.

On affected builds the round-N large-prompt request receives a literal foreign nonce as its complete response, typically from a round-(N−1) burst request. Verbatim from run logs at e8f19cc0:

```
R4/C got='pd-20260722-115649-3-d1'      (expected: reply echoing pc-...-4-c + a summary)
R5/C got='pd-20260722-115649-4-d2'
R6/C got='pd-20260722-115649-1-d1'
R7/C got='pd-20260722-115649-6-d1'
R8/C got='pd-20260722-115649-7-d1'
R3/C got='<!-- run:pc-20260722-115649-2-d0 -->'   <-- chimera: pc-...-2 stem fused with a -d0 burst suffix
```

In production we additionally observed: a poisoned slot re-serving its stored answer to unrelated requests **20+ minutes later** (the victim's `usage` then reports the foreign request's token counts), and occasional degeneration into repeated single characters (`/////...`).

## Overview
This PR optimizes Vulkan prompt processing performance specifically for K-quant formats including Q4_K, Q5_K and Q6_K.

## vulkan: transpose A-matrix data layout for K-quant mul_mat

*Last updated: 2026-06-08*

### What this does

`mul_mat` reads the quantized weight (matrix A) with a non-contiguous, stride-based pattern. With K-quant blocks (~144–176 bytes) this wastes L1. This PR repacks the weight from `[row, k_block]` to `[k_block, row]` once at upload, so the shader reads A sequentially.

- Types: **Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_1**.
- Repacked once in `set_tensor`; `get_tensor` reverses it, so host-visible layout is unchanged.
- Covers dense and MoE expert weights (`MUL_MAT_ID`); token embedding stays in original layout.
- Toggle: `GGML_VK_NO_TRANSPOSE_A=1`.

### Where it applies

Enabled **only on the CM1 (`VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix`) MUL_MAT / MUL_MAT_ID path** — the `_transa` pipelines exist only in that branch. `set_tensor` repacks only when `ggml_vk_has_transa_pipeline(dtype)` is true.

| Path | Behavior |
|---|---|
| CM1 (`VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix`) | repacked → speedup |
| CM2 (`VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2`) | no `_transa` pipeline → no repack → correct, no speedup (CM2 already recovers most of this via larger tiles) |
| No coopmat | same as CM2 |

Ops that don't understand the layout (`GET_ROWS`, `FLASH_ATTN_EXT`, `CPY`) call `ensure_non_transposed(src)` at dispatch — a zero-cost set lookup that reverts on demand. In real inference it never fires (embedding isn't transposed, KV cache is f16); it only triggers under `test-backend-ops`.

### Use cases

- **Dense K-quant, prompt processing** — main target: +5–8% (Q4_K), up to +11–15% (Q6_K).
- **MoE, prompt processing** — smaller (+2–3%); sub-512 per-expert batch + routing dilutes it.
- **Token generation** — flat ±1% (mat-vec path untouched).
- **`--no-mmap`** — correct, no speedup: the repack needs the whole tensor at once, but `--no-mmap` uploads in round-byte chunks that can split a quant block, so it falls back to the standard pipeline.

### How to A/B test

Same binary, env-var toggle, skip TG (`-n 0`):

```bash
# ON (default)
llama-bench -m model.gguf -ngl 99 -p 512,1024,2048 -n 0 -r 5
# OFF
GGML_VK_NO_TRANSPOSE_A=1 llama-bench -m model.gguf -ngl 99 -p 512,1024,2048 -n 0 -r 5
```

Add `--no-mmap` to both to check that path (expect parity). On an NVIDIA CM2 device, set `GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT2=1` to force the CM1 path.

### Benchmarks (pp512, ON vs OFF, `-r 5`)

| Device | Model | OFF | ON | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R9700 (RDNA4) | Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M | 2936 | 3106 | +5.8% |
| R9700 | Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M | 2554 | 2758 | +8.0% |
| R9700 | Gemma-4 E4B Q6_K | 4022 | 4475 | +11.3% |
| R9700 | Gemma4 26B.A4B Q4_K_M (MoE) | 3715 | 3825 | +3.0% |
| RTX 4080 (CM1) | Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M | 5068 | 5225 | +3.1% |

Standalone MUL_MAT (m=4096, n=512, k=14336): Q4_K +3.5%, Q5_K +3.0%, **Q6_K +15.2%** (heavier per-block dequant → bigger win). RTX 4080 CM1 also +6.1% / +5.3% at pp1024 / pp2048. Community: 780M dense Qwen3.5-27B Q4_K +28–30%; 7900XT Qwen3.6-35B-A3B ~+10%; RX 9070 XT (mesa) Gemma-4 E4B Q6_K +3.4%.

### Correctness

`test-backend-ops` passes for `MUL_MAT`, `MUL_MAT_ID`, `GET_ROWS`, `FLASH_ATTN_EXT`, `CPY` — both with coopmat2 enabled and with `GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT2=1`. Models bit-identical ON vs OFF across `{mmap, --no-mmap}`.

### Scope

CM2 transpose left off (already benefits from larger tiles). Q4_0/Q8_0 (block 32) excluded — repacking breaks mat-vec coalescing and regresses TG; this row→col shape only suits superblock-256 K-quants.

## Requirements

All architectural design, C++/shader implementation, benchmark configuration, performance analysis and final PR content writing are done entirely by myself. I fully understand every part of this change and can answer any related technical questions in detail.
